cohort.body_name: Durham Public Schools Board of Education
cohort.label: 2016–2018 School Board
cohort.transition_reason: Swearing-in of March 15, 2016 election winners: Steve Unruhe (At-Large, succeeding retiring Leigh Bordley), Xavier Cason (Consolidated District B, succeeding outgoing Chair Heidi Carter who ran for Durham Board of County Commissioners), and unopposed incumbent Minnie Forte-Brown (Consolidated District A). Mike Lee elected Chair; Natalie Beyer elected Vice Chair. Mid-term resignation of District 2 member Sendolo Diaminah in late August 2016 amid meeting attendance scrutiny (triggering a 60-day statutory appointment window ending October 24, 2016), leaving a 6-member board while 11 applicants were vetted. Unanimous appointment and swearing-in of Bettina Umstead on October 5, 2016 to fill the unexpired District 2 term of Sendolo Diaminah, restoring the 7-member board. Mike Lee served as Chair; Natalie Beyer served as Vice Chair.

conflicts.meeting_title: Durham Public Schools Board of Education Monthly Meeting October 27, 2016 6:30PM
conflicts.issue: Sixth-Grade Eligibility for Middle School Athletics (Policy 3505)
conflicts.summary: The board voted 5-2 to revise Policy 3505 so sixth graders may try out for middle school sports excluding football beginning in January 2017, over objections from two members regarding timing and academic transition readiness.
conflicts.side_a_position: Approve 6th-grade athletic eligibility (excluding football) effective January 18, 2017.
side_a_arguments: Parents, rather than the school board, should decide whether their sixth grader is mature enough to balance tryouts and academics.

Middle school coaches, athletic directors, and Durham Council PTA parents expressed support, and participation—especially in non-cut sports like track and cross country—fosters school belonging and academic motivation.
conflicts.side_b_position: Delay or reject mid-year implementation pending broader community engagement and focus on sixth-grade academic transition.
side_b_arguments: The State Board of Education pushed discretion to local districts hastily, and current sixth graders entered middle school expecting to wait until seventh grade.
Implementing the change mid-year in January leaves insufficient time for community feedback and parent readiness guidance.
conflicts.resolution: Motion passed 5-2.

conflicts.meeting_title: Durham Public Schools BOE Operational Services Work Session 05 11 2017
conflicts.issue: Inclusion of $15/Hour Living Wage and Deferred Needs in FY 2017-18 County Budget Ask
conflicts.summary: Board members split across multiple amendment votes over whether to restrict the county funding request to a vetted ~$9.2M package (restoring school-level positions and teacher retention items) or expand it to ~$10.8M–$13.2M by adding deferred needs such as bus driver incentives, substitute pay, teacher recruitment, and a $2.3M $15/hour living wage.
conflicts.side_a_position: Limit the county ask to ~$9.2M covering the $3.48M base request, $3.155M in school-level restorations, and $2.6M in teacher retention items, while studying living wage jointly with the county next year.
side_a_arguments: DPS already agreed with Durham County to study total compensation and benefits differences (including 5-year vs. 25-year retirement vesting) before proposing living-wage alignment next cycle.
Deferred items like bus driver incentives and substitute pay had not been fully vetted or prioritized against other deferred capital needs such as $5M in annual facility upkeep.
A $9.2M ask is already ambitious (requiring local tax effort and losing 18% to charter schools) and represents a disciplined, defensible budget.
conflicts.side_b_position: Expand the county ask to include deferred employee and operational priorities—ideally all ~$4M including the $2.3M $15/hour living wage (Forte-Brown/Beyer), or at minimum bus driver incentives, substitute pay, and teacher recruitment (Beyer/Cason/Umstead on reconsideration).
side_b_arguments: Classified staff such as bus drivers and custodians face the same living costs and deserve parity with Durham City and County's $15/hour wage.
Bus driver incentives, substitute pay, and teacher recruitment directly align with board goals and the severe substitute shortage.
Durham taxpayers and progressive county commissioners cannot fund needs the board does not formally request.
conflicts.resolution: Forte-Brown's $4M all-items amendment failed 2-4; Beyer's 3-item amendment (excluding living wage) tied 3-3 before passing 4-2 on reconsideration (moved by Umstead, seconded by Unruhe), and the final ~$10.8M amended budget ask passed 4-2 without a named roll call.

conflicts.meeting_title: Durham Public Schools BOE Academic & Student Services Work Session November 03, 2016 4:30 PM
conflicts.issue: Adoption vs. Tabling of Draft BOCC–BOE Memorandum of Understanding (MOU)
conflicts.summary: Board members split 5-2 on whether to adopt a negotiated draft Memorandum of Understanding with the Durham Board of County Commissioners immediately or table it until January to revise its terms with the newly elected commission.
conflicts.side_a_position: Table the draft MOU until January to revise unbalanced provisions and negotiate with the incoming Board of County Commissioners.
side_a_arguments: The draft imposes reporting duties on DPS while lacking concrete county commitments on competitive staff pay (Point 9) and includes an undefined 'financial crisis' loophole on per-pupil funding (Point 7).
Point 11's mandate for joint planning prior to purchasing school sites and finalizing architectural specifications encroaches on statutory school board authority.
Point 1 should specify submitting a 'draft' or 'preliminary' budget in March rather than a final budget, and waiting until January allows board-to-board negotiation after county commission elections.
conflicts.side_b_position: Adopt the draft MOU immediately as an imperfect but workable living document to avoid further intergovernmental friction.
side_b_arguments: The draft is a major improvement over the county's initial draft and represents a non-contractual commitment to collaborate early in the annual budget cycle.
Delaying risks prolonging political squabbles over wording instead of focusing on the upcoming budget; the MOU can always be amended later if needed.
conflicts.resolution: Dr. Mike Lee's motion to table the MOU until January passed 5-2 by raised-hand vote (roll call not read in transcript; Bettina Umstead's vote on the hand count was not verbally stated).

conflicts.meeting_title: Durham Public Schools Board of Education Monthly Meeting April 27, 2017
conflicts.issue: Superintendent Search Structure, Openness, and Community Engagement Process
conflicts.summary: Board members held differing views on whether to conduct a broad, open national search using an outside firm and rapid public feedback vs. protecting candidate confidentiality, avoiding a disruptive system reset, and organizing multi-region community engagement.
conflicts.side_a_position: Conduct a wide search informed by rapid public input and written search-firm proposals (with Steve Unruhe and Natalie Beyer favoring broader external searches and Matt Sears exploring non-traditional talent acquisition firms).
side_a_arguments: Steve Unruhe argued it would be irresponsible to close off the search from thousands of external leaders and urged soliciting community input on May 4 without delay.
Matt Sears advocated requesting written search-firm proposals and exploring outside headhunter/evaluation models rather than limiting options to NCSBA.
Natalie Beyer urged collecting additional parent and student feedback beyond red-shirted union attendees while ensuring a thorough, deliberate search.
conflicts.side_b_position: Caution against an open, rushed search or costly firm reset, warning that top sitting superintendents require confidentiality and that genuine community engagement requires organized regional meetings.
side_b_arguments: Minnie Forte-Brown warned that top sitting leaders will not apply in a fully public search, cautioned teachers and staff against another leadership reset, noted DPS already has extensive stakeholder survey data, and called a one-hour May 4 hearing disingenuous unless regional sessions across North, South, and East Durham are properly organized.
Dr. Mike Lee favored developing a profile of Durham's needs for candidates to address rather than a rigid candidate profile, while Xavier Cason emphasized collaborative, deliberate outreach.
conflicts.resolution: No formal vote was taken; the board reached consensus to hold an initial listening session at 5:30 PM on May 4, task Minnie Forte-Brown, Bettina Umstead, and Xavier Cason with proposing a broader community hearing schedule, and solicit written proposals from search firms.

conflicts.meeting_title: Operational Services & Policy/Academic Student Services Board Work Session March 8, 2018 4:30 PM
conflicts.issue: Resolution in Support of Community Schools Initiative in Durham (pilot scope and governance)
conflicts.summary: With Chair Dr. Mike Lee watching remotely, the board voted 5-1 to adopt a resolution supporting exploration of the Community Schools model in Durham. Five members backed the resolution as a staff-initiated effort authorizing partnerships with local governments, foundations, and Duke University, whereas Minnie Forte-Brown opposed rolling out the model only in select schools rather than districtwide and questioned communication and leadership structure.
conflicts.side_a_position: Adopt the resolution authorizing administration to explore the Community Schools model and seek city, county, foundation, and Duke partnerships for schools whose staff choose to pursue it.
side_a_arguments: The resolution merely authorizes exploration and partner outreach rather than mandating a districtwide rollout.
The initiative arose from the ground up through school staff votes rather than being imposed from central office.
conflicts.side_b_position: Oppose a resolution supporting a Community Schools model limited to select schools.
side_b_arguments: Effective public school models should apply across the entire district rather than being handed only to select schools.
Communication around the resolution was uneven and its success relies heavily on individual leadership rather than a uniform district approach.
conflicts.resolution: Resolution adopted 5-1 by voice vote (Dr. Mike Lee absent/watching remotely).

conflicts.meeting_title: Durham Public Schools BOE Academic & Student Services Work Session September 01, 2016
conflicts.issue: Policy 4132.8 First-Day vs. Tenth-Day Magnet School Enrollment Deadline
conflicts.summary: The board split 5-1 on revising Policy 4132.8 to require magnet-school students to commit by the first day of school instead of allowing a 10-day window to return automatically to base schools, with Matt Sears dissenting in favor of family flexibility.
conflicts.side_a_position: Lock in magnet assignments on the first day of school so late moves require a special-assignment transfer.
side_a_arguments: More than 100 students leaving magnets during the first 10 days destabilize receiving and sending schools right as teacher allotments are adjusted at day 10.
Families receive lottery results in March and have open houses and orientation before day one, matching regional district best practices.
conflicts.side_b_position: Retain flexibility for families during the opening days of school without imposing an extra transfer hurdle.
side_b_arguments: Roughly 100 students spread across more than 20 magnet schools is a modest number.
Requiring a formal transfer after day one adds friction against school choice if a child tries a school on the first day and finds it is not a fit.
conflicts.resolution: Policy 4132.8 revision passed 5-1 with Matt Sears opposed.

conflicts.meeting_title: Durham Public Schools BOE Academic & Student Services Work Session September 01, 2016
conflicts.issue: District 2 Vacancy Criteria Ranking, Public Record Disclosure, and Interview Procedures
conflicts.summary: Board members debated how to weight school-system experience versus community leadership in the District 2 application packet, whether to hold public candidate interviews with standardized questions, and exact September deadlines.
conflicts.side_a_position: De-emphasize prior school employment in favor of public education advocacy and community leadership, disclose public-record status, and wait on deciding interview format until seeing applicant volume.
side_a_arguments: Steve Unruhe argued putting school-system experience at the top of the qualifications list discourages non-educator community leaders.

Minnie Forte-Brown opposed putting candidates through public job-style interviews and preferred seeing who applies first, while Xavier Cason proposed a September 20 deadline with Board of Elections verification on the 21st.
conflicts.side_b_position: Ensure transparent, standardized public interviews or Q&A and publish submitted application materials while meeting early October appointment targets.
side_b_arguments: Dr. Mike Lee argued any interviews in open session must ask every candidate the same core questions for fairness and favored a fast timeline ahead of the October 24 statutory cutoff.
Natalie Beyer favored brief follow-up Q&A on written packets and Letters of Support, while Matt Sears urged explicit public-record notice on applications and face-to-face meetings with applicants.
conflicts.resolution: The board reordered criteria to list commitment to public education advocacy first, added a public-record disclosure notice, set a September 20 deadline with September 22 public review, deferred interview format until reviewing applicants, and approved packet cleanup and outreach 6-0.

conflicts.meeting_title: Durham Public Schools Board of Education Monthly Meeting August 25, 2016
conflicts.issue: Piloting Off-Site School Board Work Sessions vs. Keeping Meetings Downtown
conflicts.summary: Public commenters opposed holding work sessions at outlying high schools due to public-transit burdens, while board members unanimously backed a limited two-school pilot at Hillside and Northern High Schools using existing district equipment.
conflicts.side_a_position: Test two pilot work sessions at Hillside High School (November) and Northern High School (April) without purchasing new hardware.
side_a_arguments: Holding occasional sessions at high schools engages communities, showcases schools, and provides ample parking on bus lines.
Limiting the effort to two pilots while borrowing cameras from School for Creative Studies and reusing existing Chromebooks avoids extra spending.
conflicts.side_b_position: Keep all board work sessions at the central downtown Fuller Building rather than rotating to outlying schools.
side_b_arguments: Public commenters Jackie Wagstaff and Dr. E. Lavonia Allison argued that low-income, transit-dependent residents face multiple bus transfers to reach schools outside downtown, whereas board members should visit schools individually instead.
conflicts.resolution: The board voted 6-0 to plan two pilot remote work sessions at Hillside High and Northern High.

conflicts.meeting_title: Durham Public Schools BOE Operational Services & Policy Work Session January 11, 2018 4:30 PM
conflicts.issue: Use of EVAAS Growth Data and Local Due Process Policy in 2018-2019 Multi-Year Teacher Contracts
conflicts.summary: Board members disagreed over relying on SAS EVAAS student-growth metrics to determine teacher eligibility for four-year contracts under new state rules, and over whether the proposal accounted for DPS's 2015 local due-process/career-status policy before taking action.
conflicts.side_a_position: Multi-year teacher contract eligibility should rely on clear performance data, including EVAAS and evaluation ratings, to hold educators accountable for student progress.
side_a_arguments: Minnie Forte-Brown argued the board should not shy away from evaluation and that 'the data must be the driver' in holding adults accountable because students only get one year in a grade.
HR staff noted that principals had reviewed the criteria in December and recommended straightforward data benchmarks using NCEES standards and EVAAS growth.
conflicts.side_b_position: EVAAS student-growth scores are an unreliable single-year metric for contract length, and action should be deferred to verify DPS's 2015 due-process policy and consult DAE.
side_b_arguments: Xavier Cason questioned elevating SAS EVAAS growth figures designed for cohorts rather than individual teachers, noting national research favors at least three-year trends and districts like Houston abandoned EVAAS.

Natalie Beyer and Steve Unruhe expressed strong misgivings about relying on flawed EVAAS data, with Steve Unruhe requesting a fall review if implemented and Matt Sears pointing to missing 2015 due-process policy language and urging consultation with DAE before voting.
conflicts.resolution: No formal vote was taken; by consensus following Matt Sears's request, the board tabled the item to its next meeting so staff could locate the 2015 due-process policy (found later in the meeting as April/August 2015 revisions to Policy 5430) and meet with DAE leadership.

conflicts.meeting_title: Durham Public Schools BOE Operational Services & Policy Work Session October 12, 2017 4:30 PM
conflicts.issue: Immediate Approval vs. Pre-Approval Vetting of Budget Process Advisory Committee Nominees
conflicts.summary: The board split 3-2 on whether to immediately approve the updated membership list for the renamed Budget Process Advisory Committee (formerly Zero-Based Budgeting Committee) or pause approval of two new nominees until the Chair and Vice Chair spoke with them.
conflicts.side_a_position: Approve the administration's updated committee membership list immediately so the committee can continue its work without delay, and conduct Chair/Vice Chair outreach afterward.
side_a_arguments: The two new members had already attended the first committee meeting and understand its function.
The next budget committee meeting was scheduled for October 24, and the board could always amend the membership list later if needed.
conflicts.side_b_position: Hold off on approving the updated membership list until Chair Dr. Mike Lee and Vice Chair Natalie Beyer speak with the two newly highlighted nominees.
side_b_arguments: The board previously used a formal appointment process and should verify that new members understand the heavy homework and commitment required before formal approval.
conflicts.resolution: Motion to approve the updated Budget Process Advisory Committee list passed 3-2 without a named roll call; Natalie Beyer opposed immediate approval prior to vetting, while the three Aye voters and second Nay voter were not identified by name.

conflicts.meeting_title: Durham Public Schools BOE Special Session 04 19 2017
conflicts.issue: Confidential vs. Open Superintendent Search and Role of External Search Firms
conflicts.summary: Board members expressed differing preferences on whether the superintendent search should be open or confidential, how heavily to weigh internal succession versus national recruitment, and whether to hire a search firm.
conflicts.side_a_position: Conduct an external/broader search—either open to internal and external applicants (Steve Unruhe) or confidential and proactive through talent-acquisition firms (Natalie Beyer, Matt Sears).
side_a_arguments: Steve Unruhe favored an open search allowing both strong internal candidates and external candidates to compete.
Natalie Beyer argued that the highest-caliber sitting superintendents will not risk applying in a public/open search, favoring a confidential process.
Matt Sears urged looking beyond traditional education search firms to proactive talent-acquisition processes.
conflicts.side_b_position: Prioritize continuity, existing community survey data, and evaluating internal succession without rushing into an expensive search-firm reset.
side_b_arguments: Minnie Forte-Brown argued DPS already has ample stakeholder survey data, warned that parents and staff do not want another system reset, and urged assessing whether current internal leadership can meet community standards before spending heavily on a search.
Dr. Mike Lee favored first building a profile of Durham Public Schools through community meetings before narrowing candidate criteria.
conflicts.resolution: No formal vote was taken; the board agreed to reconvene at the April 27 full board meeting to vote on a search direction, firm/process, and timeline.

conflicts.meeting_title: Durham Public Schools BOE Academic & Student Services Work Session  October 6, 2016 4:30 PM
conflicts.issue: Advancing 6th-Grade Middle School Athletic Eligibility Proposal to October Action Agenda
conflicts.summary: Board members disagreed over whether to advance the sixth-grade athletic eligibility proposal for action at the October full board meeting, resulting in a split voice vote without an announced numerical tally.
conflicts.side_a_position: Advance the sixth-grade athletic eligibility policy revision to the October full board meeting for action.
side_a_arguments: Parents, not the school board, are best positioned to decide whether a sixth grader is ready for competitive tryouts, and participation can strengthen school engagement and academic motivation.
Middle school principals and athletic directors recommended the change and surrounding districts had already acted.
conflicts.side_b_position: Oppose rushing the proposal to immediate action without further study of academic transitions and equity across schools.
side_b_arguments: Sixth grade is a major developmental and academic transition, and the state policy shift came hastily after the school year had already begun.
More time is needed to review academic eligibility standards, examine disparities in which middle schools offer which sports, and gather family input.
conflicts.resolution: Voice vote passed to place the item on the October full board action agenda despite audible opposition; exact numerical tally was not read aloud.

conflicts.meeting_title: Durham Public Schools Board of Education Monthly Meeting April 26, 2018 6:30 PM
conflicts.issue: Scope and contingencies of board directive for a May 16 school operations plan
conflicts.summary: Following public comment from 22 speakers on the May 16 teacher rally and reports of 791 teacher absence requests, board members split 5-2 on a motion directing administration to return with a contingency plan for May 16. Debate centered on whether board contingencies regarding principals' approval of personal days would complicate administrative planning and whether the board should wait for administration's data before signaling closure.
conflicts.side_a_position: Direct administration to bring back a formal May 16 contingency plan for board consideration at a special meeting.
side_a_arguments: 791 teacher absences already exceed the district substitute pool and preclude normal instruction.
Directing a contingency plan sets clear direction and gives staff and community time to coordinate testing, meals, and childcare.
conflicts.side_b_position: Oppose the motion directing a formal contingency plan with added board conditions.
side_b_arguments: Adding board contingencies around principal leave approvals makes developing an operational plan more problematic for administration.
Further study with administration is needed before locking in directives.
conflicts.resolution: Motion passed 5-2 by voice vote (individual Aye and Nay voters were not named on the record), leading to the May 2 special called meeting.

conflicts.meeting_title: Durham Public Schools Board of Education Organizational Meeting July 18, 2017 4:30 PM
conflicts.issue: Contested Election for Board Vice Chair (Natalie Beyer vs. Steve Unruhe)
conflicts.summary: Following Dr. Mike Lee's unanimous 7-0 re-election as Chair, two members—Natalie Beyer and Steve Unruhe—were nominated for Board Vice Chair, resulting in a 2-5 defeat for Beyer and a 6-0-1 election of Unruhe.
conflicts.side_a_position: Support Steve Unruhe for Board Vice Chair (winning 6-0-1 on the second ballot after opposing Natalie Beyer's nomination 5-2).
side_a_arguments: Secured a majority of board members present under Policy 2200 after the first nominee did not obtain a majority.
conflicts.side_b_position: Support Natalie Beyer for Board Vice Chair (receiving 2 Ayes to 5 Nays on the first ballot; one unnamed member abstained on Unruhe's vote).
side_b_arguments: Nominated first for Vice Chair under Policy 2200.
conflicts.resolution: Natalie Beyer's nomination failed 2-5 on a voice vote, and Steve Unruhe was elected Vice Chair 6-0-1 with zero opposed and one abstention (no roll call was read in the transcript to identify individual voters).

conflicts.summary: Minnie Forte-Brown moved and Natalie Beyer seconded amending Steve Unruhe's $9.2M budget motion to add ~$4 million covering all four deferred needs, including the $2.3M $15/hour living wage.

conflicts.side_b_position: Voted Nay / Opposed

conflicts.meeting_title: Durham Public Schools BOE Academic & Student Services Work Session April 3, 2017 4:30 PM
conflicts.issue: Policy 4321 Warrant Review Scope (ICE Only vs. All Law Enforcement) and Interpretation Mandates
conflicts.summary: Board members, staff, and legal counsel debated whether revisions to Policy 4321 should require all law enforcement warrants (not solely ICE requests) to be cleared through the superintendent's office, whether to mandate ('shall') law enforcement interpretation services, and how to balance student protections with school safety.
conflicts.side_a_position: Broaden Policy 4321 Point 7 to require superintendent review and tracking of all law enforcement warrants on school grounds and strengthen interpretation language from 'should' to 'shall'.
side_a_arguments: Dr. Mike Lee urged sending all warrants to the superintendent's office for verification and tracking, and asked to convene a joint summit with the Sheriff, Police Chief, City Council, and County Commissioners.
Natalie Beyer argued for taking immediate action on Point 6 (student data privacy), Point 7 (warrant tracking/review), and changing 'should provide' interpretation to 'shall provide/allow'.
Xavier Cason and Minnie Forte-Brown questioned why DPS could not stand more firmly for students and noted public testimony showed arrests were still occurring in view of peers rather than privately.
conflicts.side_b_position: Consult local law enforcement first and maintain legal/safety boundaries before adopting an across-the-board superintendent warrant-clearance gate or binding law enforcement agencies via school policy.
side_b_arguments: Board attorney Ken Soo warned that instructing principals or staff to hold or judge criminal arrest warrants crosses legal lines, creates liability for school employees, and could conflict with officers responding to campus safety threats.

Superintendent Dr. Bert Lumm and Soo cautioned that DPS policy cannot legally compel outside law enforcement agencies to provide interpreters, and warned against putting uncertified DPS staff between officers and students.
Staff noted April 3 was a first reading and that face-to-face training for 4,500 employees could not happen overnight.
conflicts.resolution: Because it was a first reading, no vote was taken; the board directed administration to meet with local law enforcement leadership and return with modified Policy 4321 language (including strengthened arrest-privacy enforcement and SRO training) for second reading.

conflicts.meeting_title: Durham Public Schools BOE Operational Services and Policy Work Session 03 09 2017
conflicts.issue: Framing and Size of March 15 FY 2017-18 Funding Request to Durham County
conflicts.summary: Board members disagreed on whether the preliminary March 15 MOU submission to Durham County Commissioners should be limited to the conservative $4.4 million baseline ask or formally include the $6 million K-3 class-size exposure and $2.3 million $15/hour living-wage request.
conflicts.side_a_position: Submit only the conservative $4.4 million baseline request (with an asterisk noting K-3 and living-wage uncertainties) to maintain trust with County Commissioners and avoid an alarming $13.4 million headline.
side_a_arguments: Submitting $4.4 million respects the collaborative budget MOU process with the county and avoids putting commissioners on the defensive before state numbers are finalized.

DPS had already invested heavily to reach an earlier living-wage benchmark and should compare total compensation and retirement vesting (5 years vs. 25 years) with the county before proposing $15/hour parity.
conflicts.side_b_position: Formally include the $6 million K-3 class-size mandate, $2.3 million $15/hour wage parity, and full $1.5 million Whitted School pre-K request alongside the base ask in clearly separated requests.
side_b_arguments: Omitting the $6 million K-3 risk and $2.3 million living wage would effectively end public advocacy with commissioners on urgent threats to 100 arts, music, and PE positions and staff pay equity.
Separating Whitted School's $1.5 million pre-K funding from the general appropriation is necessary to prevent 18% from flowing to K-12 charter schools.
conflicts.resolution: Steve Unruhe withdrew his unseconded $4.4M-only motion and Bettina Umstead withdrew her three-part amendment; the four remaining board members unanimously approved a two-part, four-line-item request combining $5.15M ($3.65M base + $1.5M Whitted) and $8.3M ($6M K-3 + $2.3M $15/hour wages).

conflicts.meeting_title: Durham Public Schools BOE Operational and Policy Work Session September 08, 2016
conflicts.issue: Necessity of Adopting Policy 2302 on Remote Participation in Board Meetings
conflicts.summary: Following intense public opposition to draft Policy 2302, board members present concluded that existing Policy 2300 already adequately permitted remote participation under exceptional circumstances and declined to advance the optional policy, contrasting with Chair Dr. Mike Lee's absent position favoring formal guidelines.
conflicts.side_a_position: Existing Policy 2300 suffices for exceptional circumstances and no separate Policy 2302 should be adopted.
side_a_arguments: Policy 2300 already requires in-person attendance while permitting telephone or electronic participation under exceptional circumstances.
Adopting a detailed standalone remote-participation policy is unnecessary and sends the wrong signal to the community.
conflicts.side_b_position: Formal written guidelines in Policy 2302 could clarify permissible circumstances such as work travel or medical recovery.
side_b_arguments: Written parameters were previously raised by Chair Dr. Mike Lee (noted by public speakers from newspaper reporting and August 11 discussion) to formalize when members with outside obligations could call in.
conflicts.resolution: No motion was made on Policy 2302; the board concluded no action was needed and moved on to the next agenda item.

conflicts.meeting_title: Durham Public Schools BOE Operational Services and Policy Work Session August 11, 2016
conflicts.issue: Policy 2302 on Remote Participation in Board Meetings
conflicts.summary: Board members disagreed over whether to adopt formal remote-participation rules in Policy 2302 after public commenters attacked the proposal as excusing Sendolo Diaminah's absences.
conflicts.side_a_position: Avoid adopting Policy 2302 or keep remote participation strictly ad hoc/case-by-case.
side_a_arguments: Steve Unruhe warned that adopting a formal policy gives the public the impression the board encourages remote attendance.
Xavier Cason preferred leaving the seven-member board's long-standing case-by-case practice untouched unless legally required to change.
Natalie Beyer emphasized the importance of in-person attendance and urged waiting for Minnie Forte-Brown and Sendolo Diaminah before any decision.
conflicts.side_b_position: Establish clear written policy parameters allowing remote call-in for work travel or medical recovery.
side_b_arguments: Dr. Mike Lee argued that clear written guidelines provide fair flexibility for working board members who travel or face medical recovery without replacing ad hoc rules with guesswork.
Matt Sears noted the board had previously failed to explain members' out-of-town call-in reasons clearly to constituents while expressing openness to keeping an informal trust-based approach.
conflicts.resolution: Postponed without a formal vote to a future work session so absent members Minnie Forte-Brown and Sendolo Diaminah could participate.

conflicts.meeting_title: Board of Education Retreat  -   Staff Development Center   M-1  8:00 AM   -  1:00 PM
conflicts.issue: Standardized Intervention Language in Strategic Plan Strategy 4 and Board Feedback Process
conflicts.summary: During the Strategic Plan draft review, board members debated whether Strategy 4's 'standardized intervention strategies' risked a rigid 'cookie cutter' approach and how individual board members' policy concerns should be discussed versus relayed directly to administration.
conflicts.side_a_position: Warned against standardized 'cookie cutter' interventions and asserted every board member's equal right to air serious concerns publicly
side_a_arguments: Avoid governing DPS with a 'cookie cutter' approach that treats every school identically
Past districtwide curriculum standardization like Reading Street failed when imposed rigidly
Every one of the seven board members stands on equal footing and must have a platform to voice serious concerns about goals or metrics
conflicts.side_b_position: Supported a standardized baseline framework of effective interventions and preferred funneling member edits to staff without back-and-forth floor debate
side_b_arguments: Standardization ensures every school provides intervention strategies rather than having uneven pockets of quality
Allowing comments to stand without back-and-forth debate lets administration synthesize edits and follow up individually
conflicts.resolution: Administration recorded board feedback (including disaggregation and EC/ESL graduation barriers) for finalization ahead of the June 28 adoption vote.

conflicts.meeting_title: Durham Public Schools BOE Operational Services and Policy Work Session January 12, 2017 4:30 PM
conflicts.issue: Timing of Community Engagement Meetings for FY 2017-2018 Budget Cuts
conflicts.summary: Board members disagreed over whether to launch north-south-central community listening meetings immediately to explain the looming $8.2M-$12M budget shortfall or wait until staff identifies concrete reduction options.
conflicts.side_a_position: Hold north-south-central board-led community listening meetings early in the budget cycle rather than leaving principals to explain cuts alone.
side_a_arguments: Xavier Cason warned that lack of community engagement at the board level threatens district visioning and places 53 school principals on the defensive explaining complex district-level budget formulas they do not control.
Minnie Forte-Brown added that educating the community early about charter school budget impacts and potential state legislation helps build public allies.
conflicts.side_b_position: Defer community budget meetings until staff identifies realistic reduction options from the $8.2 million gap so the board presents concrete proposals.
side_b_arguments: Natalie Beyer noted the district had spent down its fund balance leaving no reserve cushion and argued that going out to the community before identifying realistic $8.2 million in cuts 'just says yikes' without moving the process forward or helping relations with County Commissioners.
conflicts.resolution: No formal vote; by informal consensus at 02:12:06, Xavier Cason agreed to wait to schedule the community meetings until the board and staff identify concrete reduction options.

conflicts.meeting_title: Durham Public Schools Board of Education Monthly Meeting September 22, 2016
conflicts.issue: Allowing Live Public Comment in Support of District 2 Vacancy Candidates
conflicts.summary: During planning for the District 2 candidate forum, Chair Dr. Mike Lee proposed allowing public speakers to testify in support of applicants, while Minnie Forte-Brown and Natalie Beyer opposed live support testimony as biased, time-consuming, and unnecessary given written letters of support.
conflicts.side_a_position: Allow live public comment in support of individual District 2 applicants during the candidate forum.
side_a_arguments: Community involvement and direct public input on the applicants are worth a longer meeting.
conflicts.side_b_position: Limit the candidate forum to applicant presentations and rely on written letters of support and normal community outreach.
side_b_arguments: Live cheering or support testimony introduces bias favoring candidates with larger organized followings.
Applicants already submitted two letters of support each, and public testimony for 13 candidates would make the meeting run all night.
Community members can already email or contact board members directly.
conflicts.resolution: The board proceeded without live public-support testimony during the candidate forum, scheduling candidate-only presentations on September 27 (backup October 3) and a selection vote on October 5.

conflicts.meeting_title: Durham Public Schools BOE Operational Services and Policy Work Session October 13, 2016 4:30 PM
conflicts.issue: State-Mandated Concealed-Carry Vehicle Provision in Weapons on Campus Policy 5027/7275
conflicts.summary: The board voted 5-1 to advance updated Policy 5027/7275 (Weapons on Campus) to the October consent agenda, with one member dissenting in objection to the North Carolina law requiring schools to permit concealed-carry handguns locked inside vehicles on campus.
conflicts.side_a_position: Advance updated Policy 5027/7275 to consent because state law requires boards to include the locked-vehicle concealed-carry exception.
side_a_arguments: State law mandates that local boards adopt a policy accommodating valid concealed handgun permits for weapons stored inside locked vehicles, leaving the board no authority to do otherwise.
Deleting mace/pepper spray language and revising visitor-escort wording to rely on SROs and law enforcement improves safety and enforceability.
conflicts.side_b_position: Vote against advancing the policy to register objection to concealed-carry weapons on school grounds.
side_b_arguments: Explicitly opposed allowing concealed-carry handguns on campus under any circumstances, even if required by state statute.
conflicts.resolution: Motion to refer Policy 5027/7275 to the October consent agenda passed 5-1; the dissenting speaker was not named in the transcript.

conflicts.meeting_title: Durham Public Schools Board of Education Special Called Meeting May 2, 2018 5:30 PM
conflicts.issue: Closing DPS schools to students on May 16, 2018 as an optional teacher workday (Option 2)
conflicts.summary: The board voted 6-1 by show of hands to adopt Administration Option 2 closing schools to students and designating May 16, 2018 as an optional teacher workday amid 1,028 teacher personal-day requests for the Raleigh education rally. Six members supported closure to ensure safety and stand with educators, while one unidentified member opposed the motion after discussion noted impacts on AP/IB testing, student meals, and classified staff wages.
conflicts.side_a_position: Close schools to students on May 16, 2018 and designate the day as an optional teacher workday so educators can rally without losing personal leave.
side_a_arguments: 1,028 teacher personal-day requests make normal safe school operations and instruction impossible.
Supporting teachers' advocacy in Raleigh for state funding and pay benefits students and public education long term.
Making May 16 an optional teacher workday prevents teachers from losing personal leave or pay.
conflicts.side_b_position: Oppose closing schools to students on May 16, 2018.
side_b_arguments: Closing schools disrupts student instruction, AP/IB and early-calendar exams, and school-based meals.
A closure creates an estimated $50,000 pay loss for transportation workers and $100,000 revenue loss for child nutrition.
conflicts.resolution: Motion to adopt Option 2 passed 6-1 by show of hands (individual Aye and Nay voters were not read aloud on the record).

conflicts.meeting_title: Durham Public Schools Board of Education Monthly Meeting May 23, 2018 6:30 PM
conflicts.issue: Procedural 6-1 Split Vote on Entering Closed Session
conflicts.summary: The procedural motion to enter closed session at the May 23, 2018 monthly meeting passed on a 6-1 voice vote after one board member voiced opposition when asked for nays, though no floor debate or individual member names were recorded.
conflicts.side_a_position: Supported entering closed session for the reasons stated on the agenda (6 unnamed members)
side_a_arguments: Proceed with closed session items as listed on the meeting agenda
conflicts.side_b_position: Opposed entering closed session (1 unnamed member)
side_b_arguments: No floor rationale stated on the audio record
conflicts.resolution: Motion passed 6-1 by voice vote and the board entered closed session.

conflicts.meeting_title: Operational Services & Policy/Academic Student Services Board Work Session May 10, 2018 4:30 PM
conflicts.issue: Immediate approval of Item 7C Technology Purchases vs. deferring for full plan details on May 24
conflicts.summary: During consideration of Item 7C (Technology Purchases, pulled from the consent agenda), one board member objected to voting immediately because they understood consensus was to bring full context and details back at the May 24 board meeting. The majority approved the purchases immediately on a 6-1 voice vote while retaining the expectation of receiving the full context later.
conflicts.side_a_position: Approve the technology purchases immediately while requesting full implementation context at the May 24 meeting.
side_a_arguments: Approval can proceed now while staff still provides the broader technology plan context at May 24.
conflicts.side_b_position: Hold approval until full plan details and context are presented at the May 24 meeting.
side_b_arguments: Board consensus had been for the item to return with fuller detail and a plan on May 24 prior to approval.
conflicts.resolution: Passed 6-1 by voice vote (individual Aye and Nay names were not read into the record).

conflicts.meeting_title: Durham Public Schools Board of Education Monthly Meeting March 22, 2018 6:30 PM
conflicts.issue: Motion to enter closed session
conflicts.summary: A procedural motion to enter closed session for the reasons stated on the agenda passed 4-1 by voice vote among five present voting members; no debate preceded the vote and individual member positions were not read into the record.
conflicts.side_a_position: Enter closed session for the reasons stated on the agenda.
side_a_arguments: Proceed with closed session as scheduled on the meeting agenda.
conflicts.side_b_position: Oppose entering closed session.
side_b_arguments: Single Nay recorded on the voice vote without stated floor remarks.
conflicts.resolution: Passed 4-1 by voice vote (individual voter names were not read into the record).

conflicts.meeting_title: Durham Public Schools BOE Operational Services Work Session 06 15 2017   4:30
conflicts.issue: Whether to Hold July 2017 Work Sessions for Redistricting, Budget, and Custodial Work
conflicts.summary: Board members debated scheduling one or two Wednesday work sessions in July to advance redistricting, custodial, and budget items versus preserving the traditional July hiatus for district staff.
conflicts.side_a_position: Hold one or two Wednesday work sessions in July so administration can present initial work chunks (such as redistricting priorities) rather than pausing until August.
side_a_arguments: A backlog of major items—redistricting, budget, and custodial matters—remained on the board's plate after canceling public hearings.
Meeting on Wednesday would avoid holding staff late at the end of their four-day summer workweek.
conflicts.side_b_position: Oppose July work sessions to give 11-month district staff a break and limit July activity to the required annual organizational meeting (plus urgent personnel closed session if needed).
side_b_arguments: Staff work 11 months a year and 12–15 hour days on summer 4-day schedules, making July their only reset window before year-round schools open July 17.
Board members had summer travel conflicts in July, making full work sessions difficult.
conflicts.resolution: Resolved by unanimous compromise: the board scheduled only its annual organizational meeting for Tuesday, July 18, 2017 at 4:30 PM (accommodating Bettina Umstead's July 19–21 absence) without adding July work sessions.

conflicts.meeting_title: Durham Public Schools BOE Operational Services Work Session 05 11 2017

conflicts.summary: On reconsideration, Natalie Beyer's amendment to add $200,000 for bus driver incentives, $1.0 million for substitute teacher pay, and $500,000 for teacher recruitment passed 4-2.
conflicts.side_a_position: Voted Aye (Passed 4-2)
conflicts.side_b_position: Voted Nay / Opposed
conflicts.resolution: Passed (4-2)

conflicts.meeting_title: Durham Public Schools Board of Education Monthly Meeting October 27, 2016 6:30PM
conflicts.issue: Contract Extensions for 10 Senior Staff Members
conflicts.summary: Following closed session, the board approved contract extensions for ten senior staff members by a 4-2 voice vote.
conflicts.side_a_position: Approve the ten senior staff contract extensions recommended after closed session.
side_a_arguments: Supported by four of the six remaining board members following closed-session personnel review.
conflicts.side_b_position: Oppose the contract extensions (two Nay votes cast).

conflicts.resolution: Passed 4-2 by voice vote without a named roll call identifying the four Ayes or two Nays (among Dr. Mike Lee, Natalie Beyer, Bettina Umstead, Matt Sears, Xavier Cason, and Steve Unruhe, with Minnie Forte-Brown having departed earlier).

meetings.title: Durham Public Schools Board of Education Monthly Meeting June 28, 2018 6:30 PM
meetings.executive_summary: At its June 28, 2018 monthly meeting—conducted 5-0 with Matt Sears (work travel) and Steve Unruhe (family) excused—the Durham Public Schools Board of Education honored its May Student of the Month from Northern High, Riverside High athletics coach Chambers, and CFO Paul LeSieur for financial reporting transparency, and heard Superintendent Dr. Pascal Mubenga report $52.6 million in graduating class scholarship offers. The board unanimously approved its agenda, amended June 22 retreat minutes (adding Xavier Cason to attendance) alongside May 23 minutes, and second-reading consent policies 4301 (Code of Student Conduct) and 4403 (Head Lice). Following Dr. Debbie Pittman's presentation, the board waived first reading to adopt Policy 2500 reducing student transfer hearing panels from three to two or more members, and approved continuing the Envision contract for visually impaired instructional services. In the centerpiece action of the evening, the board unanimously adopted the five-year DPS Strategic Plan along with its spending priorities—including raising local teacher supplements toward nearly $22 million in total investment and $500,000 for classified staff—and heard community schools updates noting $120,000 in county funding for coordinators at E.K. Powe and Southwest Elementary alongside DPS pilots at Lakewood and Club Boulevard before approving the June 28 personnel report after closed session.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Celebrations, and Superintendent's Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Dr. Mike Lee called the meeting to order, led a moment of silence ahead of the Strategic Plan vote, and joined Chip for celebrations recognizing Northern High Student of the Month Leonzo, Riverside High coach Chambers (Chambers Court and NCHSAA/NCADA honors), and CFO Paul LeSieur for transparent financial reporting. Dr. Mubenga reviewed his first seven months of leadership reorganization and reported $52.6 million in estimated scholarship offers alongside post-graduation military and credential goals.

agenda_items.title: Public Comment Check, Agenda Approval, Minutes, and Consent Policies (4301 and 4403)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Confirming no general public commenters, Chair Lee noted excused absences for Matt Sears and Steve Unruhe while maintaining a five-member quorum. The board passed the agenda 5-0, approved May 23 minutes and June 22 retreat minutes amended to add Xavier Cason to attendance 5-0, and adopted second-reading consent Policies 4301 (Code of Student Conduct) and 4403 (Head Lice) 5-0.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Agenda, Minutes, and Consent items each passed 5-0 (Voice)

agenda_items.title: Policy 2500 (Hearings Before the Board) and Visually Impaired Services Contract
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Dr. Debbie Pittman presented Policy 2500 reducing student transfer appeal hearing panels from three or more to two or more board members (the state minimum, while retaining full-board votes in closed session) to speed scheduling, and the board waived first reading and adopted the policy 5-0. Executive Director of Exceptional Children Dr. Kristin Bell then presented continuation of the Envision contract for up to 2.5 licensed teachers for visually impaired students, which passed 5-0.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Policy 2500 and Envision contract each passed 5-0 (Voice)

agenda_items.title: Five-Year Strategic Plan and Spending Priorities Adoption
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Board members and staff discussed the five-year Strategic Plan and its fund-balance/recurring spending commitments, highlighting local teacher supplement increases (bringing local supplement investment to nearly $22 million) and $500,000 for classified staff, as well as forthcoming press releases and salary schedules for employees. The board voted 5-0 to adopt the Strategic Plan including its spending priorities.

agenda_items.title: Community Schools Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: During item public comment, Nicholas Graber-Grace of the Community Alliance for Public Education (Southern Vision Alliance) reported the Durham County Budget Office approved $120,000 for community school coordinators at E.K. Powe and Southwest Elementary Schools. Staff added that DPS's own pilot sites are Lakewood Elementary and Club Boulevard Humanities Magnet School and that an MOU with CAPE is in development.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session and June 28, 2018 Personnel Report
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board voted 5-0 to enter closed session and returned to open session at 01:38:23. Members approved the June 28, 2018 personnel report 5-0 and adjourned.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Closed session and Personnel report each passed 5-0 (Voice)

votes.item_title: Approval of June 28, 2018 Monthly Meeting Agenda
votes.notes: Matt Sears and Steve Unruhe were excused/absent.
votes.discussion_detail: Board members moved and seconded approval of the June 28, 2018 agenda as presented. Passed 5-0 by voice vote; Chair Lee announced Matt Sears and Steve Unruhe had excused absences.

votes.item_title: Approval of May 23, 2018 Meeting Minutes and Amended June 22, 2018 Retreat Minutes
votes.notes: Matt Sears and Steve Unruhe were excused/absent.
votes.discussion_detail: A board member pointed out that Xavier Cason had been omitted from the June 22 retreat attendance list and moved approval of the May 23 minutes and the amended June 22 retreat minutes. Passed 5-0 by voice vote.

votes.item_title: Approval of Consent Items: Policy 4301 (Code of Student Conduct) and Policy 4403 (Head Lice) Second Reading
votes.notes: Matt Sears and Steve Unruhe were excused/absent.
votes.discussion_detail: Board members moved and seconded approval of second-reading consent items Policy 4301 (Code of Student Conduct) and Policy 4403 (Head Lice). Passed 5-0 by voice vote.

votes.item_title: Waiver of First Reading and Adoption of Policy 2500 (Hearings Before the Board)
votes.notes: Matt Sears and Steve Unruhe were excused/absent.
votes.discussion_detail: Following Dr. Debbie Pittman's presentation on reducing transfer hearing panel sizes from three or more to two or more board members, the board moved to waive first reading and adopt Policy 2500 immediately. Passed 5-0 by voice vote.

votes.item_title: Approval of Envision Contract Continuation for Visually Impaired Instructional Services
votes.notes: Matt Sears and Steve Unruhe were excused/absent.
votes.discussion_detail: Following Dr. Kristin Bell's presentation, the board moved and seconded continuing the Envision contract for up to 2.5 licensed teachers for visually impaired students. Passed 5-0 by voice vote.

votes.item_title: Adoption of Five-Year Strategic Plan and Listed Spending Priorities
votes.notes: Matt Sears and Steve Unruhe were excused/absent.
votes.discussion_detail: Board members moved and seconded adopting the DPS five-year Strategic Plan including the spending priorities listed within it (including teacher supplement raises and $500,000 for classified staff). Passed 5-0 by voice vote.

votes.item_title: Motion to Enter Closed Session
votes.notes: Matt Sears and Steve Unruhe were excused/absent.
votes.discussion_detail: A board member moved and another seconded entering closed session for the reasons stated on the agenda. Passed 5-0 by voice vote.

votes.item_title: Approval of June 28, 2018 Personnel Report
votes.notes: Matt Sears and Steve Unruhe were excused/absent.
votes.discussion_detail: Reconvening in open session, the board moved, seconded, and approved the June 28, 2018 personnel report 5-0 by voice vote.

boe_dae_events.event_title: Five-Year Strategic Plan and FY 2018-19 Spending Priorities (Teacher Supplements & Classified Study Phase-In)
boe_dae_events.dae_position: Educators and classified staff sought concrete multi-year budget commitments raising local teacher salary supplements to stay competitive with neighboring districts and initiating pay adjustments from the classified salary study.

member_positions.stance_summary: Highlighted the approved spending package's ~22 million local investment in certified teacher salary supplements (raising beginning supplements from $4,375 to $4,900 and average supplements toward $7,200) to compete with neighboring counties and retain teachers inside Durham rather than losing them down I-40. Presided over the unanimous 5-0 vote (Sears and Unruhe absent).
member_positions.key_quote: We are very serious about retaining and keeping our teachers here, keeping our teachers happy.

member_positions.stance_summary: Highlighted adding three bilingual interpreter positions and expanding CTE credentials in the Strategic Plan and formally moved final adoption of the plan and $5.4 million spending priorities (including $500,000 for classified salary study phase-in, restorative-practice coordinators, and custodial transition support).
member_positions.key_quote: If there's no more discussion, I move that we approve the strategic plan for Durham Public Schools.

member_positions.stance_summary: Welcomed the inclusive strategic planning process and seconded Umstead's motion approving the plan and spending priorities, including educator supplements and initial classified study funding.
member_positions.key_quote: I'm excited about the plan and thank everyone who put in that time.

member_positions.stance_summary: Walked through the $5.4 million spending package publicly—emphasizing recurring investments in restorative-practice center coordinators (replacing punitive ISS), Spanish interpreters, the $500,000 initial classified salary-study phase-in, teacher supplements, and custodial in-house implementation—so the public could see how fund balance jump-started labor and equity priorities.
member_positions.key_quote: So by approving this tonight, you're approving the 5.4 million of which 3.4 is recurring, and your commitment to use your fund balance and your lapsed salary is what's jump-starting this strategic plan.

member_positions.stance_summary: Praised the recurring budget commitments inside the five-year Strategic Plan as 'putting your money where your plan is' so compensation and school-support positions endure beyond the five-year horizon.
member_positions.key_quote: Look at the spending options; it's about putting your money where your plan is, and there are several recurring items that will impact students for many years past that five years.

boe_dae_events.event_title: Community Schools Pilot Update and DPS-DAE/CAPE Memorandum of Understanding
boe_dae_events.issue_category: DAE Advocacy / Recognition / Day of Action
boe_dae_events.dae_position: CAPE/Southern Vision Alliance and DAE lobbied Durham County for $120,000 to fund two additional Community Schools coordinators (at E.K. Powe and Southwest Elementary) alongside DPS's two pilots (Club Boulevard and Lakewood), and urged finalizing a tri-party MOU giving coordinators consistent training and student-data access.

member_positions.stance_summary: Asked administration to clarify which schools received county-backed coordinator grants alongside the two board-approved sites and reiterated her message to parents that every DPS school belongs to its community regardless of pilot designation. Affirmed that teachers across non-designated schools are equally 'energized and brilliant' without needing a separate label.
member_positions.key_quote: Because every school is a community school, all the schools belong to the community, so the energizing of teachers in community schools should be the same energizing of teachers that are in schools that have not been designated as such.

member_positions.stance_summary: Celebrated the extraordinary teacher enthusiasm DAE's Community Schools campaign generated—calling it unmatched in helping empower and retain educators—and welcomed county commissioners doubling the pilot footprint. Urged attorney Ken Soo's tri-party MOU with CAPE and DAE to guarantee county-funded coordinators equal student-data access alongside in-house DPS coordinators.
member_positions.key_quote: I have not seen teachers excited about anything as I've seen them about community schools, and I'm excited about its potential for energizing our teachers and helping as a part of actually empowering and retaining teachers in Durham.

member_positions.stance_summary: Urged DPS to rely heavily on school principals as operational details in the MOU are finalized and welcomed the collaboration across DPS, DAE, and community partners as an example of Durham leading statewide.
member_positions.key_quote: As the MOU is coming together, I hope we can really rely on our principals to let us know what they're looking for, and let's do it and let's do it well and let's do it together.

member_positions.stance_summary: Acknowledged operational coordination across DPS-funded and county/CAPE-funded sites would be tricky at first, but expressed confidence the Community Schools coordinators would help schools directly implement the Strategic Plan's community-partnership goals.
member_positions.key_quote: I think that I'm excited about this; the operational stuff seems tricky, but I think we'll figure out how to make sure it works well.

meetings.title: Board of Education Retreat  -   Staff Development Center   M-1  8:00 AM   -  1:00 PM
meetings.executive_summary: With all seven members present at its June 22, 2018 Board Retreat, the Durham Public Schools Board of Education unanimously approved its agenda and conducted a comprehensive review of the draft five-year Strategic Plan crafted by the 52-member Strategic Planning Committee. Board members debated the draft motto/logo, priority ordering, goal metrics, and Strategy 4's standardized intervention language—with Minnie Forte-Brown and Natalie Beyer warning against a rigid 'cookie cutter' model akin to Reading Street and asserting every member's equal right to voice concerns, while Chair Dr. Mike Lee urged funneling edits to staff without back-and-forth debate—and Bettina Umstead highlighted Exceptional Children and ESL students as key graduation-rate priority groups. Later in the retreat, CFO Paul LeSieur and HR Director Atkins presented a $1.5 million proposal (Option 2A) to raise local teacher supplements from 12.5% to 14% for teachers with 0-10 years of experience while warning of future local budget pressure from state raises and announcing restorative practices coordinators in every middle and high school. After a closed session, the board unanimously approved the June 22, 2018 personnel report 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Moment of Silence, and Agenda Approval
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Dr. Mike Lee welcomed all seven board members, senior administration, and a packed audience to the Staff Development Center retreat and led a moment of silence. The board approved the retreat agenda 7-0 by voice vote and noted no public comment sign-ups.

agenda_items.title: Five-Year Strategic Plan Draft Review
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Superintendent Dr. Pascal Mubenga and staff walked through the draft five-year Strategic Plan developed with a 52-member committee, covering career pathways, spark branding, public and school-level data dashboards, and Priority 1-5 targets. Minnie Forte-Brown and Natalie Beyer questioned 'standardized intervention strategies' under Strategy 4 (citing Reading Street's past failure and avoiding a cookie-cutter approach), prompting discussion with Chair Lee over how member concerns are relayed, while Bettina Umstead noted Exceptional Children and ESL students had the lowest graduation rates.

agenda_items.title: Local Teacher Supplement Increase Proposal and Restorative Practices Staffing
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following a middle gap in the digest, staff presented a $1.5 million proposal (out of $3.4 million in recurring revenue) to raise local teacher supplements from 12.5% to 14% for teachers with 0-10 years of experience to combat high early-career turnover and compete with Wake, Chapel Hill-Carrboro, and Charlotte-Mecklenburg (which just moved to 16%). Administration recommended Option 2A (maintaining percentage format in 2018-19 while flagging a possible shift to fixed-dollar allotments next year, since every 5% state raise adds $1 million in local supplement cost), agreed to study broader pay/benefits (extracurricular, lead teacher, bilingual interpreter pay), and announced restorative practices coordinators in every middle and high school.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Informational / No vote (slated for June 28 approval)

agenda_items.title: Closed Session and June 22, 2018 Personnel Report
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board voted 7-0 to enter closed session for the reasons stated on the agenda. Returning to open session at 05:16:05, the board approved the June 22, 2018 personnel report 7-0 and adjourned.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Closed session and Personnel report each passed 7-0 (Voice)

votes.notes: Unanimous 7-0 voice vote.

votes.notes: Unanimous 7-0 voice vote.
votes.discussion_detail: Returning to open session, the board moved, seconded, and approved the June 22, 2018 personnel report 7-0 by voice vote.

Past districtwide curriculum standardization like Reading Street failed when imposed rigidly

meetings.title: Operational Services & Policy & Academic Student Services Board Work Session June 14, 2018
meetings.executive_summary: In the full ~4 hour 41 minute recording of the June 14, 2018 DPS Board of Education work session, the board unanimously amended its agenda to pull Consent Item 6A (the updated DPS-Student U MOU) to Item 7E, approved prior work session minutes, and approved Consent Items B, C, D, and E after clarifying how committees select consent items. Operations staff recognized Northern Division Bus Driver of the Year Danny Evans, and Budget Process Advisory Committee (BPAC) co-chairs Julie and Emily presented recommendations on inclusive stakeholder engagement, program evaluation questions, and transparent budget visualizations. After a mid-recording digest gap (partially covered in companion Part 1 video Q3w7rFx6jf0), the board discussed Strategic Plan targets—including raising Latino staff from 2% to 10%, art and PE inclusion, and Spanish translation—and reviewed the Restart single-dollar-allotment budget model ($4,878 state and $2,531 local per pupil) for Glenn and Lakewood Elementary Schools. The board unanimously approved a school bell-time adjustment recommendation with staff pay accounted for, requested a Spanish interpreter for future full board meetings, and unanimously approved the June 14 personnel report following closed session.

agenda_items.title: Strategic Plan Discussion and Restart Schools Update (Glenn & Lakewood Elementary)

CFO Paul LeSieur and Ms. Stroud then detailed the Restart single-dollar-allotment model for Lakewood and Glenn Elementary Schools ($4,878 state and $2,531 local per pupil), flexibility with lapsed salaries, teacher experience cost trade-offs, and Lexia, Imagine Learning, and Eureka Math adoption.

agenda_items.title: Bell Time Adjustment Approval

The recording concludes during a detailed review of the draft Strategic Plan covering Vision statements, Priority 1 school-growth and proficiency baselines (46.4% vs. 58.9% state average), teacher turnover metric phrasing, and Priority 4 family engagement baselines.

meetings.title: Durham Public Schools Board of Education Monthly Meeting May 23, 2018 6:30 PM
meetings.executive_summary: At its May 23, 2018 monthly meeting, the Durham Public Schools Board of Education observed a moment of silence for Hospital School Principal Dr. Kendra O'Neill's daughter Jillian Ray Catherine Williams and Carrington Middle School student Terrell Taylor before holding extensive end-of-year celebrations honoring Media Coordinator of the Year Elizabeth Huskiff, Battle of the Books champions, National Latin Exam awardees, magnet award schools, and faith/community partners who fed students during the May 16 teacher walkout. Following a mid-meeting gap in the digest, operations staff reported a ~$20 million construction shortfall on the Northern High School replacement project (originally budgeted at $51.875 million in 2014) amid $90 million in 2016 bond funding vs. $186 million requested, and board members gave informal direction to pursue additional county funding while advancing design and land exploration. The board unanimously approved the 2018-19 meeting calendar as amended by Matt Sears (moving May 8 to May 9 and June 12 to June 13). On the procedural motion to enter closed session, the board passed a 6-1 split voice vote (six unnamed members voting Aye and one unnamed member voting Nay, with individual member names not announced in the transcript), before returning to open session to unanimously approve the May 23, 2018 personnel report.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order and Moment of Silence
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Dr. Mike Lee convened the regular monthly meeting and led a moment of silence extending condolences to Hospital School Principal Dr. Kendra O'Neill on the loss of her daughter Jillian Ray Catherine Williams and to the Taylor family on the loss of Carrington Middle School student Terrell Taylor.

agenda_items.title: End-of-Year Celebrations and May 16 Community Meal Support Recognition
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board honored the Student of the Month, Social Worker of the Year Ms. Martin, Media Coordinator of the Year Elizabeth Huskiff (Club Boulevard), Battle of the Books teams (Hillandale Elementary, DSA, Riverside High), Lakewood National Latin Exam winners, Magnet School honorees (School for Creative Studies and Club Boulevard), and high school honorees. Simone Kado of the Durham Association of Educators also recognized NC Council of Churches, Wall Street Baptist Church/Rebound, and St. John's Missionary Baptist Church for feeding students during the May 16 teacher rally.

agenda_items.title: Superintendent's Update, Northern High School Replacement Shortfall, and 2016 Bond Progress
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Superintendent Dr. Pascal Mubenga began his update prior to a digest gap, after which operations director Mr. Long briefed the board on a $20 million shortfall on the 250,000-square-foot Northern High School replacement (originally budgeted at $51,875,000 in 2014) driven by site constraints ($4 million premium) and market construction inflation. Noting the county funded $90 million of the district's $186 million bond request while most other 2019 bond projects were expedited to finish by late 2018, board members voiced frustration over deteriorating Northern conditions and gave informal direction to seek additional funding while pursuing design and land acquisition.

agenda_items.title: 2018-2019 Board of Education Meeting Calendar Approval
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board reviewed the proposed 2018-19 meeting calendar and Matt Sears amended his motion to shift two meeting dates from May 8 to May 9 and June 12 to June 13. The amended calendar passed unanimously by voice vote.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session (6-1 Split Vote) and May 23, 2018 Personnel Report
agenda_items.discussion_summary: On a voice vote to enter closed session for the reasons stated on the agenda, one unnamed board member voted in opposition and the motion carried 6-1. Returning to open session at 03:15:02, the board unanimously approved the May 23, 2018 personnel report and adjourned.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Closed session passed 6-1 (Voice); Personnel report passed unanimously (Voice)

votes.notes: Unanimous voice vote.

meetings.title: Operational Services & Policy/Academic Student Services Board Work Session May 10, 2018 4:30 PM
meetings.executive_summary: At its May 10, 2018 combined work session presided over by Vice Chair Natalie Beyer, the Durham Public Schools Board of Education heard public comment from George Watts Montessori staff requesting elimination or reduction of pre-K tuition for DPS teachers under Policy 4115 and unanimously approved the $432 million FY 2018-19 budget (including a $4.9 million new money request: $3.9 million for DPS and $1.0 million for charter schools) for submission to the County Commissioners. Operational Services staff briefed the board on stalled affordable teacher housing negotiations with CASA over 30-year property equity, prompting unanimous support to explore alternative foundation or nonprofit models, while Item 7C (Technology Purchases) passed 6-1 by voice vote without individual member votes read into the record after one member objected that full plan details were expected at the May 24 meeting. The board also heard an update on the nascent DPS Education Foundation, reviewed first-reading revisions to Policy 4303 governing alternative services and Lakeview School (unanimously advancing it to May 24 with potential language refinements), and unanimously approved a $118,035 Title IV Part A summer reading initiative distributing 98,300 books with Book Harvest and American Reading Company. Following a closed session, the board unanimously approved the May 10, 2018 personnel report before adjourning.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Moment of Silence, and Agenda Review and Approval
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The work session was called to order and opened with a moment of silence. Staff requested moving Item 6B (Technology Purchase) from the consent agenda to Item 7C under Operational Services, and the board approved the amended agenda on a motion by Bettina Umstead seconded by Xavier Cason.

agenda_items.title: General Public Comment: Pre-K Tuition for DPS Teachers
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Two George Watts Montessori employees (Amanda Watson and a colleague) asked the board to revise Policy 4115 (A3D) so all DPS teachers, regardless of Durham County residency or magnet status, can enroll their children in DPS pre-K without tuition. They offered three options: zero tuition, calculating tuition solely on the teacher's salary rather than household income, or a 50% tuition reduction.

agenda_items.title: Approval of April 19, 2018 Work Session Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board reviewed the minutes from the April 19, 2018 board work session. Matt Sears moved approval and Dr. Mike Lee seconded with no further discussion.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Approval
agenda_items.discussion_summary: With Item 6B moved to Operational Services Item 7C, the remaining consent agenda covered the Club Boulevard Roof Replacement Project contract, IT SmartNet equipment warranty and maintenance, a waste and recycling contract amendment, Budget Amendment #2 for 2017-18, and the annual security contract. Dr. Mike Lee moved approval and Steve Unruhe seconded.

agenda_items.title: Operational Services: Affordable Teacher Housing Proposal (CASA)

Staff presented Asheville and other school-system examples using closely aligned foundations or local charities, and the board voiced unanimous support for continuing teacher housing efforts.

agenda_items.title: Approval of FY 2018-19 Budget
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff presented the $432 million FY 2018-19 budget following the May 3 public hearing, including a $4.9 million new money request ($3.9 million for DPS and $1.0 million for charter schools) ahead of the May 15 statutory deadline to submit to County Commissioners. Board members described the budget as a holding pattern pending the new strategic plan and emphasized adding bilingual counselors and interpreters using fund balance or open positions.

agenda_items.title: Operational Services Item 7C: Technology Purchases
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Scott Denton and Elaine Batten presented the technology purchase item moved from consent, and board discussion emphasized expanding 1:1 device access beyond school hours to students' homes. agenda_items.title: DPS Education Foundation Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Dr. Pascal Mubenga introduced Jim Key, Larry Hurst (Triangle E-Cycling), and Megan Thigpen (with Zach Hawkins absent) as the four-person organizing team spearheading the new Durham Public Schools Education Foundation. agenda_items.title: Policy 4303 Revision (First Reading — Alternative Services & Lakeview School)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Board members reviewed first-reading revisions to Policy 4303 authorizing superintendent discretion when serious misconduct or threats make alternative services infeasible, while stressing that Lakeview School must maintain an educational, non-prison environment with vocational opportunities and community oversight. Natalie Beyer urged narrower wording so ordinary school fights could not be swept into the exclusion criteria, and the board voted unanimously to place Policy 4303 on the May 24 consent agenda with refined language if needed.

meetings.title: Durham Public Schools BOE Public Hearing and Board Work Session FY 2018-19 Budget May 3, 2018 5:30PM
meetings.executive_summary: The Durham Public Schools Board of Education convened a special meeting on May 3, 2018 presided over by Chair Dr. Mike Lee to hold the statutory public hearing and work session on the proposed FY 2018-19 budget, unanimously approving the meeting agenda as its sole formal vote. During public comment, speakers urged support for Rebound Alternatives for Youth conflict-mediation services, praised the transition toward in-house custodial services and improved budget transparency, requested dedicated funding for bilingual staff and ESL interpreters, and called for funding nurses, social workers, and psychologists rather than school resource officers while raising concerns over flat local teacher supplements ahead of the May 16 Raleigh rally. CFO Aaron Beaulieu reviewed the $432.9 million budget proposal ($410.0 million DPS, $22.8 million charter schools), including a $4.9 million new money request ($3.9 million DPS, $1.0 million charters), a $1.6 million fund balance appropriation, a $17.7 million capital budget, and over $140 million in combined county requests. Board members framed the continuation budget as a bridge to Superintendent Dr. Pascal Mubenga's upcoming strategic plan while questioning reliance on $1.6 million in lapsed-salary fund balance and confirming details on the two-school community schools pilot.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Moment of Silence, and Agenda Approval
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Dr. Mike Lee called the special public hearing and budget work session to order, led a moment of silence, and noted the small crowd compared to the previous night's May 2 meeting. The board moved, seconded, and unanimously approved the agenda as written.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing Comment on FY 2018-19 Proposed Budget
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Speakers included Amy Rublin (President of Rebound Alternatives for Youth) seeking funding alignment for conflict-mediation alternatives to suspension, a speaker praising the in-house custodial transition and data-driven budget work, a Spanish-speaking parent (via translator) requesting increased funding for bilingual/ESL personnel, and a DAE-affiliated speaker applauding the new budget book and custodial plan while urging investments in nurses, social workers, psychologists, ESL services, and local teacher supplements instead of SROs.

agenda_items.title: FY 2018-19 Proposed Budget Review and Discussion
agenda_items.discussion_summary: CFO Aaron Beaulieu presented the $432.9 million proposed budget ($410 million DPS, $22.8 million charters), $4.9 million new money request ($3.9 million DPS, $1.0 million charters), $1.6 million fund balance use, $17.7 million capital outlay budget ($1.37 million county appropriation), and Budget Process Advisory Committee (BPAC) contributions ahead of May 10 board approval and May 15 county delivery. Board members discussed the modest continuation ask pending Dr. Mubenga's Blueprint strategic plan, the teacher deferred needs placeholder, funding for two community schools pilot sites, and concerns about propping up recurring operations with lapsed-salary fund balance.

agenda_items.title: Final Public Comment Opportunity and Adjournment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: After concluding board budget discussion, Chair Dr. Mike Lee invited any late-arriving members of the public to offer public comment. Seeing no additional speakers, he adjourned the meeting.

votes.item_title: Approval of May 3, 2018 Special Meeting Agenda
votes.notes: Unanimous voice vote; no action was taken on the budget itself during the public hearing.
votes.discussion_detail: The board moved, seconded, and unanimously approved the May 3, 2018 public hearing and budget work session agenda as written.
