meetings.title: Durham Public Schools Board of Education Special Called Meeting May 2, 2018 5:30 PM
meetings.executive_summary: At a packed May 2, 2018 special called meeting presided over by Chair Dr. Mike Lee to address contingency plans for the May 16 statewide teacher rally in Raleigh, the board unanimously amended the agenda to allow public comment and heard urgent testimony from parents, students, and educators—including Stephanie Lynch, Turquoise LeJeune Parker, Brianna Kennedy, and Melanie Middleton—calling for schools to close on May 16 due to classroom underfunding, large class sizes, and low educator pay. Superintendent Dr. Pascal Mubenga reported that 1,028 teachers had requested personal leave as of that morning and detailed operational challenges including summer feeding equity and estimated single-day income losses of roughly $50,000 for transportation employees and $100,000 in child nutrition revenue. Board members discussed the impossibility of safely staffing schools with over 1,000 teacher absences and confirmed that closing to students as an optional teacher workday would prevent teachers from losing personal leave or pay. By a 6-1 show-of-hands vote—with individual member votes not read into the record, though Steve Unruhe and other speakers explicitly declared support during debate—the board adopted Option 2 closing schools to students and designating May 16, 2018 as an optional teacher workday.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Moment of Silence, and Amended Agenda Approval
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Dr. Mike Lee convened the special called meeting to review contingency plans for more than 800–900 educators expected absent on May 16 and led a moment of silence. On his request, the board unanimously amended the agenda to hear public comment prior to the administration's update.

agenda_items.title: Public Comment on May 16 School Operations
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Parents, teachers, and students (including Stephanie Lynch, Joy Harrell Goff, Turquoise LeJeune Parker, Brianna Kennedy, student Aria, Melanie Middleton, Teresa DeLaCruz, and student Iwati) urged the board to close schools on May 16. Speakers cited inadequate teacher pay, personal financial hardship, shortages of instructional assistants and classroom supplies, and overcrowded classes such as 45 students in a room equipped for 25.

agenda_items.title: May 16 Contingency Options and School Closure Vote (Option 2)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Dr. Pascal Mubenga reported 1,028 teacher personal-day requests and outlined impacts on summer feeding equity, ~$50,000 in transportation worker pay, and ~$100,000 in child nutrition revenue. Board members (including Steve Unruhe, who pledged to march in Raleigh with a photo of his father's LA strike picket sign) discussed AP/IB testing and feeding logistics, confirmed teachers would not be docked personal leave under an optional workday, and voted 6-1 by show of hands to adopt Option 2 closing schools to students on May 16.

votes.item_title: Approval of Amended May 2, 2018 Special Meeting Agenda Adding Public Comment
votes.notes: Unanimous voice vote.
votes.discussion_detail: Following Chair Dr. Mike Lee's request to add public comment before the administration's May 16 update, a motion and second were made and passed unanimously by voice vote.

votes.item_title: Adoption of Option 2 Closing Schools to Students and Designating May 16, 2018 as an Optional Teacher Workday
votes.notes: Vote conducted by show of hands ('vote by hands') with tally announced as 6-1; individual member votes were not read aloud on the record, though Steve Unruhe explicitly spoke in support of closing schools on May 16.
votes.discussion_detail: Chair Dr. Mike Lee entertained a motion to accept Option 2 closing schools to students and designating May 16, 2018 as an optional teacher workday; the motion was moved, seconded, and passed 6-1 by show of hands.

disagreements.meeting_title: Durham Public Schools Board of Education Special Called Meeting May 2, 2018 5:30 PM
disagreements.issue: Closing DPS schools to students on May 16, 2018 as an optional teacher workday (Option 2)
disagreements.summary: The board voted 6-1 by show of hands to adopt Administration Option 2 closing schools to students and designating May 16, 2018 as an optional teacher workday amid 1,028 teacher personal-day requests for the Raleigh education rally. Six members supported closure to ensure safety and stand with educators, while one unidentified member opposed the motion after discussion noted impacts on AP/IB testing, student meals, and classified staff wages.
disagreements.side_a_position: Close schools to students on May 16, 2018 and designate the day as an optional teacher workday so educators can rally without losing personal leave.
side_a_arguments: 1,028 teacher personal-day requests make normal safe school operations and instruction impossible.
Supporting teachers' advocacy in Raleigh for state funding and pay benefits students and public education long term.
Making May 16 an optional teacher workday prevents teachers from losing personal leave or pay.
disagreements.side_b_position: Oppose closing schools to students on May 16, 2018.
side_b_arguments: Closing schools disrupts student instruction, AP/IB and early-calendar exams, and school-based meals.
A closure creates an estimated $50,000 pay loss for transportation workers and $100,000 revenue loss for child nutrition.

boe_dae_events.event_title: May 16 Educator Day of Action — Approval of Option 2 (Schools Closed / Optional Teacher Workday)
boe_dae_events.issue_category: DAE Advocacy / Recognition / Day of Action
boe_dae_events.dae_position: DAE representatives and 28 educators, classified workers, parents, and students demanded the board adopt Option 2 to close schools for students as an optional teacher workday after 1,028 teachers committed to attend the May 16 Raleigh rally, rather than keeping schools open or using an early-release compromise.

member_positions.stance_summary: Endorsed Option 2 outright, declaring the district could not provide a safe environment with 1,028 educators absent while rejecting claims that closing schools teaches the wrong lesson, arguing students learn civic participation by seeing adults stand up for them. Recounted his Los Angeles teacher father's strike sign—'Teachers want what children need'—and pledged to carry it in Raleigh (individual 6-1 show-of-hands vote not read into the record).
member_positions.key_quote: We are unable to provide a safe environment and that is our top priority, and yes, our children will indeed learn a lesson in civic participation.

member_positions.stance_summary: Expressed explicit support for closing schools on May 16, noting 1,028 teachers were sacrificing pay and instructional time because state policies like K-3 class-size mandates and ISD hurt classrooms. Urged partnering with the city, county, and faith groups on food and childcare while framing May 16 as one step in a broader power-sharing campaign (individual 6-1 show-of-hands vote not read into the record).
member_positions.key_quote: So I support us closing on May 16th, I think we need to do that for all those people.

member_positions.stance_summary: Rejected Superintendent Mubenga's preferred Option 3 early-release compromise because it depended on capping morning absences at 250 when 1,028 educators had already committed to go to Raleigh. Speaking as a former band teacher and the child of two teachers, concluded the district lacked the staffing numbers to open safely (individual 6-1 show-of-hands vote not read into the record).
member_positions.key_quote: The numbers don't add up to me to where we can open on May 16th.

member_positions.stance_summary: Cited her segregated-school mother and her own participation in a 1972 Baltimore teachers' strike to affirm solidarity with teachers' struggle against North Carolina's 47th-place pay ranking, yet read a Durham Committee on the Affairs of Black People statement opposing preemptive closure and declared 'Of course I believe in the compromise, the third option.' Warned closing schools would leave homeless and free-lunch students vulnerable on the streets and urged teachers to prepare for sustained statewide political organizing beyond one march ('Stay woke') (likely lone NAY in 6-1 hand vote, though individual votes were not read aloud).
member_positions.key_quote: Now it looks like the decision has been made; of course I believe in the compromise, the third option.

member_positions.stance_summary: Invoked her grandmother's pay discrimination as a single-mother principal to frame teacher advocacy as justice in a female-dominated profession and apologized that the board had delayed a week before uniting behind educators. Dismissed Options 1 and 3 as unviable—stating DPS does not exist without its teachers—and pledged to join staff in Raleigh (individual 6-1 show-of-hands vote not read into the record).
member_positions.key_quote: I appreciate options being on the table, but to me, two of the three options aren't even valid for consideration, and I look forward to join you in Raleigh on May 16.

member_positions.stance_summary: Took chair responsibility for the five-day wait to verify community food and care infrastructure, noting DAE representatives and teachers had already been organizing support sites behind the scenes despite facing $50 substitute deductions. Concluded closing schools was the 'only option that's viable here' and promised to stand with educators in Raleigh on May 16 (individual 6-1 show-of-hands vote not read into the record).
member_positions.key_quote: There's only one option that's viable here, and that option is to close schools, and I will be with you in Raleigh on May 16th.

member_positions.stance_summary: Pressed to clarify on record that under Option 2 teachers would not have to pay out-of-pocket for substitutes, while noting legally the superintendent holds operational authority over school closures and the board's vote gives policy direction. Confident administration would resolve remaining IB/AP and operational logistics before May 16 (individual 6-1 show-of-hands vote not read into the record).
member_positions.key_quote: It's still a concern to me about whether teachers are paying out of pocket with this option; I think what I want to do is give the administration direction to resolve these issues.

meetings.title: Durham Public Schools Board of Education Monthly Meeting April 26, 2018 6:30 PM
meetings.executive_summary: At its April 26, 2018 monthly meeting presided over by Chair Dr. Mike Lee, the Durham Public Schools Board of Education held a moment of silence for Spring Valley Principal Gwendolyn Wilson's late son, recognized National Board Certified teachers and Hillside High School Student of the Month Amaya Jarman, and heard 22 public speakers urging school closure for the May 16 teacher rally in Raleigh. After debating whether to constrain principals on granting personal leave amid 791 reported teacher absences, the board passed a 5-2 voice vote—with individual member votes not read into the record—directing Superintendent Dr. Pascal Mubenga to bring back a contingency plan for May 16. The board also reviewed the FY 2018-19 proposed continuation budget (highlighting a $4 million DPS local ask, interactive transparency tools, and a two-school community schools pilot funded via fund balance), unanimously approved the custodial services contract contingent on legal review preserving existing part-time wages and Schedule C, and unanimously approved the April 26, 2018 personnel report following closed session.

Celebrations recognized Student of the Month Amaya Jarman (in absentia for a scholarship interview), National Board Certified teachers, and Capturing Kids' Hearts, followed by Dr. Pascal Mubenga's update on district leadership data reviews and the 52-member Strategic Planning Committee.

disagreements.side_a_position: Direct administration to bring back a formal May 16 contingency plan for board consideration at a special meeting.
side_a_arguments: 791 teacher absences already exceed the district substitute pool and preclude normal instruction.
Directing a contingency plan sets clear direction and gives staff and community time to coordinate testing, meals, and childcare.
disagreements.side_b_position: Oppose the motion directing a formal contingency plan with added board conditions.
side_b_arguments: Adding board contingencies around principal leave approvals makes developing an operational plan more problematic for administration.
Further study with administration is needed before locking in directives.
disagreements.resolution: Motion passed 5-2 by voice vote (individual Aye and Nay voters were not named on the record), leading to the May 2 special called meeting.

boe_dae_events.event_title: May 16 Educator Day of Action Contingency Plan Directive
boe_dae_events.issue_category: DAE Advocacy / Recognition / Day of Action
boe_dae_events.dae_position: DAE President Bryan Proffitt and over 20 educators and parents reported 791 DPS teacher personal-leave requests (up to 99% at Southwest Elementary) for the May 16 Raleigh rally and called on the board to close schools so staff could advocate for state education funding.

member_positions.stance_summary: Stated the board stood with teachers against North Carolina's 'embarrassing' 47th-place national pay ranking, yet read a skeptical email from a political action group concerned about lost instructional days at 21 turnaround schools and raised AP exam conflicts. Ultimately moved the directive (confirmed by Minutes) instructing administration to prepare a May 16 contingency plan for 800+ absences rather than immediately closing schools (individual 5-2 votes were not read aloud).
member_positions.key_quote: I have an email from a political action group here that has a different take on it, that is also being somewhat skeptical about the closing of schools and saying to us that they are watching to see what we're doing in terms of making sure that our children don't miss a day of education.

member_positions.stance_summary: Praised DAE organizing, declared HR's absence data proved schools could not operate safely on May 16, and pledged to march in Raleigh alongside teachers because inflation-adjusted state funding lagged behind 2008 levels. Urged relieving principals of leave-approval pressure and seconded Forte-Brown's contingency-plan motion (confirmed by Minutes) while pushing for an emergency meeting early the next week to finalize closure logistics.
member_positions.key_quote: What I do think that I've heard all seven of us say loud and clear is that our staff shows us with 791 absences far exceeds our sub pool or any way that we would be able to actually have a viable school day.

member_positions.stance_summary: Recalled family lessons from MLK Day advocacy and initially sought clarity on existing contingency preparations before pushing hard to make a closure decision immediately that night rather than waiting a week, warning delay could forfeit vital community mobilization time. Accepted the special-meeting timeline once apparent the majority wanted more planning (individual 5-2 vote not recorded aloud).
member_positions.key_quote: I'm worried we won't use this week as well as we could unless all of us kind of take up and advocate hard for what these solutions can be, and that's why I'm pushing hard for tonight is that I think a week does matter.

member_positions.stance_summary: Argued schools cannot offer a safe learning environment with 60% to 99% of staff out and backed educators marching in Raleigh for better working conditions, pay, and retention. Proposed giving administration space to bring concrete options to an emergency meeting early the following week so families would get timely clarity (individual 5-2 vote not recorded aloud).
member_positions.key_quote: The reason for the teachers being in Raleigh on May 16th is that we get better conditions and for the students to have teachers who are going to work in the district for at least three years or longer.

member_positions.stance_summary: Shared that he left the classroom after losing Master's and National Board pay incentives following state cuts around 2010 and strongly urged closing schools immediately that night rather than merely charging administration to return with a plan. Argued community partners would only mobilize around meal and childcare coverage once the board made a decisive commitment (individual 5-2 vote not recorded aloud).
member_positions.key_quote: I'm one person that's ready to vote today, and my concern with charging the administration is I think our community is going to wait for us to make a decision before they decide if we're going to go into this and bring the community resources around it.

member_positions.stance_summary: Stated bluntly he saw no way to offer instruction on May 16 and highlighted DAE-identified logistics including AP/IB exams, student meals, and protecting hourly workers' pay—especially after the board's recent push to take care of custodians—perhaps by swapping a scheduled teacher workday. Urged principals to respect teacher leave requests while supporting giving administration a short window to solve calendar-law constraints (individual 5-2 vote not recorded aloud).
member_positions.key_quote: I don't see any way that we offer instructional time on May 16th, so the question is, what do we do with our children and how do we meet their needs while simultaneously honoring and respecting the advocacy work of our teachers?

member_positions.stance_summary: Affirmed personal solidarity with teachers—noting he had met with Bryan Proffitt and DAE, planned to buy a red shirt, and would attend the May 16 rally—while arguing Durham leads best when it pairs advocacy with a concrete care plan. Declined to vote to close schools immediately until administration worked with DAE to verify meal and childcare capacity for roughly 20,000 vulnerable students (individual 5-2 vote not recorded aloud).
member_positions.key_quote: I'm not ready to vote a yes for closing the school today because I want to charge the administration to develop this plan with DAE before we do that.

boe_dae_events.event_title: FY 2018-19 Proposed Continuation Budget Discussion (Staff Pay, Custodial Living Wage & Community Schools)
boe_dae_events.dae_position: DAE and staff advocates pressed for sustained local investment in teacher and classified raises, in-house custodial living wages, and funding for Community Schools coordinators beyond two district-funded pilot sites.

member_positions.stance_summary: Warned that a conservative continuation budget risked letting DPS fall further behind Wake and Chapel Hill-Carrboro on local teacher salary supplements and urged asking County Commissioners sooner rather than later. Pointed out that the entire ~$4 million new local request merely covered inflation, custodial living wages, and SROs while deferred teacher needs relied on internal savings.
member_positions.key_quote: My biggest concern really when I look at some of that information is that I see we're not keeping up with Wake and Chapel Hill in local salary supplements, and we can't fall behind.

member_positions.stance_summary: Supported the transparent continuation budget in a transition year and commended the disaggregated racial achievement data in the new budget book. Challenged the district to tie real budget dollars in the next cycle to closing equity gaps.
member_positions.key_quote: So what I'm looking for in the next cycle's budget is dollars attached to these challenges.

member_positions.stance_summary: Praised the budget book's collaborative preparation and responsible fund-balance use, noting with relief that the district was not facing another 'budget crisis.' Questioned specifically what funding remained allocated in the budget for the Community Schools resolution.
member_positions.key_quote: It feels good to know that we're really sitting back and looking at things broadly and that we're using our fund balance wisely.

member_positions.stance_summary: Appreciated linking academic data to budget transparency and asked how restart schools would be funded in upcoming budget plans. Supported Dr. Mubenga's strategic approach to pairing new funding requests with clear performance goals.
member_positions.key_quote: I appreciate the connection of our academic data and some of these other points that always need to be connected to our budget.

member_positions.stance_summary: Commended the Budget Process Advisory Committee and administration for creating an interactive, transparent budget document and backed using fund balance strategically for the upcoming Strategic Plan rollout before requesting broader county increases.
member_positions.key_quote: I am in favor of the continuing budget because this is tied to the overall plan of doing the strategic plan now.

member_positions.stance_summary: Pressed administration for public updates on Community Schools funding—specifically asking what happened after the board's earlier Community Schools vote—and bilingual services, while underscoring the importance of keeping the public hearing separate from final budget adoption so community concerns could be heard.
member_positions.key_quote: The community is asking us about several things from community schools to bilingual services, and so I think we do need to go on record to share with the community where we are on some of these things.

member_positions.stance_summary: Endorsed the continuation budget's framing—'continuation budget, but not business as usual'—signaling support for shifting priorities under the incoming Strategic Plan without requesting excessive unfocused tax increases.
member_positions.key_quote: What I like most is the phrase after the comma, but not business as usual.

boe_dae_events.event_title: Custodial Services Interim Contract Approval (SSC Service Solutions)
boe_dae_events.dae_position: Custodial representative Deborah Bailey and sustainability coordinator Brian Callaway warned the interim SSC Service Solutions contract lacked Attachment C service specifications, omitted explicit part-time wage guarantees, and dropped a contested 7.5% healthcare supplement.

member_positions.stance_summary: Pressed COO Aaron Beaulieu to verify whether legal counsel had reviewed the omission of Attachment C before moving approval contingent on legal verification that existing part-time wages remained intact and Attachment C was included. Sought to keep the six-month bridge in place so the December in-house custodial transition could proceed.
member_positions.key_quote: I would move approval of the contract contingent upon legal review that ensures we have a continuation of the same part-time wages as the previous contract and Attachment C.

member_positions.stance_summary: Questioned administration directly on custodian Deborah Bailey's concerns over the dropped 7.5% healthcare supplement and pressed legal counsel on how part-time wage rates were contractually guaranteed if not printed in the draft text. Voted for the contract only once conditioned on attorney review ensuring part-time pay protections.
member_positions.key_quote: Mr. Beaulieu, you were saying that they're going to get paid what they were getting paid before, so it sounds like the board is asking, what's the mechanism by which we know that?

member_positions.stance_summary: Promised to circulate final reviewed contract documents and contact every board member individually before signing the agreement, and sought clear answers for Ms. Bailey on whether the $15 full-time wage was protected and why part-time rates were omitted.
member_positions.key_quote: Before I signed it, we would send it out to everyone, and I would call each one of you guys individually and talk about it.

member_positions.stance_summary: Acknowledged DPS needed a bridge vendor to keep schools clean until December, but warned Service Solutions 'they aren't doing us any favors' and criticized their $10,000 summer premium as trying to extract extra profit from taxpayers. Instructed district legal counsel to push back hard in final contract checks.
member_positions.key_quote: Service Solutions needs to know that they aren't doing us any favors, that we are clearly paying them, and then with this $10,000 extra, they're really trying to get a little butter from the duck.

meetings.title: Operational Services & Policy/Academic Student Services Board Work Session April 19, 2018 4:30 PM
meetings.executive_summary: At its April 19, 2018 combined work session presided over by Chair Dr. Mike Lee, the Durham Public Schools Board of Education unanimously approved the Toshiba print-managed services contract, a Memorandum of Understanding with CASA for the Affordable Teacher Housing project, and the consent agenda (Parkwood and Spaulding roof replacements and the quarterly capital change order report). During the Toshiba copier contract discussion, a board member criticized receiving a May 1 contract so close to its start date after reducing monthly board meetings from three to two, while still supporting the collaborative IT-finance procurement that returns standalone printer and toner costs to school budgets. Staff paid tribute to CASA CEO Debra King following her recent passing and reported that Senator McKissick was finalizing local teacher-housing bill language, leading to unanimous MOU approval so CASA could submit its credit union grant application. On the $3.5 million-plus interim custodial contract covering over 300 custodians prior to moving services in-house, members voiced frustration over receiving printed copies at the dais and voted unanimously to advance the custodial contract to the April 26 regular board meeting for action before entering closed session and adjourning with no post-session action.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Moment of Silence, and Agenda Approval
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Dr. Mike Lee called the delayed work session to order after traffic delayed several members and led a moment of silence. Steve Unruhe moved and Xavier Cason seconded approval of the agenda, which passed unanimously.

agenda_items.title: Public Comment (Custodial Contract and PBIS)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Jackie Wagstaff signed up for general public comment to address Item 8 (the custodial contract) early in the meeting. Later during the mid-meeting public comment break (01:18:34), Jacqueline and other speakers commented on Positive Behavior Intervention and Support (PBIS) at Holt Elementary, Brogden Middle, and Northern High School.

agenda_items.title: Approval of March 8, 2018 Minutes and Consent Agenda
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board unanimously approved the March 8, 2018 board work session minutes. It then unanimously approved the three-item Operational Services consent agenda: roof replacement contracts for Parkwood and Spaulding elementaries and the quarterly capital change order report.

agenda_items.title: Academic & Student Support Services and Strategic Planning Updates
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Dr. Stacey Hardy and Ms. Cross presented academic and student support updates, noting 82 students at Jordan and 28 at Northern and discussing program results and communications. Dr. Hardy then provided an informational progress update on the Strategic Planning Committee's framework, belief statements, vision, and timeline.

agenda_items.title: Operational Services: Print Managed Services / Copier Contract (Toshiba)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Scott Denton and Elaine Batten presented the cross-collaborative IT and finance RFP selecting Toshiba within existing copier budgets while eliminating costly standalone printers and freeing school budgets (excluding paper, which remains cheaper on state contract). One board member criticized voting on a May 1 contract so late after moving to two meetings per month, though the contract passed unanimously.

agenda_items.title: Affordable Teacher Housing Memorandum of Understanding with CASA
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff announced the passing of CASA CEO Debra King and credited her leadership in spearheading the Affordable Teacher Housing Project while noting Senator McKissick was finalizing local enabling legislation. The board unanimously approved the MOU with CASA so the organization could submit its credit union grant application.

agenda_items.title: Custodial Services Contract Review ($3.5M+)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff presented a $3.5 million-plus interim custodial contract covering more than 300 custodians, including a $10,000 three-month summer supplies trade-off and transition timeline toward an in-house custodial model with custodian representatives (Debora, Janice, and Theo). Expressing concern over receiving printed copies at the dais, the board voted unanimously to move the contract to action at the April 26 regular board meeting.

agenda_items.title: Follow-Up Items and Closed Session
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff summarized follow-ups on the PBIS public comments (Holt, Brogden, and Northern) and advancing the custodial contract to April 26. The board voted unanimously to enter closed session for personnel and confidential student matters, later reconvening in open session with no action and adjourning.

votes.item_title: Approval of April 19, 2018 Work Session Agenda
votes.notes: Unanimous voice vote.
votes.discussion_detail: Steve Unruhe moved and Xavier Cason seconded approval of the April 19, 2018 work session agenda; passed unanimously by voice vote.

votes.item_title: Approval of March 8, 2018 Work Session Minutes
votes.notes: Unanimous voice vote.
votes.discussion_detail: The board moved, seconded, and unanimously approved the March 8, 2018 board work session minutes.

votes.item_title: Approval of Print Managed Services Contract with Toshiba
votes.notes: Unanimous voice vote.
votes.discussion_detail: The board approved the print managed services contract with Toshiba as vendor after revising the motion to reflect the full contract terms.

votes.item_title: Approval of Affordable Teacher Housing Memorandum of Understanding with CASA
votes.notes: Unanimous voice vote.
votes.discussion_detail: The board moved, seconded, and unanimously approved the MOU with CASA to support its credit union grant application for the Affordable Teacher Housing Project.

votes.item_title: Motion to Move Custodial Contract to April 26, 2018 Regular Board Meeting for Action
votes.notes: Unanimous voice vote.
votes.discussion_detail: After noting the $3.5M+ custodial contract had just been distributed at the dais, the board voted unanimously to place the contract on the April 26 regular board meeting agenda for action while accepting the transition timeline as informational.

votes.item_title: Motion to Enter Closed Session
votes.notes: Unanimous voice vote; reconvened at 02:42:14 with no action to approve.
votes.discussion_detail: The board moved, seconded, and unanimously voted to enter closed session to address personnel matters and confidential student information.

meetings.title: Durham Public Schools Board of Education Monthly Meeting March 22, 2018 6:30 PM
meetings.executive_summary: At its March 22, 2018 monthly meeting presided over by Chair Dr. Mike Lee (with two board absences noted initially and one member arriving shortly thereafter), the Durham Public Schools Board of Education heard Dr. Pascal Mubenga's 90-day entry plan completion report and extensive public testimony from DAE President Bryan Proffitt and parents backing the Community Schools model. The board unanimously approved the 2018-19 small specialty high school calendars, a Gun Violence Prevention Resolution supporting peaceful student walkouts and calling on Congress and the General Assembly to strengthen background checks and raise the minimum age for assault rifles, Take Two EOG/EOC summer test re-administration, and Policy 7410 teacher contracts enabling four-year contracts for over 1,000 certified teachers. CFO Aaron Beaulieu also presented the initial FY 2018-19 budget outline featuring a $4,985,000 new money request ($3,971,000 for DPS and ~$1.0 million for charter schools, alongside $21 million in existing local charter funding across 47 charter schools), 3% certified and 1.5% classified pay assumptions, and an off-duty SRO placeholder. Later, a motion to enter closed session passed 4-1 by voice vote with five members voting and individual member votes not read into the record, after which the board reconvened and unanimously approved the March 22, 2018 personnel report.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Moment of Silence, Celebrations, and Superintendent's Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Dr. Mike Lee convened the meeting, led a moment of silence, and noted the board was down two members before one female member arrived at 00:20:24. Following student and Southern School of Energy and Sustainability parent celebrations, Superintendent Dr. Pascal Mubenga reported completing his 90-day entry plan—visiting every school and meeting principals, DAE, and custodians—and transitioning to strategic plan development.

agenda_items.title: General Public Comment: Community Schools Pilot
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Parents, school counselors, and DAE President Bryan Proffitt spoke in strong support of adopting the Community Schools model across five pilot schools, emphasizing family engagement, wraparound health and social services, and school-level staff votes (including a 69-1 staff vote at one school).

agenda_items.title: Agenda Approval, Minutes, and Consent Agenda
agenda_items.discussion_summary: At the chair's request, the board unanimously amended the agenda to move Item 12A (Gun Violence Prevention Resolution) up to Item 8B while attendees were present. The board then unanimously approved the February 22, 2018 board minutes and the consent agenda setting 2018-19 calendars for small specialty high schools.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Agenda passed Unanimous; Minutes passed Unanimous; Consent passed Unanimous

agenda_items.title: Item 8B: Resolution Regarding Gun Violence Prevention
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following public comment including remarks by NRA life member Lucy Zastro, board members affirmed Second Amendment rights alongside support for students' peaceful First Amendment walkouts and called on Congress and the North Carolina General Assembly to improve background checks and raise the purchase age for assault rifles. The resolution passed unanimously.

agenda_items.title: Summer Programming & Take Two EOG/EOC Re-Administration
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Dr. Stacey Hardy, DeShana Gooch, and Karen Thompson presented 2018 summer learning opportunities including Mission Possible Operation Literacy (86% student growth over baseline), Read to Achieve, Extended School Year, Newcomer Academy, Credit Recovery, and Take Two. The board unanimously approved re-administering EOG and EOC assessments during the Take Two summer program.

agenda_items.title: Policy 7410: Teacher Contracts Revision
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Human Resources presented Policy 7410 technical revisions incorporating prior Policy 5405 language clarifying assignments, licensure, and contract return requirements, positively impacting over 1,000 certified teachers eligible for four-year contracts. Although listed as first reading, the board waived waiting and unanimously approved Policy 7410 as amended on second reading so contracts could be distributed on time.

agenda_items.title: Initial FY 2018-19 Budget Presentation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: CFO Aaron Beaulieu outlined initial FY 2018-19 budget drivers, noting $21 million in local funding across 47 charter schools (16% of every new local dollar) and projecting +300 charter students and -231 DPS students, yielding a $4,985,000 total new money request ($3,971,000 DPS; ~$1.0 million charters) covering 3% certified/1.5% classified raises, an off-duty SRO placeholder, custodial transition, and deferred teacher needs. Board members stressed state budget uncertainty, confirmed the SRO line was a placeholder, and refuted a charter leader's legislative claim of $2,100 per-pupil underfunding.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session and March 22, 2018 Personnel Report
agenda_items.discussion_summary: A motion to enter closed session for the reasons stated on the agenda passed 4-1 on a voice vote with five members voting. Upon returning to open session, the board unanimously approved the March 22, 2018 personnel report and adjourned.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Closed session passed 4-1; Personnel report passed Unanimous

votes.item_title: Approval of Amended March 22, 2018 Agenda Moving Item 12A to 8B
votes.notes: Unanimous voice vote among members present (the chair noted two absences earlier in the meeting and one subsequent arrival at 00:20:24).
votes.discussion_detail: The board moved, seconded, and unanimously approved amending the agenda to move Item 12A (Gun Violence Prevention Resolution) to Item 8B.

votes.item_title: Approval of February 22, 2018 Board Meeting Minutes
votes.notes: Unanimous voice vote among members present.
votes.discussion_detail: The board moved, seconded, and unanimously approved the February 22, 2018 regular board meeting minutes.

votes.item_title: Adoption of Resolution Regarding Gun Violence Prevention
votes.notes: Unanimous voice vote among members present.
votes.discussion_detail: Following public comment and board remarks supporting student walkouts, improved background checks, and raising the minimum age to purchase assault rifles, the board moved, seconded, and unanimously adopted the resolution as written.

votes.item_title: Approval to Re-Administer EOG and EOC Assessments During Take Two Summer Program
votes.notes: Unanimous voice vote among members present.
votes.discussion_detail: The board moved, seconded, and unanimously authorized staff to re-administer End-of-Grade and End-of-Course assessments at the conclusion of the Take Two summer learning program.

votes.item_title: Approval of Policy 7410 (Teacher Contracts) as Amended on Second Reading
votes.notes: Unanimous voice vote among members present.
votes.discussion_detail: To allow timely contract distribution for over 1,000 certified teachers eligible for four-year contracts, the board moved, seconded, and unanimously approved Policy 7410 as amended as a second reading.

votes.item_title: Motion to Enter Closed Session
votes.notes: Split voice vote (4-1) among five present voting members; individual Aye and Nay voter names were not read aloud on the record.
votes.discussion_detail: A motion to enter closed session for the reasons stated on the agenda was seconded and passed 4-1 by voice vote with five members voting.

votes.item_title: Approval of March 22, 2018 Personnel Report
votes.notes: Unanimous voice vote among members present.
votes.discussion_detail: Upon reconvening in open session after closed session, the board moved, seconded, and unanimously approved the March 22, 2018 personnel report.

meetings.executive_summary: At its March 8, 2018 combined work session presided over by Matt Sears (with Board Chair Dr. Mike Lee present through the custodial vote before participating remotely later in the meeting), the Durham Public Schools Board of Education unanimously approved an attorney-client closed session, the consent agenda (including Forest View modular fabrication, Fuller roof replacement, Riverside roof lottery application, Middle College bell schedule, and 2007 bond closures), and, following testimony from 12 custodial workers and advocates, directed staff 7-0 to pursue Custodial Program Option 4 as a fiscally cautious interim transition toward an in-house model. Later, with Dr. Mike Lee absent/remote, the board split 5-1 on Item 8B adopting a Resolution in Support of the Community Schools Initiative in Durham: Natalie Beyer, Steve Unruhe, Bettina Umstead, Matt Sears, and Xavier Cason voted Aye to authorize exploration and partnerships, while Minnie Forte-Brown voted Nay, objecting that the model was aimed at select schools rather than districtwide and questioning its communication and leadership structure. The board also unanimously moved Item 8C (the Gun Violence Prevention Resolution) to the March 22 regular board meeting after setting aside a request to post the unapproved draft online, and unanimously approved the March 8, 2018 personnel report after closed session.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Amended Agenda Approval, Minutes, Consent Agenda, and Attorney-Client Closed Session
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Matt Sears called the work session to order, and the board unanimously approved the amended agenda (adding an attorney-client closed session after 6E and adding the Gun Violence Prevention Resolution as 8C) on a motion by Natalie Beyer seconded by Bettina Umstead. The board then unanimously approved the February 8 work session minutes, the five-item consent agenda (Middle College bell schedule, Forest View modular fabrication, Fuller roof replacement, Riverside partial roof lottery application, and 2007 bond closure/transfer), and entered a brief attorney-client closed session under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3).

agenda_items.title: Item 7A: Custodial Program Updates and Option 4 Direction
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Reconvening in open session, the board heard 12 public commenters (including Lavelle Young, Ms. Watson, and Clifton Holly) opposing custodial outsourcing and calling for living wages, sick days, and benefits. Staff presented four options, noting Option 1 did not reflect Durham values and outlining Option 4—an interim in-house transition paying initial part-time custodians on the state salary schedule ($1.1 million cost vs $1.5 million for Option 3, plus $1.0–$1.2 million equipment startup)—and the board voted 7-0 on Dr. Mike Lee's motion seconded by Steve Unruhe to direct administration to proceed with Option 4.

agenda_items.title: Item 8B: Resolution in Support of Community Schools Initiative in Durham
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following public comment by DAE President Bryan Proffitt and Page McCullough and an overview by Dr. Stacey Hardy, board members debated the Community Schools resolution. Minnie Forte-Brown objected to piloting the model in select schools rather than districtwide and raised concerns over leadership and communication, while Natalie Beyer and Steve Unruhe emphasized it came from the ground up from school staff and simply authorized exploration with city, county, foundation, and Duke partners; the resolution passed 5-1 with Dr. Mike Lee remote.

agenda_items.title: Item 8C: Deferral of Gun Violence Prevention Resolution to March 22
agenda_items.discussion_summary: After Matt Sears noted he had spoken with Chair Dr. Mike Lee, who was watching remotely, Steve Unruhe moved to defer Item 8C (Gun Violence Prevention Resolution) to the March 22 regular board meeting. A proposal to post the unapproved draft online drew two objections and received no vote before the motion to move Item 8C to March 22 passed.

agenda_items.title: Follow-Up Items, Closed Session, and March 8, 2018 Personnel Report
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff summarized follow-ups on custodial implementation timelines, Michael Tharp's data request regarding the Student Code of Conduct task force, and board questions on Code of Conduct data. The board entered closed session on a motion by Natalie Beyer seconded by Steve Unruhe and later reconvened to unanimously approve the March 8, 2018 personnel report.

disagreements.meeting_title: Operational Services & Policy/Academic Student Services Board Work Session March 8, 2018 4:30 PM
disagreements.issue: Resolution in Support of Community Schools Initiative in Durham (pilot scope and governance)
disagreements.summary: With Chair Dr. Mike Lee watching remotely, the board voted 5-1 to adopt a resolution supporting exploration of the Community Schools model in Durham. Five members backed the resolution as a staff-initiated effort authorizing partnerships with local governments, foundations, and Duke University, whereas Minnie Forte-Brown opposed rolling out the model only in select schools rather than districtwide and questioned communication and leadership structure.
disagreements.side_a_position: Adopt the resolution authorizing administration to explore the Community Schools model and seek city, county, foundation, and Duke partnerships for schools whose staff choose to pursue it.
side_a_arguments: The resolution merely authorizes exploration and partner outreach rather than mandating a districtwide rollout.
The initiative arose from the ground up through school staff votes rather than being imposed from central office.
disagreements.side_b_position: Oppose a resolution supporting a Community Schools model limited to select schools.
side_b_arguments: Effective public school models should apply across the entire district rather than being handed only to select schools.
Communication around the resolution was uneven and its success relies heavily on individual leadership rather than a uniform district approach.
disagreements.resolution: Resolution adopted 5-1 by voice vote (Dr. Mike Lee absent/watching remotely).

boe_dae_events.event_title: Custodial Program Update and Transition to In-House Model (Option 4)
boe_dae_events.dae_position: DAE, including President Bryan Proffitt, alongside custodians and employee advocates, urged the board to end outsourcing to SSC Service Solutions, protect workers from vendor retaliation, and bring custodial staff in-house with full DPS benefits and fair pay.

member_positions.stance_summary: Praised custodians and community stakeholders for organizing what he called 'the Durham way' and thanked them for speaking up despite risks with their current employer. Pressed administration to preserve centralized custodial supervision so principals are not overburdened, while ultimately backing Option 4 so DPS could balance custodial equity with upcoming classified-study adjustments and teacher hiring.
member_positions.key_quote: I appreciate so much that you guys said you know what, we're looking for something better in the face of what could happen.

member_positions.stance_summary: Noted that school principals already have to coordinate with building custodians even under subcontractors, then seconded Dr. Mike Lee's motion for Option 4. Explained he wanted to move toward Option 3's full schedule eventually, but backed Option 4 as a fiscally cautious transition while other classified-pay pieces remained unsettled.
member_positions.key_quote: I want to get to option three, but I worry about the scale of that impact right away, so to me option four is a more cautious option.

member_positions.stance_summary: Apologized to custodians she met earlier that week for prior board oversight gaps in outsourced contracts and affirmed that being treated equitably as part of the 'DPS family' is an entitlement of working people. Applied the board's equity lens to endorse promoting experienced in-house staff and voted for Option 4.
member_positions.key_quote: Being able to say that you are a Durham Public Schools employee was so very important to them, that they worked for Durham Public Schools and were treated like those people who are in the family.

member_positions.stance_summary: Explicitly thanked DAE and allied organizers for surfacing custodial inequities the board had missed and called on organizers to join DPS before the County Commissioners to sustain the funding. Initially expressed preference for Option 3, but supported Option 4 once clarified that part-time employees would stay on the state schedule ($11.22-$11.50/hr with state benefits) pending parity with the broader 1,000-employee classified salary study.
member_positions.key_quote: I'm appreciative to DAE and others who have helped organize and bring us the issues about inequity that we didn't even see that were in front of us.

member_positions.stance_summary: Declared 'organizing works, right?' in welcoming custodians' campaign and condemned contractors for failing to meet DPS standards or depriving workers of what they deserve in 2018. Highlighted how bringing custodians in-house builds generational wealth through access to retirement and the State Employees' Credit Union.
member_positions.key_quote: Organizing works, right, and so thank y'all for showing up and keep showing up and continuing to do that and bringing these attentions to light.

member_positions.stance_summary: Presided over the work session discussion, asked administration what decision was required to build the March budget and whether a phased transition was feasible, and steered the board toward a decisive vote rather than dragging the issue out. Supported Option 4 in the unanimous 7-0 show-of-hands vote.
member_positions.key_quote: We select an option and then that compels the administration to set the timeline through discussion.

member_positions.stance_summary: Verified with staff that custodians brought in-house under Option 4 would subsequently be moved onto the upcoming districtwide classified salary study rates rather than staying permanently behind. Formally moved to adopt Option 4 to transition custodial services in-house.
member_positions.key_quote: I'm going to go ahead and make a motion that we move forward with option four in changing the contract services.

boe_dae_events.event_title: Resolution in Support of Community Schools Initiative in Durham, N.C.
boe_dae_events.issue_category: DAE Advocacy / Recognition / Day of Action
boe_dae_events.dae_position: DAE President Bryan Proffitt and allied educators urged the board to adopt a resolution committing DPS staff to partner with DAE's Community Schools Working Group to launch a shared-leadership pilot at schools where at least 75% of staff voted in favor.

member_positions.stance_summary: Cast the lone dissenting vote against DAE's pilot resolution, questioning why wraparound supports required a separate model in select schools—some of which she characterized as 'Duke neighborhood schools'—rather than universal implementation through existing PLCs. Raised concern about outside control beyond the boardroom and argued strong principal leadership, rather than an externally designed pilot, is what transforms schools.
member_positions.key_quote: I don't understand it, I don't get it unless there's some kind of control that's outside of what happens in this room.

member_positions.stance_summary: Moved the resolution after attending extensive community and educator meetings, expressing readiness to commit DPS staff time immediately. Argued the DAE-championed Community Schools model is a research-backed improvement approach freer from the bureaucratic constraints that limit traditional School Improvement Teams.
member_positions.key_quote: This is an effective model for school improvement in ways that the structure of school improvement teams rarely are because of the constraints that are put on them.

member_positions.stance_summary: Sought to reassure Forte-Brown on equity by emphasizing that excited staff at four to five schools—including high-need Eastway Elementary—were driving the pilot, backed by Dr. Hardy's Baltimore experience. Welcomed the resolution as a framework that brings parents and restorative practices directly to the decision-making table.
member_positions.key_quote: I think community schools gives a framework and a model, so it's no longer one-offs, and it brings so many different people who are not normally at the decision-making table to the table.

member_positions.stance_summary: Emphasized communication and collaboration, noting that educators and organizers had proactively invited him into conversations to explain how the Community Schools initiative worked before the vote. Voted in favor of authorizing the partnership pilot.
member_positions.key_quote: This resolution when I saw it, it didn't seem like it's something new to me because people have come to me and invited me and talked to me and had me talk to people who are doing this.

member_positions.stance_summary: Seconded the resolution and framed support around honoring grassroots educator initiative rather than top-down mandates. Highlighted that school-level staff themselves organized and voted for the model.
member_positions.key_quote: For me again, process, you've got to start with step one and these are schools where this came from the ground up, this came out of the staff and not imposed upon the staff.

member_positions.stance_summary: Presided over the discussion of the resolution and cast an aye vote in the 5-1 passage alongside Beyer, Unruhe, Umstead, and Cason, with Dr. Mike Lee absent for the item.

meetings.title: Durham Public Schools Board of Education Monthly Meeting February 22
meetings.executive_summary: At its February 22, 2018 monthly meeting (video dated 2018-02-23) presided over by Chair Dr. Mike Lee, the Durham Public Schools Board of Education opened with reflections on 18 school violence incidents in 2018 including the Parkland, Florida tragedy, celebrated student performances from Shepherd Middle, Eno Valley Elementary, and Neal Middle, and heard Superintendent Dr. Pascal Mubenga's remarks on Parkland. The board unanimously approved the agenda, corrected January 25 minutes (recording Minnie Forte-Brown's Gold Award), and a consent modification to the 2018-19 year-round school calendar. Principal Nick Ritoski and Southwest Elementary parents presented results from the school's Dual Language Immersion program—noting 61% Latino male proficiency versus 30% districtwide—while raising concerns over the lack of dedicated district funding, H-1B visa legal fees, and licensure equity. The board then unanimously approved proposed special local legislation authorizing DPS to develop affordable rental housing for teachers and local government employees (including long-term nonprofit leases) and, after closed session, unanimously approved the February 22, 2018 personnel report.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Moment of Silence on School Safety, and Celebrations
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Dr. Mike Lee opened with a moment of silence referencing 18 school violence incidents in 2018, the Parkland, Florida shooting, and lockdown drills. Celebrations featured Student of the Month, Lakeview leadership, two new principals, Shepherd Middle poetry, Eno Valley Elementary's musical 'We Call Her Moses,' and Neal Middle School's Black History living museum.

agenda_items.title: Superintendent's Update (Parkland Tragedy)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Superintendent Dr. Pascal Mubenga opened his update by addressing the tragedy at Marjory Stoneman Douglas High School in Parkland, Florida. Additional portions of the mid-meeting update were omitted in the digest.

agenda_items.title: Agenda Approval, Corrected January 25 Minutes, and Year-Round Calendar Consent
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board unanimously approved the agenda as presented and approved the January 25, 2018 minutes as amended to record Minnie Forte-Brown's Gold Award. It then unanimously approved the single consent item modifying the 2018-19 year-round school calendar after confirming family communication plans.

agenda_items.title: Dual Language Immersion Program Update (Southwest Elementary)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Southwest Elementary Principal Nick Ritoski, teachers, and parents presented the 70/30 and 50/50 Spanish-English immersion model, highlighting 61% Latino male proficiency compared to 30% districtwide while noting zero dedicated district funding and difficulties recruiting fifth-grade teachers. Board members discussed statutory H-1B sponsorship legal costs alongside equity concerns for other teachers struggling to pay for licensure.

agenda_items.title: Special Legislation on Teacher and Employee Housing
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff and counsel presented proposed local legislative bill language to submit to the Durham legislative delegation authorizing DPS to construct and provide affordable rental housing prioritized for teachers and other local government employees. After confirming the bill permits long-term ground leases to a nonprofit for grant eligibility, the board approved the proposed legislation unanimously.

agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board voted unanimously to enter closed session for the reasons stated on the agenda. Reconvening at 04:41:08, the board unanimously approved the February 22, 2018 personnel report and adjourned.

boe_dae_events.dae_position: Codifies multi-year 4-year contracts for post-probationary teachers in good standing to strengthen teacher stability and retention.

member_positions.stance_summary: Affirmed the draft policy codifying four-year teacher contracts and cleared it to return for second reading without requiring changes.
member_positions.key_quote: This is a good program; this is the one that extends it—you could do four year contracts, things like that.

boe_dae_events.event_title: Cultural Exchange Teacher Program (J-1 Visas) & Southwest Dual Language Teacher Retention
boe_dae_events.issue_category: DAE Advocacy / Recognition / Day of Action
boe_dae_events.dae_position: DAE President Bryan Proffitt, Southwest educators, and parents urged the Board to find a legal/contractual path to sponsor H-1B visas and retain two J-1 dual-language teachers at Southwest Elementary, framing Southwest as a grassroots community school model.

member_positions.stance_summary: Respected HR's districtwide legal and contract position, yet noted he toured Southwest with DAE and cited DAE President Proffitt calling it a community model. Argued a debt is owed to a school that built a spot of excellence, while worrying about fairness to Holt Elementary and other schools.
member_positions.key_quote: I feel like there is a little bit of a debt to be paid to a school that has created a program by themselves that is a spot of excellence in our district.

member_positions.stance_summary: Pushed back against framing the 14-year-old program as resting solely on two teachers and argued through an equity lens that Southwest has fewer than 100 Hispanic/ELL students and selective lottery access. Insisted the Board cannot create districtwide inequities for one school.
member_positions.key_quote: We have to be responsible in our decisions that we cannot create inequities based on one school.

member_positions.stance_summary: Praised the teachers' passion and the Southwest community, but concluded that breaching the Participate contract and the cultural-exchange spirit of J-1 visas was not the right solution. Urged channeling the energy into expanding dual-language programs across DPS.
member_positions.key_quote: Despite tugging at my heartstrings and wanting to save this in these specific people, that doesn't feel the right solution to me.

member_positions.stance_summary: Focused on legal constraints, asking HR whether the difficulty of obtaining H-1B visas given available U.S. bilingual candidates was an administrative efficiency issue or a statutory legal barrier.
member_positions.key_quote: I did have a question about when you said the availability of qualified candidates would make it tremendously difficult to obtain H1B visas—is that from an efficiency standpoint or from a legal standpoint?

member_positions.stance_summary: Pressed HR to follow up directly with Winston-Salem/Forsyth County Schools' counsel and Participate to ensure every possible legal avenue to keep the teachers was exhausted. Argued $5,000-$10,000 in sponsorship costs would be a 'bargain' compared to the ~$10,000 cost of replacing an experienced teacher.
member_positions.key_quote: And to me, $5,000 or $10,000 is really a bargain if that was possible to keep experienced teachers; we talk about retaining teachers.

member_positions.stance_summary: Asked whether HR had directly requested a mutual waiver from Participate—noting 'it's not breaking a contract if both parties agree'—and verified that recruiting displaced Puerto Rican U.S. citizens avoids future J-1 visa cutoffs.
member_positions.key_quote: It's not breaking a contract if both parties agree—have we reached out to say, hey, look, these are two really, really special teachers, can we work something out?

boe_dae_events.event_title: Special Legislation on Affordable Teacher and Employee Housing (Lowe's Grove)
boe_dae_events.dae_position: Teachers and DPS employees needed affordable local rental housing near schools to support recruitment and retention amid rising Durham housing costs.

member_positions.stance_summary: Asked why the bill title referenced 'other local government employees' rather than 'Durham Public Schools employees,' confirming the bill prioritizes teachers first, then all DPS employees, while remaining flexible for future sites beyond Lowe's Grove.
member_positions.key_quote: Is there a reason we talked about expanding the language to make sure it could apply to teachers and then other employees?

member_positions.stance_summary: Requested a concise list of precedent North Carolina school district housing bills to give the local legislative delegation so the bill could move quickly in both chambers.
member_positions.key_quote: If there are a way to have a very concise list of the reference documents... so they, as they're talking with their colleagues, we can move it a little more quickly.

member_positions.stance_summary: Moved approval of the special legislation request authorizing DPS to construct and provide affordable rental housing for teachers and other local government employees.
member_positions.key_quote: I would like to make a motion that we approve the agenda item entitled special legislation on teacher housing, specifically asking for authorization to construct and provide affordable rental housing for teachers and other local government employees.

member_positions.stance_summary: Asked whether the draft wording precluded transferring the property to a nonprofit partner, confirming that a long-term lease structure permits a nonprofit partner to apply for grants with State Employees' Credit Union support.
member_positions.key_quote: I do have a question that it looks to me like the wording is such that it assumes that we would continue to own the property.

member_positions.stance_summary: Seconded Minnie Forte-Brown's motion and voted aye in the unanimous 7-0 approval of the affordable teacher and employee housing legislation.

Dr. Jill Hall Freeman reported on the Durham Principal Leadership Academy (14 Cohort 1 fellows, with eight already serving as assistant principals), and staff reviewed two shortlisted custodial RFP vendors, healthcare disclosure gaps, and internal monitoring cost estimates ahead of a March 8 recommendation.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Moment of Silence, and Finance Audit Celebration
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The joint Academic and Operational Services work session opened with a moment of silence, followed by CFO Paul LeSieur introducing the finance staff. The board recognized the team for receiving an unmodified clean audit opinion and 26 consecutive years of GFOA and ASBO financial reporting awards.

agenda_items.title: Agenda Review and Approval
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following brief remarks thanking community advocates and the board chair's op-ed, the board moved and Steve Unruhe seconded approval of the agenda. The motion passed unanimously among the six members present.

agenda_items.title: General Public Comment: Community Schools Initiative
agenda_items.discussion_summary: DAE President Bryan Proffitt briefed the board on the Community Schools organizing effort, noting a threshold of 75% school staff buy-in before bringing any school forward and reporting that Club Boulevard Elementary staff voted 94% in favor after workshops. He offered to work with staff and board members on a public resolution of support.

agenda_items.title: Approval of January 11, 2018 Minutes and Consent Agenda (Security Vestibules)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Matt Sears moved and Dr. Mike Lee seconded approval of the January 11 meeting minutes, which passed 6-0. On the consent agenda, a member voiced concern over Item D (Security Vestibules project design, $3 million in the bond), urging data-driven safety decisions rather than acting on fear and noting $3 million could fund a social worker in every school for a year; the consent agenda passed 6-0.

agenda_items.title: Academic & Student Support Services: Pipeline to Leadership (DPLA)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Dr. Jill Hall Freeman presented an update on leadership development, highlighting the Durham Principal Leadership Academy (DPLA) where eight of 14 Cohort 1 fellows had already been placed as assistant principals under three-year service commitments. Staff also outlined the Assistant Principal Academy and plans to space Cohort 2 starting in 2019 to align with principal and AP vacancies.

agenda_items.title: Operational Services: Custodial Program RFP and In-House Analysis
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff narrowed five custodial RFP bids to two vendors (Service Solutions and Premier) while noting 33 full-time and two part-time DPS custodians remained on payroll and flagging Service Solutions' omission of healthcare cost disclosures. Board members requested a survey of all 53 principals (beyond the unanimous high school principals supporting existing contract hours), questioned internal monitor costs (~$46,000 plus benefits each), and asked staff not to hold custodian feedback meetings on the same day as the February 22 board meeting before returning on March 8.

agenda_items.title: Absence Note, Follow-Up Items, and Adjournment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Dr. Stacey Hardy entered a formal note that Natalie Beyer was absent due to a work obligation and summarized follow-up items to survey principals on custodial services and adjust the custodial feedback timeline. The work session then adjourned.

votes.notes: Natalie Beyer was absent due to a work obligation (recorded at 02:09:43).
votes.discussion_detail: Moved and seconded by Steve Unruhe to approve the agenda; passed unanimously among the six members present.

votes.notes: Natalie Beyer absent.
votes.discussion_detail: Matt Sears moved and Dr. Mike Lee seconded approval of the January 11, 2018 meeting minutes; passed unanimously among the six members present.

meetings.title: Durham Public Schools Board of Education Monthly Meeting January 25, 2018 6:30 PM
meetings.executive_summary: At its January 25, 2018 monthly meeting—Superintendent Dr. Pascal Mubenga's first full board meeting and Minnie Forte-Brown's return—Chair Dr. Mike Lee opened with a moment of silence noting 11 school violence incidents already in 2018, and celebrations honored Minnie Forte-Brown with the North Carolina School Boards Association Gold Award and recognized Crayons to Calculators for 10 years of providing free classroom supplies. Dr. Mubenga summarized his initial listening-and-learning tour across schools and three town halls, while Dr. Stacey Hardy introduced the district's collaborative strategic planning framework and spring timeline. Following Board Attorney Ken Soo's guidance under the open meetings law, the board voted unanimously to consolidate its separate Academic Services and Operational Services work sessions into one combined monthly work session on Operational Services Thursdays from February 8 through June 14, while retaining the regular monthly board meeting on the fourth Thursday. After a closed session, the board unanimously approved the January 25, 2018 personnel report before adjourning.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Moment of Silence, and Celebrations
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Dr. Mike Lee welcomed Minnie Forte-Brown back and recognized Dr. Pascal Mubenga's first full board meeting, leading a moment of silence for families affected by 11 school violence incidents in early 2018. Celebrations honored an Early College High School Student of the Month, Minnie Forte-Brown's NCSBA Gold Award for 2016-17 board training, and Crayons to Calculators (Unice Sanders and team) for 10 years of free teacher supplies.

agenda_items.title: Superintendent's Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Dr. Pascal Mubenga reported conducting unannounced school and classroom visits and holding three town halls drawing roughly 120, 220, and over 100 attendees as part of his quantitative and qualitative listening tour ahead of strategic planning.

agenda_items.title: General Public Comment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Six public speakers addressed the board on topics including employee clean-school awards, the statewide K-3 class-size initiative adding 90 teachers, and Club Boulevard Elementary's composting program diverting 600 pounds of cafeteria waste per week from landfills.

agenda_items.title: Agenda Approval and November 16, 2017 Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board unanimously approved the January 25, 2018 meeting agenda as presented. It then unanimously approved the meeting minutes from November 16, 2017.

agenda_items.title: Academic Services: Strategic Planning Process Overview
agenda_items.discussion_summary: At her first board meeting, Dr. Stacey Hardy outlined the strategic planning framework, town hall and virtual survey outreach, and committee schedule to develop shared beliefs, theory of action, vision, mission, and goals between February and April.

agenda_items.title: Consolidation of Monthly Board Work Sessions
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Dr. Mike Lee presented Dr. Mubenga's proposal to combine separate Academic and Operational Services work sessions into a single monthly work session to give staff more preparation time, while preserving the fourth-Thursday regular board meeting. Following Board Attorney Ken Soo's advice to formally amend the regular meeting schedule under open meetings law and confirmation that the April 19 date avoided spring break conflicts, the board unanimously voted to cancel separate Academic Services work sessions and hold combined work sessions from February 8 through June 14.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session and January 25, 2018 Personnel Report
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board voted unanimously to enter closed session for the reasons stated on the agenda. Reconvening at 02:25:08, the board unanimously approved the January 25, 2018 personnel report and adjourned.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Closed session passed 7-0; Personnel report passed 7-0

boe_dae_events.event_title: Custodial Review Committee & Strategic Planning Team (DAE Inclusion and Access Barriers)
boe_dae_events.issue_category: DAE Advocacy / Recognition / Day of Action
boe_dae_events.dae_position: Custodial Review Committee member Deborah Bailey applauded DAE's 'In This Together' campaign and urged fair custodial pay, benefits, sick leave, and coverage plans, while DAE was included among stakeholders on the 50-member Strategic Planning Team.

member_positions.stance_summary: Warned that evening meeting schedules create participation barriers for working families and urged the district to follow PTAs and community groups by providing childcare, food, translation, and central transit access for the Strategic Planning Team.
member_positions.key_quote: This could be a chance for us to sort of model what a new standard could be for these types of meetings.

member_positions.stance_summary: Pushed back on providing dinner and childcare at every strategic planning committee meeting due to cost, noting the district cannot 'go in the hole' and urging community coalitions to funnel priorities through representatives and the online survey.
member_positions.key_quote: It's gonna be too costly for us to provide childcare and all that kind of stuff for everybody every time we meet.

boe_dae_events.event_title: 2018-2019 Multi-Year Teacher Contracts Proposal (4-Year Contracts, EVAAS Removal & DAE Consultation)
boe_dae_events.dae_position: DAE supported moving eligible post-probationary teachers from annual 1-year contracts to 4-year contracts and removing EVAAS test-score data from contract eligibility; HR reported DAE was 'very pleased' with the proposal.

member_positions.stance_summary: Asked whether DPS could offer four-year contracts immediately to recruit experienced teachers away from Wake County, though board counsel noted state statute requires three consecutive years in the hiring district.
member_positions.key_quote: I'm looking for a way to lure teachers from area districts—if someone has done well in another county, are we able to offer a four-year?

member_positions.stance_summary: Thanked HR for streamlining the multi-year contract proposal, argued that teachers who receive a one-year coaching contract rather than four years should not be stigmatized, and praised the plan for meeting teachers' desire for stability and fairness.
member_positions.key_quote: And I think it meets the desires of teachers for stability and it's clear, it's fair.

member_positions.stance_summary: Commended HR for presenting a clear multi-year contract structure that directly advances the Board's longstanding priority to retain teachers.
member_positions.key_quote: I'm also appreciative of the professionalism that you brought tonight and the way you've presented something so clearly that will help us retain teachers.

member_positions.stance_summary: Shared that he left his prior university career because of perpetual one-year contracts and strongly celebrated HR's decision to drop EVAAS test scores from multi-year teacher contract eligibility.
member_positions.key_quote: EVAAS does not really show all that is done in that relationship between the teacher and the student.

member_positions.stance_summary: Praised the policy while warning that HR historically struggled to communicate protections like Policy 5430 due process to teachers, and explicitly called on DAE to play a stronger role in educating all 2,500 teachers on their contract rights.
member_positions.key_quote: So I personally would like to see DAE take a stronger role in educating the body that is our 2,500 teachers.

member_positions.stance_summary: Expressed strong enthusiasm for four-year contracts as a crucial retention tool to relieve teachers of annual end-of-year anxiety over whether they will be renewed.
member_positions.key_quote: Every summer, when we start to get close to the summer, teachers are, are we going to be renewed or non-renewed?

member_positions.stance_summary: Thanked HR for revising the proposal to be clear and confirmed that current teachers could begin receiving four-year contracts starting July 1, 2018.
member_positions.key_quote: So does that mean we could have some four year contracts being awarded in July?
