meetings.title: Durham Public Schools BOE Operational Services & Policy Work Session January 11, 2018 4:30 PM
meetings.executive_summary: Chair Dr. Mike Lee presided over the January 11, 2018 combined Operational Services and Policy Work Session of the Durham Public Schools Board of Education with all seven board members participating. Following public comments from Forestview Elementary parents and Principal Neil Clay detailing severe overcrowding, the board voted unanimously (7-0) to authorize staff to proceed with design and planning for an enclosed six-classroom modular complex at Forestview (projected at roughly $800,000) and also unanimously approved (7-0) a coaching contract with Education Resource Group (ERG) for 100 beginning teachers across 17 state-designated low-performing schools, Change Order #3 closing out a 14-school summer lighting project, consent items, minutes, and the post-closed-session personnel report. Board members held an extended policy debate over proposed 2018-2019 multi-year teacher contract criteria—specifically Minnie Forte-Brown's support for data-driven accountability versus Xavier Cason, Steve Unruhe, and Natalie Beyer's skepticism toward SAS EVAAS student-growth scores and Matt Sears's request to recover the district's 2015 due-process policy (later located as Policy 5430)—resulting in an informal consensus deferral to the next board meeting for policy review and consultation with the Durham Association of Educators. District staff also presented House Bill 13 K-3 class-size reduction impacts showing reduced magnet seats, a need for 81 additional classrooms with only six available district-wide, and roughly $10 million in preliminary FY 2018-2019 budget pressures driven by K-3 staffing, charter school transfers, benefit hikes, and the city's elimination of five school resource officers.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Moment of Silence, and Announcements
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Dr. Mike Lee opened the combined Operational Services and Policy work session, led a moment of silence, and noted the full audience in attendance. Chair Lee also promoted the updated district website and upcoming town hall meetings hosted by Superintendent Dr. Pascal Mubenga at Hillside High School (January 16), Northern High School (January 23), and Jordan High School (January 27).

agenda_items.title: Agenda Review and Approval
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Board and staff adjusted the agenda by moving Item 8a (Forestview Elementary School modular building) up to Item 6.1 as an open discussion/action item for attendees in the audience, and moving Item 8d (quarterly Construction and Capital Planning Change Order Report) onto the consent agenda as Item 6b. The amended agenda was moved, seconded, and approved unanimously by voice vote.

agenda_items.title: Approval of December 7 and December 14, 2017 Work Session Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board reviewed the minutes from its December 7, 2017 and December 14, 2017 work sessions. Following a motion and second with no questions or corrections raised, the minutes passed unanimously by voice vote.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Policy 6200 Series Second Reading and Construction Change Order Report)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: After noting no general public speakers had signed up yet (and agreeing to pause around 5:00 p.m. for latecomers), the board took up the consent agenda consisting of the School Nutrition Service Policy 6200 series on second reading and the Construction and Capital Planning Change Order Report moved from Item 8d to 6b. The board unanimously approved all consent items by voice vote, then welcomed Dr. Hardy to the district and thanked Dr. Pittman for serving as interim.

agenda_items.title: Item 6.1: Forestview Elementary School Modular Building Complex
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Forestview PTA President Dina Nablok, Principal Neil Clay, and parent Elizabeth Snyder testified about severe overcrowding at Forestview Elementary—where instruction occurs in hallways, a partitioned media center, a divided art/science room, and a converted teacher workroom/lounge, and a staff bathroom was converted for kindergarteners while protecting space for 240 ESL students. Presenting in place of John Long, staff requested authorization to proceed with design and planning (~$80,000) for an enclosed six-classroom modular building (~$800,000 projected total, or ~$700,000 if a stormwater pond is waived) on an aggressive eight-month timeline before school opens. Xavier Cason moved to authorize staff to continue with the design and planning of the Forestview modular complex, which passed unanimously.

agenda_items.title: Item 7a: Impact of House Bill 13 (K-3 Class Size Mandate) on Magnet Programs
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Director of Student Assignment Donna Hudson and Magnet Program Administrator Mary Griffith briefed the board on how House Bill 13 K-3 class-size reductions affect the 2018-2019 magnet application window (open January 8–31), reducing available magnet seats and shifting unassigned students back to base schools. Board members Steve Unruhe, Natalie Beyer, and Minnie Forte-Brown questioned waitlist adjustments if the state reverses the mandate, limited statutory waivers, and how charter school exemptions exacerbate enrollment pressures on traditional public schools.

agenda_items.title: Academic Services: New Teacher Support Contract with Education Resource Group (ERG)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Dr. Jill Fall and Dr. Dietrich Tanner proposed contracting with Education Resource Group (ERG) to provide eight intensive coaching visits each from February through May for 100 beginning teachers in tested areas across 17 of the district's 18 state-designated low-performing schools, complementing the district's 12 full-release mentors who serve 593 beginning teachers (funded 85% via Title I federal funds and $22,500 in local funds). Board members questioned why university-based state support was not chosen, pressed for mid-course evaluation and equity/restorative-practice alignment with Dr. Bullock, criticized handwritten internal contract forms and excluding non-tested beginning teachers, and requested future competitor vetting before unanimously approving the ERG contract.

agenda_items.title: Additional General Public Comment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Pausing for additional public comment, the board heard through a Spanish interpreter from parent Jacqueline, who praised her son's middle school math teacher for strong parent communication and academic support. She encouraged the district to use effective communicators as models to train other teachers.

agenda_items.title: Item 8a: Teacher Contracts for 2018-2019
agenda_items.discussion_summary: HR staff (Ms. Hagar and Arasi Adkins) presented proposed eligibility criteria under state law allowing one-, two-, rolling two-, and four-year contracts for non-career teachers with three or more years in DPS, proposing NCEES ratings and EVAAS student-growth benchmarks for four-year contracts. Minnie Forte-Brown backed holding teachers accountable with data, while Xavier Cason, Steve Unruhe, and Natalie Beyer objected to elevating EVAAS growth data, Bettina Umstead asked about new principals inheriting multi-year contracts, and Matt Sears asked staff to locate a missing 2015 local due-process/career-status policy; by consensus, the board tabled action to the next board meeting so staff could investigate the policy and consult Durham Association of Educators (DAE) leadership.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Deferred / No formal vote (agreed to bring to next board meeting)

agenda_items.title: FY 2018-2019 Budget Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Finance staff outlined roughly $10 million in preliminary FY 2018-2019 budget needs ahead of county budget submission and the General Assembly's May short session, including $6 million for ~90 K-3 class-size positions, nearly $2.2 million for projected 3% certified/1.5% classified raises, supplement matching, retirement rate increases (17.13% to 18.44%), and hospital insurance hikes ($5,869 to $6,104), a net ~$1.25 million enrollment shift (a $781,000 DPS ADM drop offset by over $2 million transferred for +600 charter students), and $300,000 to replace five city-funded School Resource Officers (SROs). Board members scrutinized county per-pupil funding formulas and urged city leadership discussions regarding restoring SRO or equity officer funding and reframing budget language around small schools.

agenda_items.title: K-3 Class Size Project Team Update and District Elementary Space Impact
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Julie Spencer and Mr. Bouier reported on the cross-departmental K-3 project team's guidance covering co-teaching, multi-age combination classes, floating classrooms, transfer appeals, and un-mothballing existing mobile units, while presenting a school-by-school capacity chart showing a projected shortfall of 81 classrooms (including nine classrooms at Eno Valley needed for phased renovations) and only six vacant classrooms district-wide while protecting 41 pre-K rooms. Officials discussed inevitable redistricting, potentially restoring two elementary school projects removed from the bond package (Elementary C and 751), and Minnie Forte-Brown requested a parent advocacy script to urge state legislators to fix the mandate.

agenda_items.title: Lighting Upgrades Installation Change Order #3
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Brian Callaway, filling in for John Long, presented closeout Change Order #3 for the 14-school summer LED lighting upgrade project—completed ahead of the school year to maximize Duke Energy rebates—covering final contract adjustments and unexpected construction issues encountered at Rogers-Herr Middle School. Board members praised the completed lighting upgrades and approved Change Order #3 unanimously by voice vote.

agenda_items.title: Follow-Up Items, Closed Session, Personnel Report, and Assistant Principal Introductions
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff reported finding the board's April and August 2015 due-process revisions in Policy 5430 and sharing them with Ms. Adkins, and thanked attending Durham Principal Leadership Academy interns. After voting unanimously to enter closed session, the board reconvened to unanimously approve the January 11 personnel report and heard introductions from six newly appointed assistant principals (with coordinator Dr. Pat Ashley) before Chair Lee adjourned the meeting at 02:43:04.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Closed session passed 7-0; Personnel report passed 7-0

votes.discussion_detail: Approved the amended agenda moving Item 8a (Forestview Elementary School modular building) up to Item 6.1 and moving Item 8d (Construction and Capital Planning Change Order Report) onto the consent agenda as Item 6b.

votes.discussion_detail: Approved the minutes from the December 7, 2017 and December 14, 2017 board work sessions without discussion.

votes.notes: Unanimous voice vote; mover and seconder not named in transcript.
votes.discussion_detail: Approved the School Nutrition Service Policy 6200 series on second reading and the quarterly Construction and Capital Planning Change Order Report (Item 6b).

votes.notes: Moved by Xavier Cason at 00:29:06; passed unanimously by voice vote.
votes.discussion_detail: Authorized district staff to continue with design and planning (~$80,000 initial planning cost; ~$800,000 projected total) for an enclosed six-classroom modular complex at overcrowded Forestview Elementary School, with final budget and costs to return to the board.

votes.notes: Unanimous voice vote; board members emphasized monitoring vendor effectiveness and aligning coaches with district equity practices.
votes.discussion_detail: Approved the contract with Education Resource Group (ERG) to deliver eight job-embedded coaching visits per teacher for 100 beginning teachers in tested subjects across 17 of 18 state-designated low-performing schools from February through May, funded 85% with Title I federal funds and $22,500 in local funds.

votes.discussion_detail: Approved closeout Change Order #3 for the 14-school summer lighting upgrade project maximizing Duke Energy rebates, including unexpected construction work at Rogers-Herr Middle School.

disagreements.meeting_title: Durham Public Schools BOE Operational Services & Policy Work Session January 11, 2018 4:30 PM
disagreements.issue: Use of EVAAS Growth Data and Local Due Process Policy in 2018-2019 Multi-Year Teacher Contracts
disagreements.summary: Board members disagreed over relying on SAS EVAAS student-growth metrics to determine teacher eligibility for four-year contracts under new state rules, and over whether the proposal accounted for DPS's 2015 local due-process/career-status policy before taking action.
disagreements.side_a_position: Multi-year teacher contract eligibility should rely on clear performance data, including EVAAS and evaluation ratings, to hold educators accountable for student progress.
side_a_arguments: Minnie Forte-Brown argued the board should not shy away from evaluation and that 'the data must be the driver' in holding adults accountable because students only get one year in a grade.
HR staff noted that principals had reviewed the criteria in December and recommended straightforward data benchmarks using NCEES standards and EVAAS growth.
disagreements.side_b_position: EVAAS student-growth scores are an unreliable single-year metric for contract length, and action should be deferred to verify DPS's 2015 due-process policy and consult DAE.
side_b_arguments: Xavier Cason questioned elevating SAS EVAAS growth figures designed for cohorts rather than individual teachers, noting national research favors at least three-year trends and districts like Houston abandoned EVAAS.

Natalie Beyer and Steve Unruhe expressed strong misgivings about relying on flawed EVAAS data, with Steve Unruhe requesting a fall review if implemented and Matt Sears pointing to missing 2015 due-process policy language and urging consultation with DAE before voting.
disagreements.resolution: No formal vote was taken; by consensus following Matt Sears's request, the board tabled the item to its next meeting so staff could locate the 2015 due-process policy (found later in the meeting as April/August 2015 revisions to Policy 5430) and meet with DAE leadership.

meetings.title: Durham Public Schools BOE Operational Services & Policy Work Session December 14, 2017 4:30 PM
meetings.executive_summary: At its December 14, 2017 Operational Services & Policy Work Session (presided over by committee chair Matt Sears, with Board Chair Dr. Mike Lee participating and offering several motions and Minnie Forte-Brown participating by phone), the Durham Public Schools Board of Education heard from Superintendent Dr. Pascal Mubenga regarding financial and staffing constraints under the state Restart program and unanimously directed the administration to draft a letter to the State Board of Education/NCDPI requesting a reduction from 14 approved restart schools to a smaller subset. The board unanimously adopted a joint BOCC-BOE resolution urging the General Assembly to phase in K-3 class-size reductions under SL 2017-9, fund enhancement teachers, and pass House Bill 866; approved a month-to-month custodial contract extension with SSC Service Solutions through May 31, 2018 while an internal/stakeholder committee evaluates in-house vs. contracted options; and accepted the 2016-17 Comprehensive Annual Financial Report audit showing an unmodified opinion, $9.4 million in general fund balance, and $141 million in net pension liability. The board also reviewed the Central Services Salary Study, unanimously approved a three-year Mark III voluntary benefits brokerage renewal, unanimously approved a memorandum to Durham County Commissioners requesting conveyance of ~5.6 acres behind old Lowe's Grove School for CASA affordable teacher housing, and unanimously approved the Case 21 mid-year and end-of-year benchmark assessment contract after members voiced concerns about instructional time and requested a spring assessment audit. No split votes occurred; following closed session, four remaining members unanimously approved the December 14, 2017 personnel report.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order and Moment of Silence
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Committee Chair Matt Sears welcomed attendees (including Minnie Forte-Brown on the phone), called the December 14, 2017 Operational Services and Policy Work Session to order, and led a moment of silence.

agenda_items.title: Agenda Review and Approval (Three Additions)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board added three time-sensitive items to the agenda: Item 6.5 for a Restart program update from Superintendent Dr. Pascal Mubenga, Item 8E for the teacher housing project, and Item 8F for the Case 21 benchmark contract. Dr. Mike Lee moved and Natalie Beyer seconded approving the amended agenda, passing unanimously.

agenda_items.title: Meeting Minutes Note and General Public Comment on Student Wellness
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff noted that the October 12 work session minutes had already been brought to the November 16 board meeting. During general public comment, School Health Advisory Council (SHAC) member Amanda Snyderman praised Wellness Policy 3021 and urged the board to reinstate a dedicated full-time Wellness Coordinator position in future strategic and budget planning.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda
agenda_items.discussion_summary: With no items pulled for separate discussion, Bettina Umstead moved and Natalie Beyer seconded approval of Item 6 consent agenda items, which passed unanimously by voice vote.

agenda_items.title: Restart Program Update and Reduction Request Letter
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Dr. Pascal Mubenga reported that implementing the Restart model across all 14 approved schools simultaneously posed severe financial and operational challenges given limited fiscal flexibility. Board members questioned the criteria for selecting the subset of schools and noted concern over messaging to the state while acknowledging K-3 class size fiscal pressures; Dr. Mike Lee moved and Xavier Cason seconded instructing the administration (with Dr. Lee editing) to submit a letter to the State Board of Education/NCDPI requesting a reduction in the number of restart schools, passing unanimously.

agenda_items.title: Joint BOCC-BOE Resolution on K-3 Class Size Reduction Implementation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Natalie Beyer introduced and read the joint resolution adopted December 11 by the Durham County Commissioners based on an NCSBA draft, documenting that SL 2017-9 would force DPS to add 63 classrooms and hire 90 additional teachers amid $399 million in unmet capital needs while threatening art, music, and PE rooms and Pre-K capacity. The resolution urged the General Assembly to enact a multi-year phase-in, fully fund enhancement teachers, and approve House Bill 866; Dr. Mike Lee moved and Steve Unruhe seconded adoption, passing unanimously.

agenda_items.title: Custodial Contract Extension (SSC Service Solutions)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: During public comment, Brian Callaway criticized the spring consultant study's comparison of full-time in-house models against part-time outsourced labor and urged bringing custodial services in-house. Staff reported that RFP bids were received the prior week and requested a month-to-month extension with SSC Service Solutions at current rates through May 31, 2018 while an internal and stakeholder committee evaluates in-house vs. outsourced options for the 2018-19 budget; Steve Unruhe moved and Natalie Beyer seconded, passing unanimously.

agenda_items.title: 2016-17 Comprehensive Annual Financial Report (CAFR) Audit
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Auditor Evan Reeves of Reeves & Associates presented an unmodified opinion on DPS's 2016-17 financial statements and federal/state program compliance, noting GFOA and ASBO financial reporting awards. He reported a $9.4 million general fund balance (plus $6 million in other local special revenue funds, largely rebuilt through lapsed salaries), $141 million in net pension liability, ~76% of total expenditures on salaries and benefits, ~$20 million in charter school payments, and a Child Nutrition fund turnaround; Dr. Mike Lee moved and Natalie Beyer seconded approval, passing unanimously.

agenda_items.title: Central Services Salary Study Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Scott Denton, Kim Hager, and equity director Dr. Kelvin Bullock updated the board on matching central services and classified positions to state salary grades and relative values, auditing experience steps, and building schedules from DPS's $13.15/hour entry floor toward a $15/hour living wage. Board members asked how applicants will view transparent salary schedules online and urged reviewing Policy 5265 (Living Wage) alongside the study before budget recommendations return.

agenda_items.title: Mark III Voluntary Employee Benefits Contract Renewal
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Freddie McNeil presented a three-year renewal (January 1, 2018 through December 31, 2020) with Mark III for voluntary employee benefits brokerage (dental, vision, disability, cancer, life, and FSA) at no direct cost to the district, supplemented by a 24-hour financial wellness helpline. Board members asked about total employee paycheck pass-through volume and emphasized clearly communicating that voluntary plans are private insurance products; Natalie Beyer moved and Dr. Mike Lee seconded approval, passing unanimously.

agenda_items.title: Affordable Teacher Housing Project Memorandum to Durham County Commissioners
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Attorney Melissa Michoud (Tharrington Smith) and CASA CFO Debbie White presented a draft memorandum for the County Commissioners' January 2, 2018 agenda requesting that the county accept ~5.6 acres behind the old Lowe's Grove School with a reverter deed restriction, contract to convey or long-term lease it to CASA for 24 Phase 1 units (up to 72 units / 100 teachers total), and amend the property's development agreement. Members discussed 80% AMI moderate-income eligibility limits versus seeking special legislation and deed safeguards limiting occupancy to DPS employees; Dr. Mike Lee moved and Steve Unruhe seconded approval, passing unanimously.

agenda_items.title: Case 21 Benchmark Assessment Contract
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Dr. Deborah Pittman and Dr. Pascal Mubenga requested approval of a Case 21 contract requiring district-wide mid-year (January) and end-of-year (April) benchmark assessments aligned to state EOGs and EOCs. Board members expressed concerns about testing fatigue, lost instructional time, and overlap with i-Ready and mCLASS, but supported Dr. Mubenga's request on condition of a comprehensive spring assessment review; Dr. Mike Lee moved and Bettina Umstead seconded approval, passing unanimously.

agenda_items.title: Follow-Up Items, Timeline Update, Closed Session, and Personnel Report
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff summarized follow-up items on restart selection criteria and building a healthier fund balance without relying on lapsed salaries, after which Dr. Mike Lee moved and Natalie Beyer seconded entering closed session to discuss agenda items and legal ramifications of the restart program. Returning to open session at 02:31:15 with four members present, the board unanimously approved the December 14, 2017 personnel report and adjourned.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Closed session passed unanimously; Personnel report passed 4-0

votes.notes: Voice vote with no opposition; Minnie Forte-Brown participated by phone (seventh member noted connecting at 00:28:38).
votes.discussion_detail: Moved by Dr. Mike Lee and seconded by Natalie Beyer to approve the agenda with three additions: 6.5 (Restart update), 8E (teacher housing project), and 8F (Case 21 contract).

votes.item_title: Direction to Submit Letter Requesting Reduction in Restart Schools
votes.notes: Passed unanimously by voice vote after board discussion of fiscal constraints and an accepted friendly amendment regarding continued deep work in remaining schools.
votes.discussion_detail: Dr. Mike Lee moved and Xavier Cason seconded instructing the administration to craft a letter to NCDPI / State Board of Education requesting a reduction in the number of DPS Restart schools (to a number determined by administration, with the letter edited by Dr. Mubenga and Dr. Lee).

votes.item_title: Adoption of Joint BOCC-BOE Resolution on K-3 Class Size Reduction Implementation
votes.notes: Passed unanimously after seventh member reconnected at 00:28:38.
votes.discussion_detail: Moved by Dr. Mike Lee and seconded by Steve Unruhe to adopt the joint resolution with the Durham County Board of Commissioners urging General Assembly action on SL 2017-9 K-3 class sizes, enhancement teacher funding, and HB 866.

votes.item_title: Custodial Contract Extension with SSC Service Solutions Through May 31, 2018
votes.notes: Passed unanimously by voice vote.
votes.discussion_detail: Moved by Steve Unruhe and seconded by Natalie Beyer to approve a month-to-month extension of the SSC Service Solutions custodial contract at current rates through May 31, 2018 while RFP bids and an in-house option are evaluated.

votes.item_title: Approval of 2016-17 Comprehensive Annual Financial Report (CAFR) Audit
votes.notes: Passed unanimously by voice vote.
votes.discussion_detail: Moved by Dr. Mike Lee and seconded by Natalie Beyer to approve the 2016-17 CAFR audit presented by Reeves & Associates.

votes.item_title: Approval of Mark III Employee Benefits Contract Renewal (2018-2020)
votes.notes: Passed unanimously by voice vote.
votes.discussion_detail: Moved by Natalie Beyer (ASR: 'Spire') and seconded by Dr. Mike Lee to approve the three-year Mark III voluntary benefits brokerage renewal from January 1, 2018 through December 31, 2020.

votes.item_title: Approval of Draft Memorandum to Durham County Commissioners on Affordable Teacher Housing
votes.notes: Passed unanimously by voice vote.
votes.discussion_detail: Moved by Dr. Mike Lee and seconded by Steve Unruhe to approve the draft memorandum requesting Durham County Commissioners consider accepting the ~5.6-acre Lowe's Grove parcel with a reverter clause, partnering with CASA for teacher housing, and amending the development agreement at their January 2, 2018 meeting.

votes.item_title: Approval of Case 21 Benchmark Assessment Contract
votes.notes: Passed unanimously by voice vote despite members voicing reluctance over total testing load.
votes.discussion_detail: Moved by Dr. Mike Lee and seconded by Bettina Umstead to approve the Case 21 contract for required mid-year and end-of-year benchmark assessments; a proposed friendly amendment regarding EOG inclusion was not accepted, while staff committed to returning with correlation data and a broader assessment review.

votes.item_title: Motion to Enter Closed Session
votes.notes: Passed unanimously by voice vote.
votes.discussion_detail: Moved by Dr. Mike Lee and seconded by Natalie Beyer to enter closed session for the reasons stated on the agenda, including legal ramifications of the Restart program.

votes.item_title: Approval of December 14, 2017 Personnel Report
votes.notes: Passed unanimously with four members remaining ('We have four here' at 02:31:33); individual names of the four remaining members and mover/seconder were not stated on the record.
votes.discussion_detail: Following closed session, Dr. Pascal Mubenga presented the December 14, 2017 personnel report for approval.

meetings.title: Durham Public Schools BOE Academic & Student Services Work Session December 7, 2017 4:30 PM
meetings.executive_summary: At its December 7, 2017 Academic and Student Services Work Session (presided over by Dr. Mike Lee filling in for usual committee chair Bettina Umstead, with Minnie Forte-Brown participating by phone), the Durham Public Schools Board of Education unanimously approved reordering the agenda to place School Improvement Plans after reports, approved the November 2 minutes, and met in closed session to review school safety components of School Improvement Plans under NCGS 115C-105.27 and 143-318.11(a)(8). In open session, the board unanimously adopted the 2018-19 traditional calendar (Draft B as amended) and year-round calendar (Draft 2), unanimously approved the K-3 class-size enhancement waiver request while condemning the unfunded state mandate and noting the County Commissioners' upcoming support resolution, and received an update on Pre-K expansion and 111 students enrolled at Whitted. The board also unanimously approved the 2017-18 School Improvement Plans in two motions—first for low-performing ('Destination Success') schools and then for all district schools—heard public comment with Spanish interpretation, and following a second closed session unanimously approved the amended December 7 personnel report. No split votes occurred.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Moment of Silence, and Agenda Review and Approval
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Board Chair Dr. Mike Lee opened the meeting in place of regular committee chair Bettina Umstead and observed a moment of silence. At Steve Unruhe's request, the board amended the agenda to move Item 1 (School Improvement Plans) below Item 5 while keeping the closed session on school safety components ahead of reports; the amended agenda passed unanimously by voice vote.

agenda_items.title: Public Comment Check and Approval of November 2, 2017 Work Session Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: No speakers had signed up for initial public comment, though the chair noted the board would check again later in the meeting. The board unanimously approved the November 2, 2017 work session minutes, with Minnie Forte-Brown unmuting her phone to confirm her affirmative vote.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session: School Safety Components of School Improvement Plans
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board voted unanimously to enter closed session under NCGS 115C-105.27 and 143-318.11(a)(8) to review the school safety components of the 2017-18 School Improvement Plans, returning to open session at 00:19:54.

agenda_items.title: 2018-2019 Traditional and Year-Round School Calendars
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Dr. Deborah Pittman and Dr. Kendra O'Neill presented the 2018-19 calendar drafts reflecting stakeholder voting, highlighting a revised workday/holiday arrangement between semesters on Traditional Draft B and later intercession timing on Year-Round Draft 2. The board unanimously approved Traditional Draft B as amended and Year-Round Draft 2.

agenda_items.title: K-3 Class Size Enhancement Waiver Request
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Dr. Julie Spencer presented the K-3 class-size enhancement waiver request so schools could maintain art, music, and PE specials while remaining in compliance. Board members criticized the unfunded state mandate, noted Durham's AAA bond capacity and county support relative to smaller districts, acknowledged Minnie Forte-Brown's NCSBA resolution, and previewed a joint County Commissioners resolution ahead of a unanimous vote to approve the waiver.

agenda_items.title: Pre-K Program Expansion and Whitted School Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Melissa Watson, Suzanne Cotterman, and Karen Thompson updated the board on countywide Pre-K stakeholder focus groups, job descriptions for a county point person, classroom startup and bathroom/facility upgrade costs amid K-3 space constraints, and Whitted's enrollment of 111 students (including 27 Exceptional Children students). Board members reaffirmed support for expanding Pre-K and expressed hope the county would pursue its penny property tax dedicated to early childhood.

agenda_items.title: 2017-18 School Improvement Plans (Destination Success & District-Wide Approval)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff reviewed school improvement plans in the NCStar platform, progress monitoring, and alignment with Restart/low-performing supports, noting that under state law even schools meeting growth remain designated low-performing unless they exceed growth with a grade above D/F. In two separate unanimous votes at 01:10:22 and 01:10:44, the board approved the 2017-18 School Improvement Plans for low-performing ('Destination Success') schools per NCGS 115C-105.37 and then approved all district School Improvement Plans.

agenda_items.title: Late Public Comment (With Spanish Interpretation)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Consistent with board practice, the chair opened a late public comment window and provided six minutes with Spanish translation for community speakers petitioning the board regarding school community trust and leadership/staffing considerations.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session and Amended Personnel Report
agenda_items.discussion_summary: At 01:18:21, the board voted unanimously to enter closed session for the reasons stated on the agenda. Returning to open session at 01:42:59, the board unanimously approved the amended December 7, 2017 personnel report and adjourned.

meetings.title: Durham Public Schools Board of Education Monthly Meeting November 16, 2017 6:30 PM
meetings.executive_summary: At its November 16, 2017 regular monthly meeting (presided over by Chair Dr. Mike Lee, with Minnie Forte-Brown participating by phone), the Durham Public Schools Board of Education celebrated October Student of the Month Grace Brielle Avery and congratulated Minnie Forte-Brown on her November 15 installation as President of the North Carolina School Boards Association. During public comment, speakers raised concerns about controlled medication safety protocols at Hillandale Elementary and advocated for funding four full-time community school coordinator positions. The board unanimously approved its agenda, the October 12 and October 26 minutes, and Consent Item Policy 3300 (School Calendar and Time for Learning, second reading), and then heard Operational Services reports on House Bill 13 K-3 class-size mandates (~90 additional teachers costing ~$6 million and ~63-65 classrooms for 2018-19), a comprehensive custodial program review detailing pay and benefit disparities for 294 contracted vs. 35 DPS custodians alongside a new stakeholder committee, and magnet versus traditional bus transportation data (~$3 million magnet routing cost across 241 buses). Following a closed session, the board unanimously approved the November 16, 2017 revised personnel report; no split votes occurred.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order and Moment of Silence
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Dr. Mike Lee convened the November 16, 2017 regular monthly meeting, noted that Minnie Forte-Brown would join by phone, and led a moment of silence.

agenda_items.title: Celebrations and Superintendent's Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Principal Marcia Navarro introduced Middle College High School senior Grace Brielle Avery as October Student of the Month, alongside recognitions for Hillside High School and interim academic leadership. Interim Superintendent Aaron Beaulieu then congratulated board member Minnie Forte-Brown on her November 15 installation as President of the North Carolina School Boards Association.

agenda_items.title: General Public Comment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Six speakers addressed the board, including parent Kimberly Harris regarding controlled student medication handling and safety at Hillandale Elementary, and parents and organizers urging DPS to commit to the Community School model with full-time site coordinators and shared leadership teams.

agenda_items.title: Agenda Approval, October Minutes, and Consent Agenda (Policy 3300)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board unanimously approved the meeting agenda as printed, approved the October 12 and October 26, 2017 board meeting minutes, and adopted Consent Item Policy 3300 (School Calendar and Time for Learning) on second reading.

agenda_items.title: Operational Services: HB 13 K-3 Class Size Mandate Budget and Staffing Impact
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following public comment from Nicholas Graber-Grace urging protection of four community school coordinator positions amid impending budget cuts, finance officer Aaron LeSueur presented 2018-19 House Bill 13 K-3 requirements (1:18 K, 1:16 1st, 1:17 2nd-3rd district averages), projecting roughly 90 additional teachers (~$6 million in salaries/benefits) and 63-65 classrooms. Board members criticized the unfunded state mandate as impossible without harming Pre-K or upper grades and called for General Assembly action in January.

agenda_items.title: Operational Services: Custodial Program Review and Stakeholder Committee
agenda_items.discussion_summary: DAE President Bryan Proffitt noted the recent murder of a DPS student and raised reports of contractor supervisor intimidation against custodians who spoke at the October meeting, while Brian Calloway critiqued outsourcing savings and the RFP's base bid removing living-wage requirements. Staff presented data comparing 329 total custodial workers (236 Service Solutions, 58 Premier, 35 DPS), showing $8.75/hour average part-time contractor pay, no sick or holiday pay, and a ~300-hour daily staffing gap; board members criticized prior delays while welcoming a diverse stakeholder committee with DAE and custodians to inform the FY 2018-19 budget.

agenda_items.title: Operational Services: Transportation Data Review (Traditional vs. Magnet Schools)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Scott Denton and Joe Harris presented transportation metrics covering 241 buses running ~600 routes (19 fewer buses than the prior year due to driver shortages and double runs), earliest pickups at 5:45 AM, ~$3 million in magnet transportation costs (~$1 million-$2.5 million local budget impact), and an expected rebound in state efficiency ratings into the 90s.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session and Revised Personnel Report
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board unanimously entered closed session at 01:55:15 for the reasons stated on the agenda. Returning to open session at 02:44:29, the board unanimously approved the November 16, 2017 revised personnel report and adjourned.

meetings.executive_summary: At its October 26, 2017 regular monthly meeting (presided over by Chair Dr. Mike Lee, with Minnie Forte-Brown participating by phone from Atlanta), the Durham Public Schools Board of Education celebrated September's Student of the Month and Northern High School's culinary program for Be Our Guest, heard Interim Superintendent Aaron Beaulieu's update welcoming incoming Superintendent Dr. Pascal Mubenga and noting the Neal Middle School mayoral forum, and heard public comment from local barber Dwight Chandler regarding parent communication and academic accountability. In Operational Services, Dr. Julie Spencer, Kim Hager, and Paul LeSueur presented a comprehensive update on House Bill 13 K-3 class-size compliance, detailing how strict caps (23 maximum per class and 1:20 average moving to lower ratios in 2018-19) forced classroom conversions of science and computer labs and threatened enhancement positions like art, music, and PE. meetings.title: Durham Public Schools BOE Superintendent Announcement
meetings.executive_summary: At a special-called meeting on October 16, 2017 (presided over by Chair Dr. Mike Lee, with Minnie Forte-Brown noted absent while traveling in Atlanta), the Durham Public Schools Board of Education unanimously approved the agenda (6-0) and met in a brief closed session under NCGS 143-318.11(a)(6) and 115C-319 to finalize confidential personnel matters. Returning to open session, the board voted unanimously (6-0) to appoint Franklin County Schools Superintendent Dr. Pascal Mubenga—a former Chewning Middle School math teacher and NCDPI transformation leader—as the next Superintendent of Durham Public Schools. Chair Dr. Mike Lee highlighted recent district momentum, including 78% of DPS schools meeting or exceeding growth and defeating the state takeover attempt, while Dr. Mubenga outlined his upcoming 90-day listening tour and strategic plan and introduced his wife Chantal, daughters Sarah and Angela, a family friend, and his pastor Dr. Carmichael. No split votes occurred.

meetings.title: Durham Public Schools BOE Operational Services & Policy Work Session October 12, 2017 4:30 PM
meetings.executive_summary: At its October 12, 2017 Operational Services & Policy Work Session (presided over by committee chair Matt Sears), the Durham Public Schools Board of Education unanimously approved an amended agenda, the September 14 minutes, and seven consent items (including Burton and Hope Valley chiller bids, 2007 bond closures, and eight new activity buses), and heard a superintendent search announcement previewing the October 16 appointment meeting. Custodians, teachers, and Don't Waste Durham speakers urged bringing custodial services in-house ahead of the newly posted custodial RFP (which sought dual living-wage and base bids with a March 8 recommendation target). The board unanimously waived first reading to approve Policy 4131.2 linking R.N. Harris, Club Boulevard, and Holt Elementary to Shepard IB Middle, unanimously approved the CCRESA Local Alternative Teacher Preparation (LATP) contract for 23 lateral-entry teachers, and reviewed major capital and budget challenges including K-3 capacity losses (63 classrooms / 90 teachers needed) and Northern High School's wetland/soil issues ($3-$4 million site impact) and rising construction costs, reaching consensus to advance Northern into design development toward a February check-in. The session's sole split vote occurred at 02:46:39 on approving an updated membership list for the renamed Budget Process Advisory Committee (formerly Zero-Based Budgeting Committee), which passed 3-2 without a named roll call: Vice Chair Natalie Beyer opposed immediate approval until the Chair and Vice Chair could vet the two newly added nominees' readiness, while the three-member majority voted to approve the list immediately and conduct those conversations afterward before entering closed session on *O.V. et al. v. DPS Board of Education*.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Agenda Amendments, Minutes, and Superintendent Search Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Committee Chair Matt Sears called the meeting to order, observed a moment of silence, and obtained unanimous approval for an amended agenda adding a superintendent search update, moving the custodial RFP to 7A, adding Budget Committee member approval after item 7, and adding a closed session. The board unanimously approved the September 14 minutes and heard an announcement of the October 16 called meeting at the Staff Development Center to appoint and introduce the new superintendent.

agenda_items.title: Public Comment (Food Sharing Tables) and Consent Items
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Crystal Dreisbach of Don't Waste Durham advocated for cafeteria food-sharing tables on behalf of Lakewood Montessori teacher Corey Levetti to curb organic food waste. Staff then presented and the board unanimously approved consent items covering chiller bids for Burton and Hope Valley Elementary, Hillside weight room equipment, quarterly change orders, 2007 bond project closures/transfers, technical corrections to Policy 6305, and a program acquiring eight new activity buses.

agenda_items.title: Custodial Services Public Comment and RFP Timeline Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Numerous custodians (including Denise Wiggins, George Conrad, Delfina Contreras, Thomas Turner, and Vicki Mc...), Hillside teacher James Finnegan (with 39 faculty signatures), DAE President Bryan Proffitt, Brian Calloway, and Crystal Dreisbach described understaffing, lack of paid sick/vacation leave, and low wages under Service Solutions and urged bringing custodians in-house. Mr. Barnes reported the custodial RFP was posted with dual options (living wage plus 7.5% health/benefits vs. vendor base schedule), with bids due December 11 and a March 8 target for a vendor or in-house recommendation alongside parallel cost analysis.

agenda_items.title: Revision of Policy 4131.2: Program/Magnet Schools Assignment Priorities
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Dr. Pittman and Mary Griffith presented Policy 4131.2 revisions granting second-tier lottery priority at Shepard IB Middle School (behind Burton Elementary) to rising sixth graders from R.N. Harris, Club Boulevard, and Holt Elementary ahead of the November 4 Magnet Fair. Although Natalie Beyer sought two separate sentences to clarify Burton's first priority, the board agreed to pass the revision as written (waiving first reading) and have staff return with clarified wording as a follow-up item.

agenda_items.title: Local Alternative Teacher Preparation Program (LATP / CCRESA) Contract
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Kim Hager presented DPS's regional partnership through CCRESA/RISA offering an accelerated in-house licensure pathway (150 hours coursework plus 150 hours mentoring) for 23 first- and second-year lateral-entry middle and high school teachers, with DPS paying $3,000 and teachers paying $1,000 in exchange for a three-year DPS commitment. The board unanimously approved the contract.

agenda_items.title: 2017-18 20-Day Enrollment and Elementary Capacity / K-3 Class Size Study
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Donna reported a net K-12 enrollment decline of 93 students (elementary -244, middle -101, high school +252 led by Hillside and Hillside New Tech), smaller than projected due to charter returns. John Long then presented a school-by-school capacity analysis showing K-3 class size mandates reduce elementary capacity to 92.75% of historic benchmarks, leave almost all schools over operational capacity, and create a deficit of 63 classrooms (41 even with functional mobiles) and ~90 teachers (~$4-$6 million).

agenda_items.title: 2016 Bond Projects Update and Northern High School Site/Budget Challenges
agenda_items.discussion_summary: John Long reported summer progress across 2016 $90 million bond projects (including boilers/chillers ~$1 million under budget) but warned that regional construction inflation and poor soils/piped wetlands beneath Northern High School's baseball field add $3-$4 million in site mitigation/retaining wall costs above the $43 million construction budget. Rather than pausing immediately to search for a new 80-acre site, the board reached consensus to authorize moving Northern High into design development through February while also exploring alternative northern county land options.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Consensus to proceed to February design development

agenda_items.title: Allotment Formula Review, Substitute Process, and Classified Salary Study
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mr. LeSueur reviewed 2017-18 state vs. local allotment formulas; Kim Hager reported cleaning up active substitute rosters from ~500 to 878, adding 120 new subs, and establishing pay for teachers and instructional assistants covering classes during planning/duty; and Scott Denton previewed a three-step classified salary equity study matching state grades and building toward a $15/hour entry wage.

agenda_items.title: Budget Process Advisory Committee Membership Approval
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff presented an updated membership list and recommended renaming the Zero-Based Budgeting Committee to the Budget Process Advisory Committee, adding two new highlighted members and a Durham Citizens Rep slot. After Natalie Beyer objected to approving the two new members before the Chair and Vice Chair could confirm their commitment to the workload, another member urged approving the list immediately and following up afterward; the motion passed 3-2.

agenda_items.title: Follow-Up Items, Timeline Update, and Closed Session (*O.V. v. DPS*)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff reviewed Gantt-chart timelines and noted follow-ups on Policy 4131 rewrite, teacher class-coverage cost estimates, and Don't Waste Durham's food-sharing inquiry. The board then unanimously entered closed session at 02:49:58 to consult the board attorney regarding *O.V. and others v. Durham Public Schools Board of Education and others*, returning to open session at 03:08:52 to adjourn.

disagreements.meeting_title: Durham Public Schools BOE Operational Services & Policy Work Session October 12, 2017 4:30 PM
disagreements.issue: Immediate Approval vs. Pre-Approval Vetting of Budget Process Advisory Committee Nominees
disagreements.summary: The board split 3-2 on whether to immediately approve the updated membership list for the renamed Budget Process Advisory Committee (formerly Zero-Based Budgeting Committee) or pause approval of two new nominees until the Chair and Vice Chair spoke with them.
disagreements.side_a_position: Approve the administration's updated committee membership list immediately so the committee can continue its work without delay, and conduct Chair/Vice Chair outreach afterward.
side_a_arguments: The two new members had already attended the first committee meeting and understand its function.

meetings.title: Durham Public Schools BOE Academic & Student Services Work Session October 5, 2017 4:30 PM
meetings.executive_summary: At its October 5, 2017 Academic and Student Services Work Session (presided over by committee chair Bettina Umstead), the Durham Public Schools Board of Education unanimously approved an amended agenda, approved its consent items, met in closed session for attorney-client consultation, unanimously appointed Reverend Michael Page to fill the vacant DPS seat on the Durham Technical Community College Board of Trustees (replacing Mary Ann Black upon her move to the state legislature), and approved prior work session minutes. Dr. Daniel reported that Lakewood Elementary had been removed from the North Carolina Innovative School District takeover list while DPS and consultants from The Innovation Project proceeded with four-phase Restart planning and deep support at Glenn Elementary. Staff also updated the board on sliding-scale tuition at Whitted (87 families processed), Teaching, Learning, and Leadership instructional coherence and Letterland phonics implementation across 14 schools, mCLASS/TRC/DIBELS and i-Ready beginning-of-year literacy and math diagnostics showing persistent gaps for boys of color, Advanced Academics/AIG screening and AP Potential efforts, and Student Support Services' suspension trends (92% overall and 88% secondary non-suspension rates) alongside Second Chance Academy and Rebound serving over 700 students. The meeting concluded with warm tributes to departing instructional leader Stacey ahead of her transition to a state-level role; no split votes occurred.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Agenda Approval, Public Comment Check, and Consent Items
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Committee Chair Bettina Umstead called the work session to order, led a moment of silence, and obtained unanimous approval for an amended agenda adding an early closed session and an appointment to fill a Durham Tech Board of Trustees vacancy. No speakers were signed up for initial public comment, and the board unanimously approved the consent agenda.

agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board unanimously voted to enter closed session to consult with the board attorney under attorney-client privilege, returning to open session at 00:27:36.

agenda_items.title: Durham Tech Board of Trustees Appointment and Work Session Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: To fill the seat vacated when Mary Ann Black joined the state legislature, the board unanimously appointed Reverend Michael Page to the Durham Technical Community College Board of Trustees and directed staff to send a confirmation letter to Durham Tech President Bill Ingram. The board also unanimously approved the prior work session minutes and offered a second window for general public comment.

agenda_items.title: Destination Success Schools & Restart Update (ISD Removal of Lakewood)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Dr. Daniel announced that following Innovative School District comprehensive needs assessments, Lakewood Elementary was removed from the state takeover list while DPS continued working to remove Glenn Elementary and prioritize wraparound, instructional coaching, and staffing supports through four-phase Restart planning with The Innovation Project.

agenda_items.title: Whitted Pre-K Sliding Scale Tuition Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff updated the board on sliding-scale tuition implementation at Whitted relative to two magnet schools, noting that 87 tuition-eligible families had been processed while enrollment continued as families moved.

agenda_items.title: Teaching, Learning, and Leadership Support & BOY Literacy/Math Data
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Instructional leaders detailed the four-layer instructional coherence framework, data dives and secondary instructional rounds, Letterland phonics rollout across 14 schools, and beginning-of-year mCLASS/TRC/DIBELS and i-Ready results (92% reading and 95% math completion). Discussion examined early-grade 'summer slide' drops, higher math than reading proficiency, and significant achievement gaps for ELL, EC, African American male, and Hispanic male students.

agenda_items.title: Opportunity & Access / Advanced Academics Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff updated the board on AIG identification diversity, universal second-grade CogAT screening to avoid relying solely on teacher nominations, and using EVAAS and PSAT AP Potential data to place underrepresented high school students into honors and AP coursework.

agenda_items.title: Student Support Services, Code of Conduct, Suspension Data, and Farewell Tributes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff reviewed separated elementary and secondary Codes of Student Conduct, reported that Second Chance Academy and Rebound kept over 700 students in educational settings, and noted 92% of all DPS students (88% secondary) received zero suspensions while targeting six focus schools and coaching teachers generating high referral rates. The board closed by honoring departing instructional leader Stacey ahead of her state-level move before adjourning at 02:59:26.

meetings.title: Durham Public Schools Board of Education Monthly Meeting September 28, 2017 6:30 PM
meetings.executive_summary: At its September 28, 2017 regular monthly meeting (presided over by Chair Dr. Mike Lee, with Minnie Forte-Brown absent in New Orleans presenting at a school board conference), the Durham Public Schools Board of Education celebrated Be Our Guest, School for Creative Studies Student of the Month, corporate partnership work at Lowe's Grove Middle, and academic honors including 78% of schools meeting or exceeding growth and 80%+ graduation rates across all high schools. The meeting marked the final board appearance of outgoing Superintendent Dr. Bert L'Homme prior to his October 1 departure; Dr. L'Homme warned against the state Innovative School District takeover threat facing Glenn and Lakewood Elementary, and board members thanked him for his leadership and presented an engraved recognition plaque. The board unanimously approved an amended agenda (adding an ISD update, 6-0) and the August 24 minutes (6-0), heard public comment from Paula Clow advocating for ESL support and teacher assistants at Glenn Elementary, received a superintendent search update and a board update reaffirming DPS's unanimous 2016 resolution opposing state takeover/privatization, and reviewed a $500,000 state bus-driver pay allocation raising starting pay from $14.04 to $14.50/hour and addressing step compression. Following closed session, the board unanimously (6-0) approved the September 28 personnel report; no split votes occurred.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order and Moment of Silence
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Dr. Mike Lee convened the September 28, 2017 regular monthly meeting, noted that Minnie Forte-Brown was absent while representing DPS and North Carolina at a school board conference in New Orleans, and led a moment of silence.

agenda_items.title: Celebrations: Be Our Guest, Student of the Month, Lowe's Grove Partner, and School Growth
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Bettina Umstead recognized parents from Glenn, Oak Grove, Merrick-Moore, Sandy Ridge, Carrington, and DSA for the Be Our Guest dinner prepared by Northern High culinary students, followed by Student of the Month from the School for Creative Studies and an RTP corporate partner's school transformation work at Lowe's Grove. Staff then recognized high-performing and high-growth schools including Mangum (A+), Burton, Holt, E.K. Powe, Rogers-Herr, Early College, and City of Medicine Academy, noting 78% of DPS schools met or exceeded growth and every high school topped an 80% graduation rate.

agenda_items.title: Superintendent's Update and Tribute to Outgoing Superintendent Dr. Bert L'Homme
agenda_items.discussion_summary: In his final board meeting prior to leaving October 1, Superintendent Dr. Bert L'Homme addressed the threat of state takeover of Glenn and Lakewood Elementary under the North Carolina Innovative School District law as a flawed experiment ignoring poverty and inequity. Board members paid tribute to Dr. L'Homme's integrity, equity focus, and 10 total years in Durham, presenting him with an engraved plaque of appreciation.

agenda_items.title: Amended Agenda Approval, General Public Comment, and August 24 Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board unanimously approved (6-0) amending the agenda to add an Innovative School District update (Item 9B) and approved the August 24, 2017 board meeting minutes (6-0). During public comment, Paula Clow spoke on behalf of Glenn Elementary, attributing lower test scores to insufficient English-learner instructional support and reductions in teacher assistants from 15 down to 5.

agenda_items.title: Reports of the Board: Superintendent Search and Innovative School District (ISD) Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Dr. Mike Lee reported that the board was actively reviewing candidate scores and interview notes in its superintendent search, while public speaker Mr. Jones commented on the search and questioned consolidating the internal audit function into fiscal operations. On Item 9B, board members reaffirmed DPS's April 2016 unanimous resolution opposing the Achievement/Innovative School District and privatization, defended Glenn and Lakewood's predominantly students-of-color communities, and noted a letter of support from the Durham County Board of Commissioners Chair.

agenda_items.title: Bus Driver Pay Allocation Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chief Operating Officer Scott Denton presented DPS's ~$500,000 share of the General Assembly's $16.8 million bus driver recruitment and retention allocation, raising starting bus driver pay from $14.04/hour to $14.50/hour toward the $15/hour goal and resolving salary compression across steps 1 through 8.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session and September 28, 2017 Personnel Report
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board voted 6-0 to enter closed session (adding attorney-client privilege consultation to the agenda items) at 01:15:28. Returning to open session at 02:24:35, the board unanimously (6-0) approved Dr. L'Homme's final personnel roster dated September 28, 2017 and adjourned.

meetings.title: Durham Public Schools BOE Operational Services & Policy Work Session September 14, 2017 4:30 PM
meetings.executive_summary: At its September 14, 2017 Operational Services and Policy Work Session (presided over by co-chair Natalie Beyer), the Durham Public Schools Board of Education heard public comments from Antonio Jones criticizing the $42,000 allocation to the Office of Equity Affairs and Central Office/Public Affairs staffing vacancies, and from Brian Calloway urging transition to in-house custodial labor rather than another Service Solutions contract extension. After unanimously pulling Item 6D from the consent agenda for public discussion of high school track repairs at three high schools (excluding Jordan High School), the board unanimously approved the remaining consent items (including cell tower lease renewals at Carrington Middle and Pearsontown Elementary) and later unanimously adopted the FY 2017-2018 budget resolution packaged with departmental organizational charts. The board also reviewed a draft board goal-setting framework aligned with Dr. Stacey Wilson-Norman's academic performance measures plan, discussed upcoming K-3 class-size mandate budget and facility pressures raised at an NCSBA update, and requested any already-compiled cost data on take-home district vehicles. agenda_items.title: Agenda Review and Approval

agenda_items.title: Superintendent Update on Suspension of DACA
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Dr. Bert L'Homme addressed the White House announcement suspending DACA and the fear and uncertainty created in Durham's community, following up on a supportive district letter. agenda_items.title: General Public Comment

agenda_items.title: 2016-2017 Student Data Review and Next Steps

Board members questioned how growth versus proficiency is measured and urged clearer use of mCLASS (K-3), i-Ready, and Lexile scores to tell parents whether children are reading on grade level.

agenda_items.title: Instructional Purchase Agreements (Curriculum Associates, Discovery Education, Learning A-Z)

Board members emphasized gathering teacher efficacy data to demonstrate return on investment to county commissioners and negotiating teacher recognition or scholarship benefits from major vendors before unanimously approving all three contracts.

agenda_items.title: 2017-2018 Work Session Topics and Follow-Up Items
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Members reviewed an evolving schedule of 2017-2018 Academic & Student Services work session topics beginning in October and recorded follow-up items: gathering names of private schools participating in Title I, adding Goal 3 to future plans, and creating a program evaluation process for Discovery Ed and related instructional contracts.

meetings.title: Durham Public Schools Board of Education Monthly Meeting August 24, 2017 6:30 PM
meetings.executive_summary: At its August 24, 2017 regular monthly meeting presided over by Chair Dr. Mike Lee, the Durham Public Schools Board of Education opened with a tribute led by Superintendent Dr. Bert L'Homme and former board member Heidi Carter honoring retiring Deputy Superintendent for Operations Hugh Osteen for 22 years of service, followed by public comments from six speakers on equity funding, the superintendent search, DACA protections, unfunded state K-3 class-size mandates, and limited school nurse coverage. On an added agenda item, the board voted unanimously by show of hands to authorize removing white supremacist Julian Carr's name from the middle school building at Durham School of the Arts, while discussing adding an educational plaque alongside the existing McKesson integration plaque. The board also reviewed revised 2017-2018 certified and principal salary schedules presented by Aaron Beaulieu and HR Director Kim Hager—funded locally (~$300,000 more for principals via central office vacancies) to offset state cuts to longevity and advanced-degree pay—and unanimously approved the schedules as amended to place specialty high schools on a separate schedule from middle schools. Following a closed session for personnel and student confidentiality matters, the board unanimously approved the August 24, 2017 personnel report and adjourned.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order and Moment of Silence
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Dr. Mike Lee opened the August 24, 2017 monthly board meeting, reviewed public comment procedures, and led a moment of silence asking attendees to reflect on national turmoil affecting students.

agenda_items.title: Celebration of Deputy Superintendent Hugh Osteen
agenda_items.discussion_summary: In place of a standard superintendent's update, Dr. Bert L'Homme and former 12-year board member Heidi Carter honored retiring Deputy Superintendent for Operations Hugh Osteen for 22 years of leadership overseeing school construction, renovations, and district operations.

agenda_items.title: Agenda Review and Approval
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Members added an item regarding the naming of the Carr Building at Durham School of the Arts (between items 8 and 9) and a closed session for student confidentiality and personnel matters. The amended agenda passed unanimously.

agenda_items.title: General Public Comment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Six speakers addressed the board, including Bryan Proffitt praising the district's post-election and DACA stances, creation of the Office of Equity Affairs, and Kim Hager's work on transfers and substitutes; Antonio Jones comparing DPS's Equity Affairs budget unfavorably with Wake County's $487,000 ($3.11/student) and promising a public records request; speakers stressing racial equity in the superintendent search; and Bill Garrity raising alarms over unfunded state K-3 class-size mandates and one-day-a-week school nurse staffing.

agenda_items.title: Removal of Julian Carr Name from Durham School of the Arts Building
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following remarks citing Julian Carr's history as a white supremacist, the board moved and seconded authorizing administration to immediately remove Carr's name from the middle school building at Durham School of the Arts. A board member requested placing an educational plaque explaining the decision next to the existing plaque honoring the McKissick/McKesson family and school integration, and the motion passed unanimously by show of hands.

agenda_items.title: Operational Services: 2017-2018 Certified & Principal Salary Schedules
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Aaron Beaulieu and HR Director Kim Hager presented revised 2017-2018 certified teacher and principal salary schedules responding to state legislation that eliminated principal longevity and tied base pay to ADM school size and growth bonuses, proposing a 20%–40% local supplement plus experience steps funded from central office vacancies (~$300,000 more for principals, with central office and classified schedules to follow). Following Minnie Forte-Brown's concern over grouping specialty high schools with middle schools, the board unanimously approved the schedules with an amendment putting specialty schools on a separate schedule.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session and Approval of August 24, 2017 Personnel Report
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Xavier Cason moved and another member seconded entering closed session under NCGS 143-318.11(a)(6), 115C-319, 115C-402, and 20 USC 1232g (FERPA) for confidential personnel and student matters, passing unanimously. Returning to open session at 02:05:45, the board unanimously approved the August 24, 2017 personnel roster and adjourned.

meetings.title: Durham Public Schools BOE Academic & Student Services Work Session August 17, 2017 4:30 PM
meetings.executive_summary: At its August 17, 2017 Academic and Student Services Work Session (presided over by co-chair Bettina Umstead), the Durham Public Schools Board of Education responded to the recent Charlottesville white supremacist rally by unanimously adopting a resolution drafted by Natalie Beyer opposing hate crimes and white supremacy, reading aloud the Day One anti-bullying Upstander Pledge, and asking administration and legal counsel to review the district's dress code policy regarding hate symbols. The board also reviewed Exceptional Children and 504 expenses (~$40 million total) before unanimously approving a Medicaid-billing consulting contract with Public Consulting Group (PCG), heard an implementation and training update on Policy 4321 protecting immigrant students' rights, and received a readiness and hiring update for the new Whitted School Pre-K center. Additionally, the board unanimously approved a one-time policy override to allow activity buses to transport EC staff on August 23 ahead of Policy 6320's second reading, entered closed session, and unanimously approved the August 17, 2017 personnel report. All votes in the meeting were unanimous.

agenda_items.discussion_summary: Co-chair Bettina Umstead called the August 17, 2017 Academic and Student Services Work Session to order and led a moment of silence.

agenda_items.discussion_summary: Board members amended the agenda to add a resolution opposing hate crimes and white supremacy, the Day One anti-bullying initiative, and a dress code policy review before reports; add approval of activity bus use after the Whitted School item; and postpone School Improvement Planning and Destination Success updates to the next meeting. The amended agenda passed unanimously.

agenda_items.title: General Public Comment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Bettina Umstead noted no speakers had signed up for public comment and stated the floor would reopen after 5:00 PM if attendees arrived later.

agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board moved, seconded, and unanimously approved the prior Academic and Student Services Work Session minutes.

agenda_items.discussion_summary: Natalie Beyer introduced a resolution condemning white nationalists, white supremacists, and neo-Nazis following the August 11-12 Charlottesville events and vehicular killing by James Alex Fields Jr., affirming DPS's commitment to teaching against racism and religious hatred. After minor edits clarifying 'Durham Public Schools Board of Education' and correcting a typo, the board unanimously adopted the resolution.

agenda_items.title: Day One Anti-Bullying Upstander Pledge and Dress Code Policy Review
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Board members reviewed and read aloud the Day One anti-bullying Upstander Pledge as a tool for principals and counselors at school opening. Members also reviewed the district dress code policy, referencing Orange County Schools' action on hate symbols, and asked administration and board attorneys to return with policy recommendations.

agenda_items.title: Public Consulting Group (PCG) Medicaid Billing Consulting Contract
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff and District 504 Coordinator Dr. Monique Link reviewed ~$40 million in total Exceptional Children and related student service expenses (~$7 million per quarter) and the state-federal funding gap covered by Durham County taxpayers. Members urged cultivating local Triangle vendors in future years before unanimously approving the consulting contract with Public Consulting Group (PCG).

agenda_items.title: Policy 4321 Training and Implementation Update (Student Rights)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff presented a comprehensive training project plan developed with Tharrington Smith, student records, data managers, and security to implement revised Policy 4321 (adopted in June) protecting student rights across all district touchpoints. Board members urged issuing a press release and encouraging principals to include Spanish-language assurances in back-to-school messages.

agenda_items.title: Whitted School Pre-K Opening and Staffing Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff reported that safety and procedural preparations were complete for opening the Whitted School Pre-K facility and detailed expedited HR hiring for 22 positions posted June 5 after budget delays. Board members praised HR staff Kim Hager and Tammy Johnson and discussed touring the facility with county commissioners.

agenda_items.title: Policy Override for August 23 Activity Bus Use
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Because revised Policy 6320 had only completed first reading and lacked public notice for a second reading, the board unanimously approved a one-time policy override allowing activity buses with drivers to transport EC staff to a required district workday event on August 23.

meetings.title: Durham Public Schools BOE Operational Services & Policy Work Session August 10, 2017 4:30 PM
meetings.executive_summary: At its August 10, 2017 Operational Services and Policy Work Session (presided over by co-chair Matt Sears), the Durham Public Schools Board of Education heard public comments on closing the opportunity gap for Black students, the Tyler Clementi Foundation's Day One anti-bullying initiative, and criticism of expanding Durham Police Department roles in schools. Superintendent Dr. Bert L'Homme reported that more than $2.5 million in additional Durham County funding enabled the district to add 76 total teaching positions (56.5 elementary, 6.5 middle, and 13 high school), lowering class-size ratios across most grades despite state AIG/ESL flexibility cuts and K-3 classroom-space constraints. Aaron Beaulieu and HR Director Kim Hager also briefed the board on the state's $35.4 million principal pay overhaul—criticized by board members for eliminating longevity and advanced-degree pay while relying heavily on EOG/EOC test growth—and outlined plans to bring forward a local principal supplement schedule within 30 to 60 days. All formal votes—covering the amended agenda, corrected minutes (on a modification by Steve Unruhe), entering closed session for personnel and litigation (*O.V. et al.* and *Tabb*), and approving the August 10 personnel report—passed unanimously.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order and Moment of Silence
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Co-chair Matt Sears called the August 10, 2017 Operational Services and Policy Work Session to order and led a moment of silence.

agenda_items.title: Agenda Review and Approval
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Dr. Bert L'Homme requested adding a teacher allotment report between items 5 and 6, while legal counsel and Matt Sears requested adding Item 9 (closed session for litigation and personnel matters). Seconded by Xavier Cason, the amended agenda passed unanimously.

agenda_items.title: Approval of Prior Work Session Minutes (as Corrected)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Xavier Cason moved and Natalie Beyer seconded approving the minutes, after which Steve Unruhe corrected page 4 to reflect that Aaron Beaulieu—not the Zero-Based Budget Committee—was asked to review the committee's recommendations. With Cason and Beyer accepting the modification, the corrected minutes passed unanimously.

agenda_items.title: General Public Comment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: William Jackson urged the board to focus on closing the opportunity gap affecting Black students; a representative of Bull City United and the Tyler Clementi Foundation previewed the Day One anti-bullying campaign; and a speaker criticized expanding Durham Police Department authority in schools after earlier proposed teacher cuts, urging the next superintendent to prioritize instruction over school security.

agenda_items.title: Teacher Allotments Update Following County Budget Increase
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Dr. Bert L'Homme reported that over $2.5 million in added county funds combined with the board's prior 33 positions funded 76 additional teaching positions (56.5 elementary, 6.5 middle, 13 high school) distributed equitably across schools, lowering student-teacher ratios despite state AIG/ESL flexibility losses and K-3 space constraints. Board members thanked parents, educators, and county commissioners and asked administration to communicate the classroom investments officially to the county.
