meetings.title: Durham Public Schools Board of Education Organizational Meeting July 18, 2017 4:30 PM
meetings.executive_summary: At its July 18, 2017 annual organizational meeting (with all seven board members present), the Durham Public Schools Board of Education unanimously re-elected Dr. Mike Lee as Board Chair by a 7-0 vote on a nomination from Minnie Forte-Brown, but split in a contested election for Vice Chair between incumbent Natalie Beyer and Steve Unruhe. Under Policy 2200 voting in order of nomination, Natalie Beyer's nomination failed 2-5 on a voice vote (no roll call was read in the transcript to identify the two Ayes or five Nays), after which Steve Unruhe was elected Vice Chair by a 6-0-1 voice vote (zero Nays and one unnamed member explicitly stating 'I didn't vote'). The board also heard public comment from Antonio Jones on the 42-applicant superintendent search and projected student enrollment loss despite city growth, unanimously approved an amended 2017-2018 meeting calendar (moving the August 3 work session to August 17 and making the December monthly meeting optional), and workshopped superintendent search priorities and interview processes with search consultants. Following a closed session for personnel and attorney-client matters, the board unanimously approved the July 18, 2017 personnel report and adjourned.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Moment of Silence, and Addition of Public Comment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Dr. Mike Lee called the July 18, 2017 organizational meeting to order (~10 minutes late so all seven members were present), led a moment of silence, and added a public comment period after officer elections by common consent because this was the board's only July meeting.

agenda_items.title: Election of Board Chair
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Superintendent Dr. Bert L'Homme temporarily took the gavel to oversee the Chair election under Policy 2200 (requiring no second and voting in order of nomination). Minnie Forte-Brown nominated Dr. Mike Lee; with no other nominations, Dr. Mike Lee was unanimously re-elected Chair 7-0 and resumed the gavel.

agenda_items.title: Contested Election of Board Vice Chair
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Both Natalie Beyer and Steve Unruhe were nominated for Board Vice Chair. Voting in order of nomination under Policy 2200, Natalie Beyer's nomination failed 2-5 on a voice vote, and Steve Unruhe was subsequently elected Vice Chair with zero Nays and one unnamed member declining to vote (6-0-1).
agenda_items.vote_summary: Natalie Beyer failed 2-5; Steve Unruhe elected 6-0-1

agenda_items.title: Public Comment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Antonio Jones congratulated Dr. Mike Lee, welcomed hearing that 42 candidates applied for the DPS superintendent vacancy, and questioned why DPS was projected to lose 400 students next year while state projections showed Durham growing by 25,000 residents over five years.

agenda_items.title: Approval of 2017-2018 Board of Education Meetings Calendar
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Board members reviewed calendar conflicts around winter holidays and mandatory April budget-season meetings. The board unanimously approved the 2017-2018 meeting calendar as amended: moving the August 3 Academic & Student Services work session to August 17, designating the December monthly meeting as optional, and retaining all April meetings.

agenda_items.title: Superintendent Search Criteria and Interview Process Workshop
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Search consultants led board members through defining superintendent leadership priorities—highlighting integrity, racial equity and cultural competence, budget management with clear metrics, teacher/principal retention, closing achievement gaps, accountability, and transparency—and outlined first- and second-round presentation and behavior-based interview plans for 7 to 10 selected applicants.

agenda_items.title: District Achievements Poster, Closed Session, and July 18, 2017 Personnel Report
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Dr. Mike Lee highlighted a wall poster showcasing DPS student and educator honors before the board unanimously entered closed session for confidential personnel matters and attorney-client consultation. Returning to open session at 02:22:00, the board unanimously approved the July 18, 2017 personnel report and adjourned.

meetings.title: Durham Public Schools Board of Education Monthly Meeting June 22, 2017 6:30 PM
meetings.executive_summary: At its June 22, 2017 regular monthly meeting presided over by Chair Dr. Mike Lee, the Durham Public Schools Board of Education recognized June Student of the Month Alisa Marie Carlson in absentia and heard a superintendent update from Dr. Bert L'Homme on summer instructional programs, retiring Deputy Superintendent Hugh Osteen, and an upcoming August principal pay proposal. Four public commenters—including Durham Association of Educators representative Alexa Goff and parent Chad Searsley—thanked the board and county commissioners for preserving 32 teacher and assistant principal positions while urgently appealing for outreach to commissioners over unexpected ~$750,000–$1 million state budget cuts to AIG and ESL budgets affecting 15.5 positions. Following consent agenda review on student voter registration policy 3640/5130 and a truncated middle section covering universal second-grade CogAT gifted screening, the board unanimously approved the FY 2017-2018 interim budget resolution and heard Aaron Beaulieu's briefing on hidden state budget costs, prompting board direction for Dr. L'Homme to contact County Commission Chair Wendy Jacobs immediately. After a closed session, the board unanimously approved the June 22, 2017 personnel report; all recorded votes in the digest were unanimous.

agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Dr. Mike Lee opened the June 22, 2017 regular monthly board meeting, led a moment of silence, and recognized Alisa Marie Carlson as June Student of the Month in absentia while she was on summer vacation.

agenda_items.title: Superintendent's Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Dr. Bert L'Homme summarized summer school initiatives (Take 2 testing, Back on Track/Credit Recovery, Spark Camp, and five-week CTE), praised retiring Deputy Superintendent Hugh Osteen's career, and committed to presenting a principal pay equity proposal in August.

agenda_items.title: Agenda Review and Approval
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board unanimously approved the meeting agenda, and a member shared Dr. Kristin Bell's Exceptional Children monthly newsletters with board members.

agenda_items.title: General Public Comment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Four speakers (Alexa Goff for DAE, Waldo Fenner, Dr. Austin, and Chad Searsley) thanked the board and county commissioners for preserving 32 teacher and assistant principal positions, warned that an unexpected ~$1 million state cut to AIG and ESL risked 15.5 positions just one business day before county budget release, and urged focusing funds on classrooms and recruiting an experienced superintendent.

agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board moved, seconded, and unanimously approved the May 24, 2017 regular monthly meeting minutes.

meetings.title: Durham Public Schools BOE Operational Services Work Session 06 15 2017   4:30
meetings.executive_summary: At its June 15, 2017 Operational Services and Policy Work Session (video dated 2017-06-16, presided over by co-chair Matt Sears), the Durham Public Schools Board of Education piloted its new consent agenda format by unanimously pulling Item 7A (budget amendment), Item 7B (student voter registration policy), and Items 7I and 7J (high school track repair bids) for full discussion, moving Item 7M to the June 22 regular meeting, and unanimously approving the remaining facility and renovation consent items (including parking lot paving, middle school gym renovations, Watts boiler replacement, Harris roof replacement, and Eno Valley renovations). After recognizing Transportation honorees Tammy Phillips, Danny Johnson, and Susan Beerholm and beginning a presentation on Zero-Based Budget Committee recommendations (before a truncated middle segment), the board unanimously approved the budget amendment item and debated whether to hold July work sessions on redistricting, custodial contracts, and budget priorities versus giving 11-month staff a July break. Members resolved the scheduling debate by unanimously voting to convene only the annual organizational meeting (and potential personnel closed session) on July 18, 2017 at 4:30 PM, and concluded with a Substitute Teacher Committee update from Aaron Beaulieu noting $4.5 million in annual substitute costs against roughly $50,000 in state reimbursement. All recorded votes were unanimous.

agenda_items.discussion_summary: Implementing a consent agenda for the first time, board members clarified that any member may pull an item prior to agenda adoption and pulled Item 7A (budget amendment), Item 7B (student voter registration policy), and Items 7I–7J (high school track repairs) to Item 10; shifted Item 7M to June 22 on a technicality; and added a discussion of potential July work sessions as Item 11. disagreements.meeting_title: Durham Public Schools BOE Operational Services Work Session 06 15 2017   4:30
disagreements.issue: Whether to Hold July 2017 Work Sessions for Redistricting, Budget, and Custodial Work
disagreements.summary: Board members debated scheduling one or two Wednesday work sessions in July to advance redistricting, custodial, and budget items versus preserving the traditional July hiatus for district staff.
disagreements.side_a_position: Hold one or two Wednesday work sessions in July so administration can present initial work chunks (such as redistricting priorities) rather than pausing until August.
side_a_arguments: A backlog of major items—redistricting, budget, and custodial matters—remained on the board's plate after canceling public hearings.
Meeting on Wednesday would avoid holding staff late at the end of their four-day summer workweek.
disagreements.side_b_position: Oppose July work sessions to give 11-month district staff a break and limit July activity to the required annual organizational meeting (plus urgent personnel closed session if needed).
side_b_arguments: Staff work 11 months a year and 12–15 hour days on summer 4-day schedules, making July their only reset window before year-round schools open July 17.
Board members had summer travel conflicts in July, making full work sessions difficult.
disagreements.resolution: Resolved by unanimous compromise: the board scheduled only its annual organizational meeting for Tuesday, July 18, 2017 at 4:30 PM (accommodating Bettina Umstead's July 19–21 absence) without adding July work sessions.

boe_dae_events.event_title: Financial Education Strategy Ad Hoc Committee Two-Year Pilot ($200,000 MetLife Trust Fund)
boe_dae_events.dae_position: Teachers and district staff needed independent, non-sales-driven retirement and financial education rather than predatory vendor pitches at mandatory faculty meetings to improve employee respect and retention.

member_positions.stance_summary: Asked clarifying budget questions about how the MetLife stock trust value was accounted for on financial statements and seconded the motion to fund the two-year employee financial wellness pilot.
member_positions.key_quote: The stock value of MetLife that we had hanging out somewhere, was that number calculated somewhere in our budget?

member_positions.stance_summary: Recounted 29 years of teachers being forced to sit through mandatory faculty meetings with high-pressure sales vendors, calling the independent financial education pilot a major step toward treating employees with respect and retaining teachers. Moved approval of the funding recommendation.
member_positions.key_quote: But it's also a step that says we're going to approach working with our employees in a different way, with a higher level of respect.

boe_dae_events.event_title: Policy 4321 Revision: Law Enforcement, Immigration Protections, and Staff Training (DAE Advocacy)
boe_dae_events.dae_position: DAE members, educators, and community advocates collaborated with DPS to revise Policy 4321 so protections apply to all law enforcement agencies, require mandatory interpretation, mandate a superintendent warrant log, and deliver face-to-face training for all school staff.

member_positions.stance_summary: Explicitly thanked DAE and partner groups for their advocacy protecting immigrant students and families, pressed for the superintendent's warrant log to enable deeper board follow-up if systemic issues arise at a school, and moved approval of Policy 4321.
member_positions.key_quote: So thank you all for the work and thank DAE and other groups for the advocacy for these groups.

member_positions.stance_summary: Seconded Dr. Mike Lee's motion to approve the Policy 4321 revisions and voted aye in the unanimous 6-0 approval.

boe_dae_events.event_title: Service Solutions Custodial Contract Six-Month Extension and In-House Cost Study
boe_dae_events.dae_position: Custodians and staff advocates urged DPS to return custodial services in-house with full state benefits rather than extending outsourcing, criticizing contractor benefit cuts (18% vs. 30% state benefits) and corporate profit margins.

member_positions.stance_summary: Asked maintenance director Ken Barnes for his recommendation, probed whether centralized in-house models like child nutrition had been studied, and noted concern over 'polar opposite opinions' on school cleanliness. Supported the six-month extension including the $15/hour living wage adjustment ($95,229) to avoid summer disruption.
member_positions.key_quote: It's just concerning that there's such polar opposite opinions of the cleanliness of the schools.

member_positions.stance_summary: Emphasized that the Board owes the community a thorough, nuanced investigation of in-house versus outsourced custodial service and noted she has always been glad DPS did not outsource child nutrition. meetings.title: Durham Public Schools BOE Operational Services Work Session 05 11 2017
meetings.executive_summary: At the May 11, 2017 Operational Services and Policy Work Session (presided over by Matt Sears, with Dr. Mike Lee absent and six members present), the Durham Public Schools Board of Education honored departing board liaison June Snyder, heard extensive public comment opposing school-level and arts cuts, and engaged in a contentious debate over the FY 2017-18 budget ask to Durham County ahead of the May 15 statutory deadline. An amendment by Minnie Forte-Brown (seconded by Natalie Beyer) to add all four deferred needs—including the $2.3 million $15/hour living wage—failed 2-4 (Ayes: Minnie Forte-Brown, Natalie Beyer; Nays: Matt Sears, Bettina Umstead, Xavier Cason, Steve Unruhe). A compromise amendment by Natalie Beyer (seconded by Minnie Forte-Brown) adding bus driver incentives ($200,000), increased substitute pay ($1.0 million), and teacher recruitment ($500,000) without the living wage initially tied 3-3 and failed (Ayes: Natalie Beyer, Minnie Forte-Brown, Xavier Cason; Nays: Matt Sears, Bettina Umstead, Steve Unruhe), before passing 4-2 on reconsideration (moved by Bettina Umstead, seconded by Steve Unruhe; Ayes on reconsidered amendment: Natalie Beyer, Minnie Forte-Brown, Xavier Cason, Bettina Umstead; Nays: Matt Sears, Steve Unruhe, without a named roll call). The final amended ~$10.8 million additional funding ask then passed 4-2 by voice/hand vote without a named roll call (Minnie Forte-Brown had stated she would vote no without a living wage and Steve Unruhe objected to adding unvetted items). The board also unanimously approved the Hillside LED lighting installation bid ($177,700), the 1817 Hamlin Road warehouse roof replacement bid ($606,824), a $0.15 paid student meal price increase to $2.90, annual Child Nutrition bid renewals, and placing four revised technology policies (3220, 3225, 3226, 3230) on the May consent agenda.

agenda_items.discussion_summary: Matt Sears called the May 11, 2017 Operational Services and Policy Work Session to order and led a moment of silence. Dr. Mike Lee was absent from the meeting, leaving six board members present.

agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board approved two amendments to the agenda: adding a special recognition as Item 5 prior to public comment (moved by Natalie Beyer) and amending Item 7B to remove the custodial contract extension, leaving only the custodial program update (moved by Steve Unruhe, seconded by Natalie Beyer). Both motions passed unanimously.

agenda_items.title: Approval of Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board moved, seconded, and unanimously approved the prior Operational Services work session minutes by voice vote.

agenda_items.title: Special Recognition of Board Liaison June Snyder
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Board members held a special recognition celebrating retiring/departing board liaison June Snyder for her years of thorough, professional service to the board and community.

agenda_items.title: General Public Comment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Speakers including Brian Callaway (criticizing executive travel stipends and prior reductions in force) and Durham School of the Arts parents and students (including Lauren Jones) urged the board to protect classroom teaching positions, arts pathways, and Hillside/DSA programs rather than making school-level cuts.

agenda_items.title: Financial Services: FY 2017-18 Budget Public Comment and Approval
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following budget public comment from four speakers—including Laura Timus, Abiira Kawajiro, and DSA/Club Boulevard parents and students advocating against arts and teacher cuts—CFO Aaron Beaulieu presented the $429,611,264 proposed budget featuring a $3.48 million base ask, a separate $1.5 million Whitted School Pre-K ask, $8 million in central office reductions (including 35 academic facilitators), and $3.1 million in school-level reductions (247 clerical months, 8.1 APs, and 24 teachers). Steve Unruhe moved a ~$9.2 million county ask adding back the $3.155 million in school-level positions and $2.6 million in teacher retention items (extracurricular pay, parental leave, extra duty pay); Minnie Forte-Brown's amendment to add all four deferred needs including living wage failed 2-4, and Natalie Beyer's amendment adding bus driver incentives, substitute pay, and teacher recruitment tied 3-3 before passing 4-2 on reconsideration, with the final ~$10.8 million amended budget ask passing 4-2.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Passed 4-2 (after failed 2-4 and 3-3 amendments and 4-2 reconsideration)

agenda_items.title: Removal of Item 7B (Custodial Update) and Item 9A (PLC) by Consent
agenda_items.discussion_summary: After a brief recess, the board consented to administration's request to remove Item 7B (custodial program update) and Item 9A (PLC item) from the agenda to allow full discussion at the upcoming Academic and Student Services work session.

agenda_items.title: Bids for Lighting Upgrade Installation at Hillside High School
agenda_items.discussion_summary: During public comment, Brian Callaway criticized administrative delays in spending bond funds and urged moving forward on a Bacon Street lighting proposal with over $100,000 in Duke Energy incentives. John Long then presented the re-bid for Hillside High School LED lighting installation (expanded by ~300 fixtures), recommending award of the $177,700 contract with 100% minority participation to Diversified Electrical Technologies, which passed unanimously.

agenda_items.title: Bids for 1817 Hamlin Road Warehouse Roof Replacement
agenda_items.discussion_summary: John Long presented six bids for a full roof replacement at the 1817 Hamlin Road warehouse under the 2016 bond program, recommending award to low bidder Triad Roofing of Winston-Salem for $606,824 including Alternate 1 (with 10% minority participation). Following a clarifying question on remaining 2007 bond funds, the board unanimously approved the bid.

agenda_items.title: 2017-18 Meal Prices and School Nutrition Services Budget Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Jim Keaton presented a proposed $0.15 increase for paid student meals (bringing paid meals to $2.90, affecting under $45,000 districtwide) to comply with federal equity-in-school-lunch-pricing rules restricting the gap with free-meal reimbursements to $0.10. Board members commended Keaton, Aaron Beaulieu, and staff for turning a $500,000 deficit two years prior into a projected surplus and unanimously approved the increase.

agenda_items.discussion_summary: Jim Keaton recommended awarding two five-year-renewable RFPs (SFSPAC/FSPAC for sanitation/chemicals and Dawn Woods Graphics for free-and-reduced printing) and exercising second-year renewals for Sysco Raleigh (food/supplies), Pet Dairy (milk), Flowers Bakery (bread), local Domino's (whole-grain Smart Slice pizza), and R&H Produce. The board unanimously approved the awards and renewals.

agenda_items.discussion_summary: Dr. Pittman and technology staff presented first-reading updates from the North Carolina School Boards Association to Policies 3220, 3225, 3226, and 3230 (including copyright compliance rules on showing commercial movies). The board unanimously voted to place the second reading and adoption of all four policies on the May full board consent agenda.

disagreements.meeting_title: Durham Public Schools BOE Operational Services Work Session 05 11 2017
disagreements.issue: Inclusion of $15/Hour Living Wage and Deferred Needs in FY 2017-18 County Budget Ask
disagreements.summary: Board members split across multiple amendment votes over whether to restrict the county funding request to a vetted ~$9.2M package (restoring school-level positions and teacher retention items) or expand it to ~$10.8M–$13.2M by adding deferred needs such as bus driver incentives, substitute pay, teacher recruitment, and a $2.3M $15/hour living wage.
disagreements.side_a_position: Limit the county ask to ~$9.2M covering the $3.48M base request, $3.155M in school-level restorations, and $2.6M in teacher retention items, while studying living wage jointly with the county next year.
side_a_arguments: DPS already agreed with Durham County to study total compensation and benefits differences (including 5-year vs. 25-year retirement vesting) before proposing living-wage alignment next cycle.
Deferred items like bus driver incentives and substitute pay had not been fully vetted or prioritized against other deferred capital needs such as $5M in annual facility upkeep.
A $9.2M ask is already ambitious (requiring local tax effort and losing 18% to charter schools) and represents a disciplined, defensible budget.
disagreements.side_b_position: Expand the county ask to include deferred employee and operational priorities—ideally all ~$4M including the $2.3M $15/hour living wage (Forte-Brown/Beyer), or at minimum bus driver incentives, substitute pay, and teacher recruitment (Beyer/Cason/Umstead on reconsideration).
side_b_arguments: Classified staff such as bus drivers and custodians face the same living costs and deserve parity with Durham City and County's $15/hour wage.
Bus driver incentives, substitute pay, and teacher recruitment directly align with board goals and the severe substitute shortage.
Durham taxpayers and progressive county commissioners cannot fund needs the board does not formally request.
disagreements.resolution: Forte-Brown's $4M all-items amendment failed 2-4; Beyer's 3-item amendment (excluding living wage) tied 3-3 before passing 4-2 on reconsideration (moved by Umstead, seconded by Unruhe), and the final ~$10.8M amended budget ask passed 4-2 without a named roll call.

boe_dae_events.event_title: FY 2017-18 Budget Amendment: $15/Hour Living Wage and All Four Deferred Employee Needs
boe_dae_events.dae_position: DAE President Bryan Proffitt urged the Board to send a bold, expanded budget request to Durham County Commissioners to prevent cuts and fund educator and classified staff priorities, while staff/community highlighted classified RIFs and the $2.3M $15/hour living wage.

member_positions.stance_summary: Strongly championed adding all four deferred needs—including the $2.3M $15/hour living wage, bus driver incentives, substitute pay, and teacher recruitment—and formally moved the amendment. Invoked being the daughter of a custodian to argue that classified workers must receive a fair share alongside teachers and that Durham should ask the county for everything students and staff need rather than self-censoring.
member_positions.key_quote: Living wage. We've got to pay people a living wage.

member_positions.stance_summary: Seconded Forte-Brown's four-item amendment and urged the Board to 'dream just a little bit bigger' with progressive county commissioners. While willing to set aside the $2.3M living wage if needed to pass the other three staff items, she voted AYE to put all four deferred employee needs in the ask.
member_positions.key_quote: I'm still appreciative of the work, but hoping that we might dream just a little bit bigger in this moment.

member_positions.stance_summary: Praised Steve Unruhe's $9.2M base motion for restoring school-level positions and teacher retention, while criticizing the rushed process and lack of clarity on how deferred numbers like living wage were built. Voted NAY on the $4M four-item amendment in favor of waiting for stronger program evaluation and ZBB review.
member_positions.key_quote: So this year I feel good about the motion that Steve made and that we are asking for more than the original ask and that we're moving the right direction away from all these cuts.

member_positions.stance_summary: Thanked community members for emailing and acknowledged that deferred compensation needs drive employees to leave Durham for neighboring counties. However, she voted NAY on adding all four deferred items at once, citing process concerns about unvetted additions.
member_positions.key_quote: And I recognize that those deferred needs are some of the things that are forcing people to leave our district and people are making decisions.

member_positions.stance_summary: Stated he strongly supports a living wage in principle and explicitly agreed with DAE's advocacy to move toward national/average school funding levels. However, he opposed adding the $2.3M living wage or deferred items to this motion because the Board had agreed to study living wage jointly with the county and the proposals were not yet fully developed.
member_positions.key_quote: However, the reason I did not put it in my own motion is because we've already made an agreement with the county to look at that.

member_positions.stance_summary: Supported the $9.2M ask covering base needs, school-level restorations, and teacher retention, calling it defensible and close to a no-cuts budget. Opposed adding the $4M deferred list because major capital and facility upkeep needs were also unranked and unstudied.
member_positions.key_quote: So as the motion stands, I can support a $9.2 million additional funding ask from the county and be proud that that gets us very close to a no cuts budget from comparing dollars to dollars.

boe_dae_events.event_title: Amended FY 2017-18 County Budget Request (~$10.8M): Bus Driver Incentives, Substitute Pay, and Teacher Recruitment
boe_dae_events.dae_position: DAE urged the Board to pass an expanded county budget request to protect classroom and school positions and fund educator and support-staff priorities, including bus driver incentives, substitute teacher pay, and teacher recruitment.

member_positions.stance_summary: Moved the three-item amendment adding $200K in bus driver incentives, $1M for substitute teacher pay, and $500K for teacher recruitment (excluding the $2.3M living wage) so the Board would highlight staff equity needs to County Commissioners. After the initial 3-3 tie failed, she persisted until reconsideration passed 4-2.
member_positions.key_quote: I think we're missing an opportunity to highlight these needs and have important conversations with our county's funders about equity for our staff and really profound needs.

member_positions.stance_summary: Initially voted NAY on the three-item amendment (creating a 3-3 tie at [01:44:32]) over process concerns about incomplete needs lists. Later moved to reconsider the amendment because adding bus driver incentives and substitute pay covered classified roles and made the budget request more inclusive across staff.
member_positions.key_quote: It makes sure to cover some folks that are in classified roles, and that I think is a more inclusive ask.

member_positions.stance_summary: Seconded Beyer's three-item amendment and voted AYE on reconsideration and the final ~$10.8M budget request. Argued the Board should stop being timid, ask commissioners for what employees and students actually need, and protect classified staff alongside teachers.
member_positions.key_quote: I just, you know, I don't know why we are afraid to be bold.

member_positions.stance_summary: Supported Beyer's three-item amendment and the final ~$10.8M budget ask because teacher recruitment and substitute pay directly aligned with goals the Board set at its retreat and prior staff directives.
member_positions.key_quote: For me particularly the teacher recruitment and the sub pay are very much aligned to our goals as a board.

member_positions.stance_summary: Seconded Umstead's reconsideration motion only to resolve the procedural impasse, but voted NAY on the three-item amendment and the final ~$10.8M budget request. Argued that adding unvetted items onto the budget ask was neither bold nor fiscally responsible when the Board already faced a hard fight for $9.2M.
member_positions.key_quote: But to me, I don't consider it bold, I don't consider it visionary to simply keep adding things to a list.

member_positions.stance_summary: Voted NAY on the three-item amendment and the final ~$10.8M budget request, reiterating that facility upkeep and other unranked priorities were left off. Characterized adding the three deferred items without a prioritized list as arbitrary.
member_positions.key_quote: Are we going to have the budget proposal as presented or are we going to add things arbitrarily, I would call arbitrarily, to the budget?

meetings.title: Durham Public Schools BOE Academic & Student Services Work Session May 4, 2017 4:30 PM
meetings.executive_summary: At the May 4, 2017 Academic and Student Services Work Session (presided over by Dr. Mike Lee ahead of the evening's superintendent search and budget hearings), the Durham Public Schools Board of Education unanimously approved the agenda, April meeting minutes, and a 2017-18 Exceptional Children contract for visually impaired and orientation and mobility services funded entirely through state and federal EC grants. Staff presented a six-step English as a Second Language (ESL) action plan to stop disrupting classroom instruction for translation—introducing an in-house translation phone line, planning-period extra-duty compensation, quality-control enforcement, protected school translation budget lines, front-office training, and bilingual HR recruitment. The board also reviewed a state-mandated Read to Achieve summer reading camp update opening nine tuition-based seats ($750 for 12 days) at Hillandale Elementary for already-proficient students, as well as spring 2017 graduation logistics across NCCU, Riverside High School, and Duke's Cameron Indoor Stadium. All votes were unanimous and no policy splits occurred.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Moment of Silence, and Agenda Review
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Dr. Mike Lee called the May 4, 2017 Academic and Student Services Work Session to order, led a moment of silence, and outlined the evening's three-meeting schedule (work session until 5:30 PM, superintendent search public comment at 5:30 PM, and budget public hearing at 6:30 PM). The board unanimously approved the agenda.

agenda_items.title: Approval of April Work Session Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: With no members signed up for general public comment, the board moved, seconded, and unanimously approved the minutes from the April 2017 work session.

agenda_items.title: ESL Actions to Address Class Disruptions and Translation Compensation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Sasha and ESL leadership presented six action steps to ensure instruction is never interrupted for translation: creating a dedicated in-house school translation phone line (shifting contracted funds to hire one district desk position), establishing school-level planning-period extra-duty pay from ESL set-aside funds, enforcing proficiency/quality guidelines, dedicating a protected budget line item for translation, training front-office staff twice yearly across languages (including Spanish, Arabic, Burmese, Karen, Swahili, and Kinyarwanda), and collaborating with HR on bilingual recruitment. Board members asked about expanding bilingual recruitment to states like Texas and Arizona and formalizing planning-period buyback compensation for substitute coverage as well.

agenda_items.title: Read to Achieve Summer Reading Camp Policy Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mr. Gibson briefed the board on a legislative change requiring districts to offer summer reading camp access to students already demonstrating proficiency, subject to district capacity. Working with the board attorney, DPS opened nine tuition-based seats at Hillandale Elementary (three each in grades 1–3) at $750 for 12 days (excluding bus transportation), with clear descriptors noting the curriculum is designed for struggling readers so parents of proficient students are not misled.

agenda_items.title: Exceptional Children 2017-18 Contract for Visually Impaired and Orientation & Mobility Services
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Dr. Bell presented a 2017-18 Exceptional Children contract for specialized visually impaired and orientation/mobility services required for student IEPs, noting the positions could not be filled directly with DPS employees. After clarifying that the contract is funded entirely from state and federal EC grants rather than DPS's $18 million local EC mandate gap, the board unanimously approved the contract.

agenda_items.title: Spring 2017 Graduation Logistics Discussion and Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff presented spring 2017 graduation schedules, venues, parking passes, and regalia logistics: four early-calendar ceremonies on May 25 at NCCU (including Hillside New Tech), two ceremonies on June 12 at Riverside High School auditorium (School for Creative Studies' first graduating class and Durham Performance Learning Center), and six comprehensive high school ceremonies on June 13–14 at Duke's Cameron Indoor Stadium.

agenda_items.title: Follow-Up Items and Adjournment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff noted one takeaway regarding publicizing and formalizing the high school planning-period buyback program, after which the chair adjourned the work session until 5:30 PM.

meetings.title: Durham Public Schools Public Comments Proposed Budget May 4, 2017 5:30 PM
meetings.executive_summary: At the May 4, 2017 FY 2017-18 proposed budget public hearing (presided over by Dr. Mike Lee, with Superintendent Dr. Bert Lumm excused due to illness), the Durham Public Schools Board of Education heard from 37 registered community speakers limited to two minutes each. Parents, students, principals, classified staff, and People's Alliance representatives urged the board to expand its funding request to Durham County to restore proposed cuts to 24 classroom teaching positions, 20 instructional facilitators, assistant principals, and Durham School of the Arts and Hillside arts pathways, as well as to raise all classified staff to a $15/hour living wage. meetings.executive_summary: At the April 27, 2017 monthly meeting (presided over by Dr. Mike Lee, with Minnie Forte-Brown arriving late prior to the superintendent search discussion), the Durham Public Schools Board of Education celebrated parent volunteers and student honorees and received Dr. Bert Lumm's update announcing AdvancED's recommendation to renew district accreditation, restorative justice training, the Early Education Preschool Task Force's universal pre-K draft plan, and his upcoming August retirement. Board members held an extended policy debate over the superintendent search process—weighing an open national search and search-firm proposals (favored by Steve Unruhe, Matt Sears, and Natalie Beyer on different dimensions) against candidate confidentiality, internal capacity, and avoiding a disruptive reset (cautioned by Minnie Forte-Brown)—ultimately agreeing to host an initial May 4 listening session, task a three-member subcommittee (Forte-Brown, Umstead, Cason) with proposing community hearing dates, and request written proposals from search firms. CFO Aaron Beaulieu then presented the formal ~$430 million proposed FY 2017-18 budget reflecting Governor's signature on HB 13 K-3 relief, $8.8 million in central office cuts, $3.1 million in school-level cuts, and $18 million in unfunded EC mandates. The board unanimously approved the agenda, March 23 minutes, closed session, and the April 27 personnel report.

agenda_items.title: Superintendent's Update

agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following public comment from Crystal Rogers, John Davis, and other community speakers urging both internal and external consideration and public engagement, the board debated how to structure the search after Dr. Lumm's retirement. Members agreed to hold an initial 5:30 PM public listening session on May 4, ask Minnie Forte-Brown, Bettina Umstead, and Xavier Cason to draft a broader community engagement schedule, and solicit written proposals from search firms for review at the May 4 work session.

agenda_items.title: Proposed FY 2017-18 Budget Presentation

disagreements.meeting_title: Durham Public Schools Board of Education Monthly Meeting April 27, 2017
disagreements.issue: Superintendent Search Structure, Openness, and Community Engagement Process
disagreements.summary: Board members held differing views on whether to conduct a broad, open national search using an outside firm and rapid public feedback vs. protecting candidate confidentiality, avoiding a disruptive system reset, and organizing multi-region community engagement.
disagreements.side_a_position: Conduct a wide search informed by rapid public input and written search-firm proposals (with Steve Unruhe and Natalie Beyer favoring broader external searches and Matt Sears exploring non-traditional talent acquisition firms).
side_a_arguments: Steve Unruhe argued it would be irresponsible to close off the search from thousands of external leaders and urged soliciting community input on May 4 without delay.
Matt Sears advocated requesting written search-firm proposals and exploring outside headhunter/evaluation models rather than limiting options to NCSBA.
Natalie Beyer urged collecting additional parent and student feedback beyond red-shirted union attendees while ensuring a thorough, deliberate search.
disagreements.side_b_position: Caution against an open, rushed search or costly firm reset, warning that top sitting superintendents require confidentiality and that genuine community engagement requires organized regional meetings.
side_b_arguments: Minnie Forte-Brown warned that top sitting leaders will not apply in a fully public search, cautioned teachers and staff against another leadership reset, noted DPS already has extensive stakeholder survey data, and called a one-hour May 4 hearing disingenuous unless regional sessions across North, South, and East Durham are properly organized.
Dr. Mike Lee favored developing a profile of Durham's needs for candidates to address rather than a rigid candidate profile, while Xavier Cason emphasized collaborative, deliberate outreach.
disagreements.resolution: No formal vote was taken; the board reached consensus to hold an initial listening session at 5:30 PM on May 4, task Minnie Forte-Brown, Bettina Umstead, and Xavier Cason with proposing a broader community hearing schedule, and solicit written proposals from search firms.

boe_dae_events.event_title: Superintendent Search Process: DAE Demands for Stakeholder Voice and Anti-Privatization Leadership
boe_dae_events.dae_position: DAE leaders and members (Bryan Proffitt, Lisa McCullough-Grimes, and John Davis) and community speakers urged an unhurried internal-and-external search with formal DAE, classified staff, teacher, student, and parent representation to hire an anti-privatization leader centered on equity.

member_positions.stance_summary: Proposed flipping the traditional candidate profile into a 'profile of Durham' built from listening sessions with teachers, principals, parents, students, and community stakeholders. Supported holding an initial listening session on May 4 while gathering written proposals from search firms.
member_positions.key_quote: Creating this profile of Durham... involves speaking with our teacher and our principals and our parents and our students, our administration and every stakeholder.

member_positions.stance_summary: Warned against a rushed one-hour listening session ('disingenuous') or forcing teachers through another disruptive leadership reset, stressing confidentiality for sitting superintendents. Invited large groups like DAE to submit one consensus paper and spokesperson while emphasizing that not every teacher is a DAE member.
member_positions.key_quote: If we're asking for public input, so we don't have repetition, I would ask for large groups like DAE, do a paper that says these are the things that we're looking at... everybody, every teacher is not a member of DAE.

member_positions.stance_summary: Urged moving quickly with a board self-assessment and rapid community input on strengths and weaknesses—including opening the May 4 listening session—without hiring an expensive consultant for assessment. Noted he was weighing employees' and residents' desire for stability against an open external search.
member_positions.key_quote: I think stability is an important part of this discussion. And I think I've been hearing both from our employees and from the community that they want us to take that into account.

member_positions.stance_summary: Emphasized listening meaningfully to stakeholders so staff and the community have buy-in on the next superintendent, while arguing the board could move expeditiously. Agreed to serve on the three-member subcommittee planning broader community hearing dates.
member_positions.key_quote: The superintendent is going to be leading all of these people and we want them to have some buy in. And so I hope that we can figure out how to do that in a meaningful way.

member_positions.stance_summary: Reported that large executive headhunter firms told him DPS's salary scale was too small for their interest, and voiced hesitation about relying solely on NCSBA. Favored requesting tailored written search-firm proposals and exploring outside evaluation models.
member_positions.key_quote: I promise this board I would look into sort of large headhunter executive search firms. And in the inquiries I put out, I found that we are not at the scale that is necessary to employ their services.

member_positions.stance_summary: Unequivocally insisted on conducting a wide, open external search rather than closing off outside leadership talent. Pointedly noted the large presence of DAE 'red shirts' in the audience and insisted the board must still seek broader input from parents, students, and non-DAE stakeholders.
member_positions.key_quote: I do notice a lot of red shirts and that's not disrespectful but do we have the full voice of the community in this body? I'm not sure we do and we've heard from you. We need to seek input from parents and students as well as other members.

member_positions.stance_summary: Proposed splitting up board members to go out to stakeholders in the community rather than requiring everyone to attend a single Thursday central-office meeting. Agreed to serve on the three-member subcommittee with Forte-Brown and Umstead to map out regional engagement.
member_positions.key_quote: If we really want to talk to our community and our stakeholders, we need to go to them.

boe_dae_events.event_title: FY 2017-18 Proposed Budget: DAE Anti-Cuts Appeal, Instructional Facilitators, and Teaching Positions
boe_dae_events.dae_position: DAE leader Bryan Proffitt (joined by Southwest PTA VP Megan) urged the Board to be courageous and ask the newly elected County Commission for more funding instead of cutting 24 teaching positions, instructional facilitators, assistant principals, and clerical months, pledging DAE would mobilize community support.

member_positions.stance_summary: Urged Chairman Lee to invite County Commissioners and county finance staff to the May 4 budget hearing so they could hear community concerns firsthand. Emphasized that even without layoffs, years of central-office and school-level cuts leave fewer adults in school buildings.
member_positions.key_quote: Because we're able to absorb people and not have to lay people off and not have to RIF people, we do have less adults in our building.

meetings.title: Durham Public Schools BOE - AdvanceED District Accreditation Presentation 04 26 2017
meetings.executive_summary: At the April 26, 2017 special called meeting (presided over by Dr. Mike Lee), the Durham Public Schools Board of Education received the exit presentation from AdvancED's External Review Team following its multi-day district accreditation visit. Team Chair Tom Jones of Kentucky commended DPS for an objective, honest self-assessment, equitable and challenging learning pockets, intentional teacher leadership professional development, and strong community support evidenced by the recent school bond passage, while noting challenges in teacher turnover, serving international/multilingual newcomers, and district communications. meetings.title: Durham Public Schools BOE Special Session 04 19 2017
meetings.executive_summary: At the April 19, 2017 special called session (presided over by Dr. Mike Lee), the Durham Public Schools Board of Education unanimously approved its single-item agenda and held an open forum on next steps following Superintendent Dr. Bert Lumm's announcement that he would retire on August 4, 2017. Board members expressed gratitude for Dr. Lumm's leadership and integrity in stabilizing the district, then debated differing philosophies for the search: Dr. Lee advocated building a community profile of Durham Public Schools for candidates to address; Minnie Forte-Brown warned against a disruptive reset and favored reviewing existing stakeholder surveys and internal candidates; Steve Unruhe called for an open search open to both internal and external applicants; Natalie Beyer argued that top sitting superintendents will not apply in an open search and urged a confidential process; and Matt Sears suggested looking beyond traditional education search firms for talent acquisition. The board closed without a formal vote on the search method, aiming to decide on a search direction and timeline at the April 27 regular meeting.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Moment of Silence, and Agenda Approval
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Dr. Mike Lee called the special session to order, noted Dr. Bert Lumm's planned August 4 retirement, led a moment of silence, and called for approval of the agenda, which passed unanimously.

agenda_items.title: Board Discussion on Superintendent Search Process and Timeline
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Board members thanked Dr. Lumm for nearly three years of steady leadership and debated the format and timeline for selecting his successor. Members discussed developing a profile of Durham Public Schools (Dr. Mike Lee), drawing on existing stakeholder surveys and avoiding upheaval while evaluating internal talent (Minnie Forte-Brown), holding an open search (Steve Unruhe) versus a confidential search to attract top sitting leaders (Natalie Beyer), and exploring broader talent-acquisition firms beyond traditional education search consultants (Matt Sears), with plans to revisit a vote on April 27.

votes.item_title: Approval of April 19, 2017 Special Session Agenda
votes.notes: Unanimous voice vote; mover and seconder not named in transcript.
votes.discussion_detail: Motion and second to approve the April 19, 2017 special session agenda passed unanimously by voice vote.

disagreements.meeting_title: Durham Public Schools BOE Special Session 04 19 2017
disagreements.issue: Confidential vs. Open Superintendent Search and Role of External Search Firms
disagreements.summary: Board members expressed differing preferences on whether the superintendent search should be open or confidential, how heavily to weigh internal succession versus national recruitment, and whether to hire a search firm.
disagreements.side_a_position: Conduct an external/broader search—either open to internal and external applicants (Steve Unruhe) or confidential and proactive through talent-acquisition firms (Natalie Beyer, Matt Sears).
side_a_arguments: Steve Unruhe favored an open search allowing both strong internal candidates and external candidates to compete.
Natalie Beyer argued that the highest-caliber sitting superintendents will not risk applying in a public/open search, favoring a confidential process.
Matt Sears urged looking beyond traditional education search firms to proactive talent-acquisition processes.
disagreements.side_b_position: Prioritize continuity, existing community survey data, and evaluating internal succession without rushing into an expensive search-firm reset.
side_b_arguments: Minnie Forte-Brown argued DPS already has ample stakeholder survey data, warned that parents and staff do not want another system reset, and urged assessing whether current internal leadership can meet community standards before spending heavily on a search.
Dr. Mike Lee favored first building a profile of Durham Public Schools through community meetings before narrowing candidate criteria.
disagreements.resolution: No formal vote was taken; the board agreed to reconvene at the April 27 full board meeting to vote on a search direction, firm/process, and timeline.

meetings.executive_summary: At the April 3, 2017 Academic and Student Services Work Session (presided over by Bettina Umstead), the Durham Public Schools Board of Education heard an update on magnet seat acceptance and orientation processes (including 362 automatic lottery declines in the first round and 160 in the second), where board members raised equity concerns about mandatory portfolio and in-person barriers. The board also heard a letter from 45 Northern High staff on unpaid planning-period coverage due to the substitute shortage, reviewed the AdvancED interview schedule, unanimously approved pursuing the Destination Success Schools innovation-zone application, designated Minnie Forte-Brown and Steve Unruhe by consensus for the joint City-County pay equity task force, and unanimously approved the April 3 personnel report after closed session.

disagreements.meeting_title: Durham Public Schools BOE Academic & Student Services Work Session April 3, 2017 4:30 PM
disagreements.issue: Policy 4321 Warrant Review Scope (ICE Only vs. All Law Enforcement) and Interpretation Mandates
disagreements.summary: Board members, staff, and legal counsel debated whether revisions to Policy 4321 should require all law enforcement warrants (not solely ICE requests) to be cleared through the superintendent's office, whether to mandate ('shall') law enforcement interpretation services, and how to balance student protections with school safety.
disagreements.side_a_position: Broaden Policy 4321 Point 7 to require superintendent review and tracking of all law enforcement warrants on school grounds and strengthen interpretation language from 'should' to 'shall'.
side_a_arguments: Dr. Mike Lee urged sending all warrants to the superintendent's office for verification and tracking, and asked to convene a joint summit with the Sheriff, Police Chief, City Council, and County Commissioners.
Natalie Beyer argued for taking immediate action on Point 6 (student data privacy), Point 7 (warrant tracking/review), and changing 'should provide' interpretation to 'shall provide/allow'.
Xavier Cason and Minnie Forte-Brown questioned why DPS could not stand more firmly for students and noted public testimony showed arrests were still occurring in view of peers rather than privately.
disagreements.side_b_position: Consult local law enforcement first and maintain legal/safety boundaries before adopting an across-the-board superintendent warrant-clearance gate or binding law enforcement agencies via school policy.
side_b_arguments: Board attorney Ken Soo warned that instructing principals or staff to hold or judge criminal arrest warrants crosses legal lines, creates liability for school employees, and could conflict with officers responding to campus safety threats.

Superintendent Dr. Bert Lumm and Soo cautioned that DPS policy cannot legally compel outside law enforcement agencies to provide interpreters, and warned against putting uncertified DPS staff between officers and students.
Staff noted April 3 was a first reading and that face-to-face training for 4,500 employees could not happen overnight.
disagreements.resolution: Because it was a first reading, no vote was taken; the board directed administration to meet with local law enforcement leadership and return with modified Policy 4321 language (including strengthened arrest-privacy enforcement and SRO training) for second reading.

meetings.title: Durham Public Schools Board of Education Monthly Meeting March 23, 2017
meetings.executive_summary: At the March 23, 2017 monthly meeting (presided over by Dr. Mike Lee), the Durham Public Schools Board of Education honored student leaders, science fair winners, National Adaptive PE Teacher of the Year Laura Brickhouse, and Montessori Magnet recognition before hearing Superintendent Dr. Bert Lumm's update thanking staff for winter-storm mobilization and warning of a $6 million K-3 class-size funding threat alongside $10 million+ in projected cuts. During an emotional 19-speaker public comment period, educators, parents, and community groups called for opposing HB 13 cuts to arts/PE/music specialists, creating an ESL newcomer center, lowering EC caseloads, increasing teachers of color and anti-racism training, and paying substitutes faster. Dr. Lumm also presented data on his four board goals (teacher retention, boys/young men of color outcomes, Pre-K expansion, and district communications), with board members requesting narrative action plans and a concrete plan for three additional Pre-K sites prior to approving the March 23 personnel report after closed session.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Moment of Silence, and Celebrations
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Dr. Mike Lee opened the meeting with a moment of silence, and Xavier Cason led parent-dinner recognitions. Student speaker Jayden urged greater diversity in AIG and achievement-gap transparency, followed by recognitions of middle school speech winners, Central Regional Science Fair winners, 2017 SHAPE America National Adaptive PE Teacher of the Year Laura Brickhouse, Montessori Magnet recognition, and mathematics specialists.

agenda_items.title: Superintendent's Update and Agenda Review
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Dr. Bert Lumm thanked central services employees for mobilizing during a major storm event, warned that failure by the state Senate to rescind the K-3 class-size mandate would create a $6 million shortfall threatening elementary arts, PE, and music alongside $10 million+ in planned cuts and a $4.98 million county ask, and asked to add a separate $1.5 million Whitted School Pre-K funding request. The board unanimously approved the amended agenda.

agenda_items.title: General Public Comment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Nineteen speakers limited to two minutes each addressed district priorities: PAAC/PAC and Rhonda Taylor Bullock urged equity budgeting, anti-racism training, and recruiting teachers of color; Jordan and Riverside ESL teachers (Marcie Pacino, Kai Caruso) and interpreter Mercedes McCarley requested a high school ESL newcomer center and bilingual front-office staff; Eno Valley teacher Lashonda Cook, fourth-grader Navia, and teachers Nicholas Graber-Grace, Jonathan Matheson, and Troy Cole urged protecting elementary specials from HB 13; Ken Bracken-Brant sought smaller EC caseloads; and Tom Bado and substitute Robin McGee urged fixing the substitute shortage and 3–4 week pay lag.

agenda_items.title: Approval of February 23, 2017 Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Board members thanked the community for the outpouring of support during public comment and unanimously approved the February 23, 2017 regular meeting minutes.

agenda_items.title: Whitted School Standalone Pre-K Center Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Suzanne Cotterman and Karen Thompson presented operational plans for the Whitted School Pre-K center opening August 2017 with 8 classrooms (6 inclusive, 2 EC; 144 seats), raising DPS total Pre-K classrooms to 50. Using the universal application with Head Start and Durham Partnership for Children, Whitted will prioritize families in the C.C. Spaulding, W.G. Pearson, Eastway, Y.E. Smith, Fayetteville Street, and Lakewood zones, run 8:30 AM–3:30 PM with sliding-scale extended care, and co-locate with a senior living center.

agenda_items.title: Authorization of Separate $1.5M County Appropriation Request for Whitted School
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Dr. Lumm proposed authorizing a formal letter to the county manager and Board of County Commissioners requesting a separate, continuing $1.5 million appropriation for Whitted School so staff could begin hiring teachers immediately. Following confirmation from legal counsel that an earmarked pre-K appropriation avoids the 18% charter-school pass-through (with Steve Unruhe and Natalie Beyer urging broader charter/pre-K budget clarity), the motion passed unanimously.

agenda_items.title: Operational Services Consent/Action: LED Light Fixture Purchase
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff presented an expedited bid contract with Durham-based Mayer Electric Supply for $385,781.72 to purchase LED light fixtures at a discount saving nearly $1.4 million and capturing Duke Energy rebates. The board unanimously approved the purchase.

agenda_items.title: Reports of the Superintendent: Progress on 2016-17 Board Goals
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Dr. Lumm presented metrics on his four September 2016 retreat goals: teacher turnover (20.43% in 2014-15; 19.19% in 2015-16; beginning-teacher spring retention 94.9% with 20 mentors), achievement/graduation/discipline rates for boys and young men of color (noting black male short-term suspensions dipped from 15.7 to 14.5 while long-term suspensions rose from 34 to 42), pre-K expansion via Whitted, and social media metrics (higher impressions but lower engagement). Board members requested end-of-year retention figures, narrative strategy plans rather than raw metrics alone, and a formal plan for three additional pre-K sites beyond Whitted.

agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board unanimously entered closed session for Item 10 agenda reasons, returned to open session at 02:37:49, unanimously approved the March 23, 2017 personnel report, and adjourned.

meetings.title: Durham Public Schools BOE Operational Services and Policy Work Session 03 09 2017
meetings.executive_summary: At the March 9, 2017 Operational Services and Policy Work Session (presided over by Xavier Cason in Matt Sears's absence), the Durham Public Schools Board of Education unanimously adjusted the agenda to hold an immediate closed session and elevate the FY 2017-18 budget update, approved the February 9 minutes, and unanimously approved annual E-Rate applications—including a three-year Time Warner Cable WAN contract ($534,540/year) for gigabit connections at all schools while awaiting updated local/long-distance data. On the FY 2017-18 county funding request due March 15 under the joint MOU, CFO Aaron Beaulieu detailed a $12.9 million starting shortfall, a $4.4 million baseline request (of which $3.2 million would flow to charter schools), and $8.5 million in cuts alongside two major unbudgeted risks: $6 million for state K-3 class-size reductions and $2.3 million to match the city/county $15/hour living wage. Board members debated whether to send only the conservative $4.4 million request (favored initially by Steve Unruhe, whose $4.4 million-only motion was withdrawn without a second) or include the K-3 and living-wage contingencies (urged by Natalie Beyer and Bettina Umstead); the four members still present ultimately voted unanimously for a two-part, four-line-item request pairing $5.15 million ($3.65M base plus $1.5M for Whitted School) with $8.3 million ($6M K-3 plus $2.3M $15/hour wage increase). The board also unanimously approved spring surplus equipment disposal and received an informational LED lighting bid preview.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Moment of Silence, Agenda Amendments, and Early Closed Session
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Xavier Cason called the March 9, 2017 Operational Services and Policy Work Session to order and led a moment of silence. To accommodate a member departing early, the board unanimously amended the agenda to hold closed session immediately and move the budget update directly after E-Rate, then voted unanimously to enter closed session (returning to open session at 00:15:53).
agenda_items.vote_summary: Agenda Amendment and Closed Session Passed Unanimously

agenda_items.title: Approval of February 9, 2017 Minutes and Public Comment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board unanimously approved the February 9, 2017 work session minutes and heard general public comment from parent Catherine Wolf regarding school admissions and Plyler v. Doe.

agenda_items.title: E-Rate Category 1 and WAN Services Applications
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Technology staff and Network Manager Steven Brown presented the FY 2017-18 E-Rate Category 1 recommendations: Frontier for burglar/fire alarm lines, month-to-month continuations with Level 3 (PRI/long distance) and Verizon (cellular, facing 20% annual federal phase-outs), and a three-year Time Warner Cable WAN contract ($534,540/year) providing gigabit connections to all schools. On a motion by Dr. Mike Lee seconded by Steve Unruhe, the board unanimously approved the E-Rate applications while requesting updated Category 1 local/long-distance detail.

agenda_items.title: FY 2017-18 Budget Update and March 15 County Funding Request
agenda_items.discussion_summary: After public comment from Brian Callaway urging transparent, equitable treatment of blue-collar staff and zero-based budgeting, CFO Aaron Beaulieu presented a $12.9 million starting shortfall, an initial $4.4 million county ask ($3.2M flowing to charter schools, $450K to DPS, and $750K for Whitted), and $8.5 million in cuts—excluding $6 million in K-3 class-size exposure and $2.3 million for a $15/hour living wage. Board members debated how to frame the March 15 MOU request, with Steve Unruhe withdrawing a $4.4 million-only motion and Bettina Umstead withdrawing a three-part amendment before the four remaining board members unanimously approved a two-part, four-line-item request: $5.15 million ($3.65M base + $1.5M Whitted) and $8.3 million ($6M K-3 + $2.3M $15/hour wage).

agenda_items.title: Mid-Meeting Public Comment on Law Enforcement Collaboration
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Public speakers addressed collaboration between local law enforcement and ICE and urged that parents always be contacted before students are questioned at school.

agenda_items.title: Surplus Equipment Disposal and Preferred Brands / LED Lighting Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff presented an inventory of obsolete vehicles, cargo vans, and equipment for spring surplus disposal, which the board unanimously approved for immediate action. John Long then previewed preferred-brand updates and bulk bids for 15,000 LED light fixtures (with base and Alternate 2 options under budget at ~$607,000), deferring formal action until March 23.

agenda_items.title: Follow-Up Items and Adjournment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff reviewed follow-up items—including parent meetings for the Brogden / Second Chance Academy transition, a custodial program analysis scheduled for April, and the DAE policy request—and committed to returning requested phone-line and budget breakdowns before Xavier Cason adjourned the meeting.

disagreements.meeting_title: Durham Public Schools BOE Operational Services and Policy Work Session 03 09 2017
disagreements.issue: Framing and Size of March 15 FY 2017-18 Funding Request to Durham County
disagreements.summary: Board members disagreed on whether the preliminary March 15 MOU submission to Durham County Commissioners should be limited to the conservative $4.4 million baseline ask or formally include the $6 million K-3 class-size exposure and $2.3 million $15/hour living-wage request.
disagreements.side_a_position: Submit only the conservative $4.4 million baseline request (with an asterisk noting K-3 and living-wage uncertainties) to maintain trust with County Commissioners and avoid an alarming $13.4 million headline.
side_a_arguments: Submitting $4.4 million respects the collaborative budget MOU process with the county and avoids putting commissioners on the defensive before state numbers are finalized.

DPS had already invested heavily to reach an earlier living-wage benchmark and should compare total compensation and retirement vesting (5 years vs. 25 years) with the county before proposing $15/hour parity.
disagreements.side_b_position: Formally include the $6 million K-3 class-size mandate, $2.3 million $15/hour wage parity, and full $1.5 million Whitted School pre-K request alongside the base ask in clearly separated requests.
side_b_arguments: Omitting the $6 million K-3 risk and $2.3 million living wage would effectively end public advocacy with commissioners on urgent threats to 100 arts, music, and PE positions and staff pay equity.
Separating Whitted School's $1.5 million pre-K funding from the general appropriation is necessary to prevent 18% from flowing to K-12 charter schools.
disagreements.resolution: Steve Unruhe withdrew his unseconded $4.4M-only motion and Bettina Umstead withdrew her three-part amendment; the four remaining board members unanimously approved a two-part, four-line-item request combining $5.15M ($3.65M base + $1.5M Whitted) and $8.3M ($6M K-3 + $2.3M $15/hour wages).

boe_dae_events.event_title: FY 2017-18 County Budget Ask: $15/Hour Classified Living Wage ($2.3M) and K-3 Arts/Class-Size Request ($6M)
boe_dae_events.dae_position: Blue-collar worker advocate Brian Callaway urged transparent, equitable budgeting that does not disproportionately harm blue-collar staff or custodial workers, while the board debated whether to formally request $2.3 million to raise classified employees to a $15/hour living wage and $6 million to protect K-3 and arts/music/PE teachers.

member_positions.stance_summary: Pressed administration on matching the city and county's $15/hour living wage for classified employees ($2.3 million) and insisted the board must publicly ask the county for the $6 million needed to protect art, music, and PE teachers. Proposed separating Whitted's $1.5M pre-K request while including both the $6M K-3 ask and $2.3M for $15/hour staff pay, and seconded the final motion.
member_positions.key_quote: Depending on what colleagues think I'd be interested in an additional 2.3 ask for a $15 an hour for staff.

member_positions.stance_summary: Left the meeting prior to the final vote; during debate, questioned whether DPS was living beyond its means amid declining enrollment and $2.1 million in annual charter losses. Urged an aggressive marketing and retention strategy rather than treating student losses to charter schools as inevitable.
member_positions.key_quote: Since I've been on the board and I've only been here two and a half years, I've wondered, are we as a school district living outside of our means?

member_positions.stance_summary: Noted DPS had invested in an earlier living-wage benchmark and requested a side-by-side total compensation comparison with the county (citing 5-year vs. 25-year retirement vesting). Initially opposed sending an ask above $4.4M and moved a $4.4M-only motion to avoid an alarming $13.4M headline, but withdrew it without a second and voted Aye once the request was split into baseline and contingency parts.
member_positions.key_quote: I will vote against submitting a budget that is above the 4.4. I think that is not the message I want to send to the county commissioners at this point.

member_positions.stance_summary: Presided over the budget vote and supported putting both the $6 million K-3 class-size figure and the $2.3 million $15/hour living-wage request into the county ask early rather than waiting until summer. Insisted that all four funding requests remain distinct line items throughout the process.
member_positions.key_quote: Yes, I agree with putting both of those two in the ask. I think we need to go ahead and get in front of what could happen this summer.

member_positions.stance_summary: Rejected Unruhe's $4.4M-only motion as ending public conversation on cuts and staff pay, and moved the final two-part ask containing $5.15M in base/Whitted funding and $8.3M for K-3 and $15/hour parity. Framed the $2.3 million living-wage increase explicitly as an equity issue for Durham's community.
member_positions.key_quote: The 2.3 is really a, not only something that we want to do, but it's an equity issue for our Durham community.

boe_dae_events.event_title: DAE Working Group Follow-Up on Law Enforcement / ICE Campus Protocols
boe_dae_events.dae_position: DAE working group representative Allison Swain (joined by parent Nancy Cortes and student Ashley) thanked Dr. L'Homme and Dr. Pittman for meeting with them and urged strengthening DPS policy language across every school so warrant, data-privacy, and parent-notification rules apply to all law enforcement agencies including ICE collaborations.

meetings.title: Durham Public Schools BOE Academic & Student Services Work Session March 2, 2017 4:30 PM
meetings.executive_summary: The Durham Public Schools Board of Education held its Academic and Student Services Work Session on March 2, 2017, with six of the seven board members attending (one unnamed female board member was noted as absent). The board received informational updates on district-wide expansion of the NCStar school improvement planning tool for 2017-18, International Baccalaureate (IB) magnet programming and budget transparency, pre-K enrollment at the Whitted facility, and summer learning programs (where members questioned the adequacy of a $30,000 ESL Newcomer Academy budget). In formal action, the board voted unanimously (6-0) to name the Whitted early childhood center "The Whitted School," declare an easement surplus and approve its sale with a name change to Lenard, and add a Whitted School promotional update to the March full board meeting agenda. On the W.G. Pearson property sale to Student U, the board first voted unanimously to allow Bettina Umstead to recuse herself and then voted 5-0-1 (with Bettina Umstead abstaining/recusing) to approve the First Amendment extending the buyer's title examination period through March 17, 2017.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Moment of Silence, and Agenda Approval
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The presiding member opened the March 2, 2017 Academic and Student Services work session and led a moment of silence. At the chair's request, the board added an update on the sale of W.G. Pearson between items 5 and 6 and reordered items 1, 2, and 3 to proceed in the order 2, 3, then 1 before approving the amended agenda by voice vote.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Passed 6-0 (Unanimous of members present; 1 unnamed member absent)

agenda_items.title: Public Comment Check and Approval of February 2, 2017 Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: After confirming that no members of the public had signed up to speak, the board took up the minutes from its February 2, 2017 work session. Following a motion and second with no discussion, the minutes passed unanimously by voice vote.

agenda_items.title: School Improvement Planning Process and NCStar Implementation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Dr. Dietrich Danner presented the district's plan to train school improvement teams with NCDPI beginning July 2017 and expand use of the free NCStar real-time planning and monitoring platform from 30 DPS schools to all schools in 2017-18. Board members stressed ensuring non-employee parent participation on every School Improvement Team and displaying school goals visibly on school walls, while Steve Unruhe thanked Dr. Danner and Mr. Denton for their Zero-Based Budget Committee preparation.

agenda_items.title: International Baccalaureate (IB) Magnet Program Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff updated the board on the K-12 IB magnet continuum across schools including Hillside High and Burton Elementary, covering teacher training, vocational career pathway inclusion, and district-wide transportation versus walk zones. Questioning the Hillside profile, a board member noted that central Magnet Office expenses such as annual IB fees and two typical magnet positions (coordinator or language teacher) were excluded from individual school budget profiles and urged fuller cost transparency for the board and public.

agenda_items.title: Whitted Pre-K Early Childhood Update and Official Naming of The Whitted School
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following a middle segment omitted from the digest, staff reviewed pre-K applications through Durham's Partnership for Children (closing at the end of April), universal screening, and waiting-list coordination for the Whitted early childhood site. A board member then moved to officially name the facility "The Whitted School" to honor its history, which passed unanimously by voice vote, with members noting an absent female board member would be pleased.

agenda_items.title: Summer Learning Programs Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff summarized summer offerings including kindergarten literacy camps at six schools, state-funded Read to Achieve camps (grades 1-3), Extended School Year (ESY) for IEP students, the ESL Newcomer Academy (136 students on a $30,000 budget sharing Title I buses), senior Back on Track, and district-centralized Credit Recovery Camp. Board members questioned whether the $30,000 ESL Newcomer Academy budget was realistic and noted that expanding summer programming would require local funds rather than relying solely on federal grants.

agenda_items.title: Property Easement Surplus Declaration and Sale (Name Change to Lenard)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Addressing a time-sensitive easement request, a board member moved to declare the easement surplus and approve the sale, and amended the motion to incorporate the name change to Lenard. The amended motion passed unanimously by voice vote.

agenda_items.title: W.G. Pearson Sale Update and First Amendment to Purchase Agreement
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff reported that Student U and its real estate counsel requested an extension of the title examination period through March 17, 2017 while still targeting an early April closing. Bettina Umstead requested recusal; the board voted unanimously to permit her recusal and then voted unanimously among remaining members to approve the First Amendment to the Agreement for Purchase and Sale of Real Property.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Recusal passed; First Amendment passed 5-0-1 (Bettina Umstead abstained/recused)

agenda_items.discussion_summary: Board members voted unanimously to add an abbreviated promotional update on The Whitted School and its enrollment process to the March full board meeting agenda. Staff logged a follow-up request for additional information on the ESL Newcomer summer school before the meeting adjourned at 01:54:28.
