meetings.title: Durham Public Schools Board of Education Monthly Meeting February 23, 2017
meetings.executive_summary: Chair Dr. Mike Lee presided over the February 23, 2017 regular monthly meeting of the Durham Public Schools Board of Education, with all actions passing unanimously by voice vote (7-0). In his superintendent's update, Dr. L'Homme warned of a complicated FY 2017-18 budget cycle driven by state K-3 class-size uncertainty, declining fund balance, and charter school enrollment losses, while reaffirming district protections for transgender and immigrant students following federal Title IX guidance changes. The board unanimously approved the consent agenda adopting Policies 5230 (Outside Employment / Conflict of Interest) and 6100 (Disposition of School Property) on second reading, approved the CASA and State Employees' Credit Union (SECU) teacher housing partnership proposal near Lowe's Grove, and adopted new Policy 6306 introducing seat belts on school buses on second reading. Following a closed session, the board reconvened and unanimously approved (7-0) the February 23, 2017 personnel roster before adjourning.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Moment of Silence, and Celebrations
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Dr. Mike Lee convened the regular monthly meeting and led a moment of silence. Steve Unruhe then led monthly celebrations recognizing parents from Oak Grove Elementary, Lakewood Montessori Middle, Easley Elementary, and the School of Creative Studies (with dinner prepared by Northern High's Culinary Program) and honoring student achievements including Hillside High junior Kayla Beasley, NCHSAA 4A state shot put champion.

agenda_items.title: Superintendent's Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Superintendent Dr. L'Homme congratulated principals Dr. Jackie Tobias and Dr. Michael Fueger on completing their doctorates and Lowe's Grove principal Dr. Mitchell on NCMLE recognition. He outlined FY 2017-18 budget challenges—uncertain General Assembly relief on K-3 class sizes threatening elementary specials, a declining fund balance, proposed state teacher raises, and a second year of enrollment decline tied to charter expansion—and affirmed equal respect and protection for transgender and immigrant students.

agenda_items.title: Agenda Review and Approval
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Dr. Mike Lee called for any additions or corrections to the February 23, 2017 meeting agenda. Following a motion and second with no discussion, the board approved the agenda unanimously by voice vote.

agenda_items.title: General Public Comment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Minister Paul Scott addressed the board during general public comment regarding Black History inclusion in Durham Public Schools. No additional public speakers had signed up.

agenda_items.title: Approval of Board of Education Meeting Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board reviewed the Board of Education meeting minutes included in the meeting packet. With no corrections or discussion, the minutes passed unanimously by voice vote.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda: Second Reading of Policy 5230 and Policy 6100
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The consent agenda consisted of second readings for Policy 5230 (Outside Employment / Conflict of Interest) and Policy 6100 (Disposition of School Property). Upon a motion and second with no discussion, the consent agenda passed unanimously by voice vote.

agenda_items.title: CASA and State Employees' Credit Union Teacher Housing Proposal
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mr. Osteen presented the proposed teacher housing partnership with CASA and the State Employees' Credit Union (SECU), starting with a 24-unit apartment building (with potential to expand to three buildings / 72 units) on DPS land near Lowe's Grove and Southpoint valued around $200,000 per acre, alongside potential city participation. Board members enthusiastically endorsed the recruitment and retention initiative, suggested amenities and future North Durham sites, and approved the proposal unanimously.

agenda_items.title: Policy 6306: Introduction of Seat Belts on School Buses (Second Reading)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff presented new Policy 6306 introducing seat belts on school buses for second-reading adoption, following a middle segment omitted from the digest. Board members expressed excitement about advancing school bus safety in North Carolina and approved Policy 6306 unanimously while welcoming visiting Duke University public policy students.

agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board voted unanimously to enter closed session for the reason stated on the agenda. Reconvening in open session at 01:31:04, the board unanimously approved the February 23, 2017 personnel roster before adjourning at 01:31:41.

meetings.title: Durham Public Schools BOE Operational Services and Policy Work Session 02/09/2017
meetings.executive_summary: The Durham Public Schools Board of Education convened its Operational Services and Policy Work Session on February 9, 2017, with all seven votes recorded passing unanimously (7-0). The board unanimously voted to advance the CASA/SECU teacher housing land-investment proposal (24 initial units near Lowe's Grove) to the February 23 meeting, approve a joint Memorandum of Understanding with the Durham Board of County Commissioners, adopt FY 2016-17 Budget Amendment #1 adding $1,468,949 (including $702,000 in state fines/forfeitures technology funds and ~$1.1 million in bonuses), renew the five-year independent audit contract with Rives & Associates, and place Policy 6100 (Disposition of School Property) on the February consent agenda. Small specialty high school calendars were also moved and seconded before a middle segment omitted from the digest. During the second half of the meeting, resident Alex Modesto urged early budget transparency and protection of classrooms ahead of a projected $8.8 million gap, and Durham Association of Educators (DAE) representatives presented student due-process recommendations requiring board-attorney warrant review and multilingual parent notice, which the board referred to staff and legal counsel for policy review.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Agenda Approval, and January 12, 2017 Minutes Approval
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The meeting was called to order and began with a moment of silence. The board unanimously approved the agenda (moved by Xavier Cason, seconded by Natalie Beyer) and the January 12, 2017 Operational Services and Policy work session minutes (moved by Steve Unruhe, seconded by Natalie Beyer).

agenda_items.title: General Public Comment and CASA/SECU Teacher Housing Proposal
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Resident Gordon Galloway of Chancellor's Ridge spoke during general public comment alongside neighbors. Staff then presented the State Employees' Credit Union (SECU) and CASA teacher housing proposal to build an initial 24-unit building (expandable to two or three buildings) on roughly two acres near Lowe's Grove valued at ~$200,000 per acre under a 40-year agreement; Dr. Mike Lee moved and Bettina Umstead seconded bringing the proposal to the February 23 meeting for approval, passing unanimously.

agenda_items.title: Memorandum of Understanding with Durham Board of County Commissioners
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Steve Unruhe and Xavier Cason presented the joint Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) between the Board of Education and the Durham Board of County Commissioners affirming shared support for Durham students. Steve Unruhe moved and Xavier Cason seconded approval of the MOU, which passed unanimously ahead of the County Commissioners' scheduled action.

agenda_items.title: FY 2016-2017 Budget Amendment #1
agenda_items.discussion_summary: CFO Aaron Beaulieu presented FY 2016-17 Budget Amendment #1 reconciling accounts through January 31, 2017 and increasing the total budget from $407,655,153 to $409,124,103 (+$1,468,949), driven primarily by $702,000 in state fines and forfeitures restricted to technology and roughly $1.1 million in state merit and teacher bonuses. Steve Unruhe moved and Bettina Umstead seconded approval, which passed unanimously.

agenda_items.title: Independent Audit Contract Renewal (Rives & Associates)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Aaron Beaulieu recommended a five-year audit contract renewal with Rives & Associates following a four-year term, noting annual Local Government Commission opt-out flexibility and total fee increases under $2,000 over five years. Dr. Mike Lee moved and Natalie Beyer seconded approval, passing unanimously.

agenda_items.title: Small Specialty High School Calendars
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Kendra O'Neill presented 181-day (1,025-hour) 2017-18 calendars for four small specialty high schools aligned with NCCU (Josephine Dobbs Clement Early College) and Durham Tech (City of Medicine Academy, Hillside New Tech, and Middle College High School). A motion to approve was made and seconded by Xavier Cason at 00:31:21 during inclement-weather calendar questions; the final vote call fell inside a middle section omitted from the digest.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Moved and seconded (final vote omitted in truncated digest)

agenda_items.title: Policy 6100 (Disposition of School Property) – First Reading
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following a middle gap omitted from the digest, staff presented first-reading updates to Policy 6100 cross-referencing Policy 5230 to bar officials managing surplus property sales from purchasing items or arranging non-public deals. Natalie Beyer moved and Xavier Cason seconded placing Policy 6100 on the February 23 consent agenda for second reading, passing unanimously after brief clarification.

agenda_items.title: Mid-Meeting Public Comment: FY 2017-2018 Budget Priorities and Transparency
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Durham resident Alex Modesto urged the board to protect classrooms and student-facing services when closing a projected $8.8 million budget gap, contending DPS spends $15 million more on centralized operations than peer districts. He also urged releasing detailed budget proposals promptly so the public has adequate time to review them prior to the March county submission.

agenda_items.title: Durham Association of Educators (DAE) Findings on Student Due Process Rights
agenda_items.discussion_summary: DAE presenters, including Riverside High teacher Ellen Holmes, proposed requiring law enforcement to present a valid warrant for board-attorney review before obtaining student data or surveilling, interviewing, detaining, or arresting students, plus multilingual parent notification. Board members strongly affirmed protecting student privacy and safety under FERPA and directed administration and legal counsel to examine existing policies, distinguish local SRO contracts from federal/ICE jurisdiction limits, and return with recommendations.

agenda_items.title: Follow-Up Items: Redistricting Survey, Second Chance Academy, and Custodial Study
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff reported receiving about 78 responses on the new redistricting/student assignment public survey, holding a staff meeting regarding the Second Chance Academy relocation to Brogden Middle (with a parent meeting pending), and preparing a comparative in-house versus contracted custodial services analysis by April before adjourning at 01:45:44.

meetings.title: Durham Public Schools BOE Academic & Student Services Work Session 02/02/2017 Eno Valley
meetings.executive_summary: Vice Chair Natalie Beyer presided over the February 2, 2017 Academic and Student Services Work Session held on the road at Eno Valley Elementary School, where all formal votes passed unanimously without dissent. After welcoming Eno Valley Principal Rodney Berry, students, and PTA leaders and hearing public comment from a Creekside Elementary parent, the board unanimously approved (7-0) an amended agenda (reordering two reports so one board member could attend a meeting at Riverside) and the prior work session's minutes. Staff and Burton Elementary administrators presented a mid-year update on the 12-school Capturing Kids' Hearts initiative, sharing i-Ready academic gains, discipline dashboards, and emotional testimony on student support following neighborhood violence. At the end of the session, the board unanimously adopted two resolutions: one urging the North Carolina General Assembly to repeal the 2016 K-3 class-size funding ratio mandate to prevent cuts to elementary art, music, and PE positions, and a second resolution supporting the cross-sector Advancing Health in Durham initiative ahead of a June 9 Health Summit.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Moment of Silence, and Agenda Approval
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Vice Chair Natalie Beyer opened the work session at Eno Valley Elementary School and led a moment of silence. One board member requested moving reports 2 (Capturing Kids' Hearts) and 4 (Update on Disengaged Students) to the top of the reports so they could hear both before leaving early for a meeting at Riverside; the amended agenda passed unanimously.

agenda_items.title: Eno Valley Elementary Welcome and Public Comment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Principal Rodney Berry, students Rodney Williams (Men of Honor) and Layla (Young Ladies of Excellence), and PTA co-president Aralea Lawat welcomed the board, while board members praised holding community work sessions in North Durham schools. A Creekside Elementary parent also addressed the board at 00:19:08 expressing hope to remain part of the Creekside community.

agenda_items.title: Approval of January Work Session Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board took up the minutes from the prior January work session (transcribed by ASR as January 15 for the January 5 session). Following a motion and second with no discussion, the minutes passed unanimously by voice vote.

agenda_items.title: Capturing Kids' Hearts Mid-Year Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Ms. Thomas and Elizabeth Shearer presented a mid-year update on Capturing Kids' Hearts leadership training and intensive coaching across 12 DPS schools, highlighting 360-degree dashboards tracking i-Ready growth, attendance, suspensions, and discipline. Burton Elementary Principal Boykin and Assistant Principal Jita shared how Capturing Kids' Hearts relational practices helped students and staff support a second grader after a fatal shooting near the bus stop; a subsequent segment (00:48:47 to 01:37:10) was omitted in the digest.

agenda_items.title: Resolution on K-3 Class Size Ratios
agenda_items.discussion_summary: A board member read into the record a resolution calling on the General Assembly to pass legislation early in the 2017 session repealing G.S. 115C-301 (Section 8.3 of the 2016 budget bill) and restoring K-3 class-size funding flexibility. Members emphasized that unfunded class-size mandates would force drastic cuts to art, music, and PE teachers, require modular classrooms, and pressure local property taxes before March budget submission, urging full repeal rather than partial modification.

agenda_items.title: Resolution in Support of Advancing Health in Durham
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff presented a model resolution drafted with Dr. Tequila Green following cross-sector health convenings led by Duke Chancellor Dr. Eugene Washington ahead of a June 9 Health Summit, aligning DPS with Durham City and Durham County. After reading the resolution highlighting county health disparities, childhood wellness, nutrition, physical activity, joint-use agreements, and healthcare workforce training with Duke Health, the board adopted it unanimously.

agenda_items.title: Summary of Follow-Up Items and Adjournment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff confirmed a follow-up request for semesterly (adjusted from quarterly) benchmark data and qualitative teacher, student, and administrator survey aggregates for the 12 Capturing Kids' Hearts schools. Vice Chair Beyer thanked attendees and adjourned the meeting at 01:49:52.

meetings.title: Durham Public Schools Board of Education Monthly Meeting January 26, 2017
meetings.executive_summary: Chair Dr. Mike Lee presided over the January 26, 2017 regular monthly meeting of the Durham Public Schools Board of Education. After celebrations and Dr. L'Homme's superintendent update addressing inequitable state performance bonuses and a new public survey on redistricting guiding principles, the board unanimously approved (7-0) an amended agenda, meeting minutes, and supporting administration's relocation of Second Chance Academy to Brogden Middle School. The board also reviewed data showing 21.4% unfilled elementary substitute absences (averaging 724 AESOP calls per day) and debated potential solutions including compensating teachers who cover classes during planning periods and recruiting retirees, and deferred formal adoption of a K-3 class-size resolution to the February 2 work session while Steve Unruhe and a colleague finalized language. Following a closed session, the board approved the January 26, 2017 personnel report by a 6-0-1 vote, with Minnie Forte-Brown recusing herself and abstaining because her husband's name appeared on the employment list.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Moment of Silence, and Celebrations
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Dr. Mike Lee opened the first monthly meeting of 2017 and led a moment of silence. Matt Sears led celebrations thanking Forest View Elementary and Morehead Montessori parents (dinner provided by Northern High Culinary Department) and honoring students including 11th grader Tamir, Riverside vocalist Noah Mofield (ACDA National Honors Chorus), State Fair student artists, and Durham School of the Arts for placing fourth at the State Fair.

agenda_items.title: Superintendent's Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Dr. L'Homme thanked the DSA string quartet and appreciated the board concentrating non-teaching state performance bonuses on the lowest-paid employees, while criticizing the state's restriction of teacher bonuses to 3rd grade, AP/IB, and CTE teachers as inequitable to pre-K through 2nd grade, specialist, counselor, and EC educators. He also announced an online public survey on redistricting guiding principles and congratulated Park Scholarship finalists from DSA, Jordan, and Riverside.

agenda_items.title: Agenda Review and Approval
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board unanimously approved swapping items 9.2 A and B so the substitute teacher item would be heard last. After clarifying with the board attorney that the draft K-3 class-size resolution fell within the K-3 teacher allotment formula report item, the board unanimously approved the full agenda.

agenda_items.discussion_summary: An elementary arts teacher addressed the board warning that the state's K-3 class-size legislation threatens art, music, and physical education positions and thanking the board for its support. The board then unanimously approved the Board of Education minutes by voice vote.

agenda_items.title: Tharrington Smith Legal Services Contract Renewal
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff presented the legal services contract renewal with Tharrington Smith increasing the hourly rate by $5 effective February 1, 2017 and again in 2018 while keeping the flat fee unchanged. boe_dae_events.event_title: K-3 Class Size Mandate Impacts on Arts/PE Teachers and Draft Legislative Resolution
boe_dae_events.dae_position: Elementary art teacher Barbie Bailey Smith warned that the unfunded state K-3 class-size mandate requiring 102 additional teachers and classrooms threatens elementary art, music, and PE teaching positions and urged the Board to advocate for legislative relief.

member_positions.stance_summary: Highlighted the roughly $5 million local cost plus 102 furnished classrooms required to absorb the mandate without cutting specials. Declared to Raleigh lawmakers that Durham Public Schools would always preserve art, music, and physical education.
member_positions.key_quote: Despite what people in the legislature may think Durham is always going to have art music and physical education.

member_positions.stance_summary: Criticized the General Assembly for failing to fix the unfunded class-size mandate during its special short session and argued House Bill 13 remained insufficient to protect specials statewide. Volunteered to refine the draft resolution with Steve Unruhe for the February 2 work session.
member_positions.key_quote: What we need is a fix that is better than the current bill that they introduced yesterday, which if folks want to look at House Bill 13, it's not good enough yet.

member_positions.stance_summary: Proposed revising the draft resolution to strike 'in kindergarten through third grade' from the specials-cuts clause because losing art, music, and PE teachers affects entire elementary schools. Supported keeping language emphasizing the property tax burden on local governments.
member_positions.key_quote: If we cut those positions, it's going for the entire elementary school right so if we could just scratch the in kindergarten through third grade.

member_positions.stance_summary: Argued the resolution focused too narrowly on flexibility when the core problem was an unfunded state mandate forcing districts to eliminate other positions. Drafted a new 'whereas' clause explicitly tying the funding failure to cuts in art, music, and PE.
member_positions.key_quote: The issue is not the flexibility. The issue is there's no money for this.

member_positions.stance_summary: Assured attending arts teachers that the Board would sign and advocate behind the resolution and urged teachers, parents, and students to contact legislators statewide. Deferred final text approval to the February 2 work session after live editing proved too slow.
member_positions.key_quote: We're going to sign this resolution and we're committing to advocate, but we need our community to do the same thing.

boe_dae_events.event_title: State Performance Bonuses (3rd Grade, AP/IB, CTE) and Classified Merit Pay ($590)
boe_dae_events.dae_position: Educators and merit-pay critics (including teacher Stu Egan, cited in discussion) opposed divisive state test-based bonuses restricted to narrow grades/subjects and called for lasting, equitable compensation systems across all certified and classified staff.

member_positions.stance_summary: Speaking as a former AP Calculus teacher who would have been eligible, denounced the state performance bonus scheme as insulting and ridiculous for singling out individual teachers while ignoring colleagues who taught those students earlier. Apologized on his own behalf to DPS teachers for having to implement the program.
member_positions.key_quote: I apologize to our staff, our teachers, for having to implement this. It's really as crazy a program as I can remember.

boe_dae_events.event_title: Substitute Teacher Shortage, Teacher Leave, and Planning-Period Coverage Compensation
boe_dae_events.dae_position: Parent Don Moffitt and educator advocates highlighted severe substitute shortages (21.4% unfilled in elementary schools and 60-day pay delays) that force teachers and instructional assistants to cover classes and lose planning time, calling for better pay, staffing, and working-condition protections.

member_positions.stance_summary: Initially questioned the high volume of Monday and Friday teacher absences and asked what administration had communicated to teachers about attendance. Later acknowledged that teaching is hard and teachers need mental health days, noting that states with collective bargaining guarantee set personal time unlike North Carolina.
member_positions.key_quote: We know teachers need mental health days. We know that teaching is hard and we know that in states where they have collective bargaining teachers have set number of days.

member_positions.stance_summary: Pushed back firmly against blaming teachers for taking time off, noting teachers sacrifice weekends for Friday conferences and professional development. Framed unfilled substitute absences as a major working-conditions driver of teacher turnover and proposed compensating regular teachers when asked to cover classes during planning periods.
member_positions.key_quote: I know for a fact that one of the pieces of the working conditions that affects teachers greatly is being asked to cover other classrooms... I would like to see us talking with teachers about methods to compensate them.

meetings.title: Durham Public Schools BOE Operational Services and Policy Work Session January 12, 2017 4:30 PM
meetings.executive_summary: The Durham Public Schools Board of Education held its Operational Services and Policy Work Session on January 12, 2017, unanimously voting (7-0) to move the substitute teacher update to the January 26 board meeting agenda and approve the December 8, 2016 work session minutes. Staff briefed the board on the district's redistricting and student assignment study (targeting 2018-19 implementation using an 85% building utilization benchmark and county growth data), while parents and community speakers raised concerns regarding low-income minority area transparency in redistricting, the proposed relocation of Second Chance Academy to Brogden Middle School alongside W.G. Pearson's transfer to Student U, and custodial outsourcing. In the FY 2017-18 preliminary budget discussion—facing roughly $8.2 million to $12 million in projected shortfalls, charter enrollment losses, and an exhausted fund balance—Xavier Cason and Natalie Beyer disagreed over community engagement timing: Cason urged immediate north-south-central board listening sessions so principals are not left defending cuts alone, while Beyer argued that holding public meetings before identifying concrete reduction options would be premature and counterproductive, resulting in an informal agreement to engage the public once realistic cut proposals are formulated.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Agenda Adjustment, and Approval of December 8, 2016 Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The work session was called to order at 4:40 p.m. with a moment of silence. The board unanimously voted (7-0) to move Item 6D (substitute teachers update) to the January 26 board meeting agenda for information and approved the December 8, 2016 Operational Services work session minutes (7-0).

agenda_items.title: Redistricting and Student Assignment Study Update and Public Comment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: After a public speaker urged transparent mapping of low-income minority target areas during redistricting, Mr. Miller presented historical and current capacity data—noting 20 schools using 80 mobile classrooms while seven schools sit more than 25% under capacity—and confirmed redistricting changes would take effect in 2018-19 rather than 2017-18 using an 85% utilization benchmark and county growth projections. Board members agreed to revisit and update the board's guiding principles with community input and clear metrics.

agenda_items.title: Public Comment on Second Chance Academy Relocation to Brogden Middle School
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Brogden parent Justin Rawlings questioned the safety and academic impact of relocating Second Chance Academy to Brogden Middle School (at 62% capacity) and requested SCA effectiveness data and alternative capacity options. A second speaker criticized the lack of parent and staff consultation, questioned why SCA was not placed at Lakeview, and raised concerns over vacating W.G. Pearson for Student U (noting a board member's employment there and $4 million in county funds).

agenda_items.title: Public Comment on Custodial Services Contract and Redistricting
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Small business owner and E.K. Powe parent Alyssa Cherry, representing a local waste-reduction coalition, opposed renewing the Service Solutions custodial contract and urged returning to in-house custodial staff or opening the contract to transparent competitive bidding. E.K. Powe parent Natalie Spring also began commenting on redistricting prior to a middle segment omitted from the digest.

agenda_items.title: FY 2017-2018 Budget Outlook and Community Engagement Strategy
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following an omitted middle segment, staff reviewed a contracting enrollment outlook, roughly $8.2 million to $12 million in projected budget gaps (versus the county's initial $2.2 million placeholder), pre-K funding requests, and an upcoming Zero-Based Budget Committee review of the $142 million local budget. Xavier Cason urged early north-south-central board-led listening meetings before cuts reach 53 schools, while Natalie Beyer contended that public meetings should wait until realistic $8.2 million reduction proposals are identified.

agenda_items.title: Follow-Up Items and Adjournment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff clarified that the feedback cycle for staff speakers follows the same tracking process as public speakers and committed to reviewing the meeting recording for any remaining follow-up requests. The meeting adjourned at 6:50 p.m. (02:13:16).

disagreements.meeting_title: Durham Public Schools BOE Operational Services and Policy Work Session January 12, 2017 4:30 PM
disagreements.issue: Timing of Community Engagement Meetings for FY 2017-2018 Budget Cuts
disagreements.summary: Board members disagreed over whether to launch north-south-central community listening meetings immediately to explain the looming $8.2M-$12M budget shortfall or wait until staff identifies concrete reduction options.
disagreements.side_a_position: Hold north-south-central board-led community listening meetings early in the budget cycle rather than leaving principals to explain cuts alone.
side_a_arguments: Xavier Cason warned that lack of community engagement at the board level threatens district visioning and places 53 school principals on the defensive explaining complex district-level budget formulas they do not control.
Minnie Forte-Brown added that educating the community early about charter school budget impacts and potential state legislation helps build public allies.
disagreements.side_b_position: Defer community budget meetings until staff identifies realistic reduction options from the $8.2 million gap so the board presents concrete proposals.
side_b_arguments: Natalie Beyer noted the district had spent down its fund balance leaving no reserve cushion and argued that going out to the community before identifying realistic $8.2 million in cuts 'just says yikes' without moving the process forward or helping relations with County Commissioners.
disagreements.resolution: No formal vote; by informal consensus at 02:12:06, Xavier Cason agreed to wait to schedule the community meetings until the board and staff identify concrete reduction options.

meetings.title: Durham Public Schools BOE Academic & Student Services Work Session January 05, 2017 4:30 PM
meetings.executive_summary: The Durham Public Schools Board of Education held its Academic and Student Services Work Session on January 5, 2017, with all observed motions passing without split votes. Staff updated the board on outreach to reduce language and waitlist barriers in the magnet lottery, a Kenan Foundation and COSBOT restorative justice grant across five pilot schools (including Riverside High and Merrick-Moore Elementary), a beginning teacher mentoring program retaining 97% of year-round hires despite 30% lateral-entry staffing, and the five-year School Improvement Grant (SIG) distribution funding literacy, math, and science coaches at five high-need schools. After questioning contract timing relative to delayed state and local budgets, the board approved the annual expenditure for Case 21 paper-pencil benchmark assessments by voice vote and unanimously voted (7-0) to add brief magnet and SIG award presentations to the monthly full board meeting agenda.

agenda_items.title: Magnet Lottery Outreach and Reducing Family Access Barriers
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Board members and staff discussed reducing language and post-acceptance enrollment barriers for Spanish-speaking and diverse families in the online magnet lottery. Staff explained that magnet coordinators led by Donna Hudson are equipped with historical seat-availability data to advise parents during tours that first-choice selections are critical because second and third choices rarely clear waitlists.

agenda_items.title: Kenan Foundation and COSBOT Restorative Practices Grant Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Elizabeth Shearer, Dr. Kelvin Bullock, and Dr. Pittman updated the board on the Kenan Foundation restorative justice grant (partnering with COSBOT and the Conflict Resolution Center) aligned with Capturing Kids' Hearts and equity training across five pilot schools. Staff addressed board questions about selecting Riverside High and Merrick-Moore Elementary, noting both principals' prior restorative justice leadership and alignment with Merrick-Moore's SIG grant.

agenda_items.title: Beginning Teacher Support and Mentoring Program Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff reported that 30% of first-year teachers are lateral entry (with 12-15% in EC and 6% in CTE) and detailed weekly/bi-weekly mentor coaching, monthly Global Sessions, the Differentiated Educators Academy, a new National Board "Beginning to Board" PLC for third-year teachers, and a 97% year-to-date retention rate for year-round schools. Board members requested mid-year survey data ahead of the next budget cycle, and staff briefly noted weekend activity cancellations ahead of a 9 a.m. weather decision.

agenda_items.title: Case 21 Benchmark Assessment Expenditure Approval
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff requested renewal of the Case 21 paper-pencil benchmark assessment agreement paid from local academic funds, noting full-price costs after a first-year discount and explaining that SchoolNet lacked five standards-aligned questions per standard for internal creation. After discussing with legal counsel whether academic contracts could be approved conditionally in June or July pending state and county budgets, the board approved the Case 21 expenditure for the year by voice vote.

agenda_items.title: School Improvement Grant (SIG) Five-Year Distribution and Coaching Model
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff presented the amended five-year SIG funding rollout (12.5% of funds in Year 1, 2016-17, for planning and pre-implementation) serving one middle school and four elementary schools, citing state data that only 7% of effective teachers work in high-need schools. Each SIG school will employ a full-time literacy coach, math coach, and half-time science coach alongside extended pre-K through 8 summer learning opportunities.

agenda_items.title: Monthly Board Presentations on Magnet and SIG Awards and Follow-Up Items
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Board members unanimously voted (7-0) to add brief magnet and SIG award presentations to the monthly full board meeting to highlight academic work publicly. Staff recorded follow-up items to share magnet data with Mr. Hawks and the DSA community regarding entry barriers and to provide mid-year mentoring program survey data.

votes.notes: Passed by voice vote; transcript captures an apparent ASR artifact 'Aye.' after 'All opposed?' at 01:31:53 immediately before staff resumed explaining SchoolNet options, with no explicit nay count or roll call announced.
votes.discussion_detail: Approved the expenditure for Case 21 paper-pencil benchmark assessments for the 2016-17 school year upon legal counsel's advice to vote on the expenditure rather than an unprovided contract.

meetings.title: Durham Public Schools BOE Operational Services and Policy Work Session December 08, 2016 4:30 PM
meetings.executive_summary: At its December 8, 2016 Operational Services and Policy Work Session (presided over by Matt Sears), the Durham Public Schools Board of Education heard public comments from parent Shelley Morales regarding an insecticide spraying incident in her son's second-grade classroom and from Kevin Overcash of Piedmont Service Group regarding energy performance contracting. The board received and unanimously accepted the FY 2015–2016 Comprehensive Annual Financial Report audit, which noted no findings, reported that salaries, wages, and employee benefits accounted for 77% of total expenditures, and highlighted a $2.5 million single-year rise in payments to charter schools. Staff also presented an update on the transition from Blackboard Connect to SchoolMessenger—cutting annual notification costs from $121,782 to $51,150 while addressing SMS opt-in and PowerSchool data-entry gaps—and reviewed Phase I of the district's LED lighting retrofit across 37 school sites with $140,000 in estimated annual energy savings. All formal votes on the agenda, minutes, and audit acceptance passed unanimously with no split votes.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Moment of Silence, and Agenda Approval
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Matt Sears called the December 8, 2016 Operational Services and Policy Work Session to order and led a moment of silence. A board member moved and Natalie Beyer seconded approval of the agenda, which passed unanimously by voice vote.

agenda_items.title: Approval of November 10, 2016 Work Session Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board reviewed the November 10, 2016 Operational Services and Policy Work Session minutes. Bettina Umstead moved and Natalie Beyer seconded approval, passing unanimously by voice vote.

agenda_items.title: General Public Comment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Parent Shelley Morales described a Raid insecticide spraying incident in her son's second-grade class, requested a school transfer after withdrawing her children since December 1, and noted a newly scheduled administrative meeting with Lois Murphy. Kevin Overcash of Piedmont Service Group spoke on energy performance contracting and his firm's building automation control installations across six DPS schools.

agenda_items.title: 2016 Comprehensive Annual Financial Report (CAFR) Audit Presentation and Acceptance
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Auditor Mr. Boulier presented the 2016 audit with no findings, reporting that salaries and wages (58%) and employee benefits (19%) comprised roughly 77% of the district's total budget, leaving 23% for operations, technology, utilities, and maintenance. Board members discussed a $2.5 million one-year increase in charter school pass-through payments (from $16 million in 2015) and the child nutrition fund's $1.4 million net position driven increasingly by federal free-and-reduced lunch reimbursements; Steve Unruhe moved and Natalie Beyer seconded accepting the audit.

agenda_items.title: SchoolMessenger Communications and SMS Texting Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following postponement from November 10 at Matt Sears's request, staff updated the board on switching from Blackboard Connect ($121,782 in FY 2014–15) to SchoolMessenger ($51,150 annually). Discussion addressed why only roughly 6,103 valid SMS numbers were recorded across 34,526 parent records, PowerSchool field-entry training for data managers, opt-in mechanics (including text code 67587), principal usage guidelines, and multi-household messaging.

agenda_items.title: LED Lighting Retrofits and Energy Efficiency Phase I Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Maintenance staff and energy manager Brian Callaway presented 59 lighting and energy projects completed across 37 DPS sites at a net local capital cost of $416,000, leveraging $487,000 in Duke Energy incentives and yielding roughly $140,000 in annual avoided energy costs (a three-year simple payback). Highlights included eliminating noisy metal halide gym fixtures at Durham School of the Arts and Hillside, whole-school or wing LED retrofits with classroom dimmers at Glenn, C.C. Spaulding, E.K. Powe, and Merrick-Moore, and Phase II plans using $1.7 million in 2016 bond funds alongside potential performance contracts.

agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff noted that Scott Denton was coordinating with Research and Accountability on the bell-times survey, and board members requested clarity on the feedback cycle for employees who speak during public comment. The work session adjourned at 5:45 PM.

meetings.executive_summary: At its December 1, 2016 Academic and Student Services Work Session (presided over by Steve Unruhe), the Durham Public Schools Board of Education reviewed comprehensive updates on English as a Second Language (ESL) programming and high school academic and graduation data. Staff reported that 10,095 DPS students speak a language other than English at home across 83 languages—including over 4,700 identified English Learners and 1,174 recent-immigrant ELs—and highlighted urgent needs among over-age, pre-literate ninth-grade arrivals, mental health partnerships with Carolina Outreach and El Futuro, and translation contracts. In the high school data briefing with Karen Beckett and Beth Gifford of the Durham Children's Data Center, the board examined EOC, SAT, ACT, and AP trends, the predictive link between ninth-grade Math 1 timing, attendance, and suspensions and on-time graduation, wraparound support at Southern High School, and a newly signed seven-year National Student Clearinghouse agreement. All formal votes—covering the agenda, minutes, entering closed session, and the December 1 personnel report—passed unanimously with no split votes.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Moment of Silence, and Agenda Approval
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Steve Unruhe called the Academic and Student Services Work Session to order and led a moment of silence. Noting no members of the public had signed up to speak, the board unanimously approved the agenda by voice vote.

agenda_items.title: Approval of November 3, 2016 Work Session Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board reviewed and unanimously approved the minutes from the November 3, 2016 Academic and Student Services Work Session by voice vote.

agenda_items.title: English as a Second Language (ESL) Program Update

Discussion covered wraparound services for Southern High School and its Neal feeder pattern, ninth-grade Math 1 course timing, non-diploma EC pathways, and a newly executed seven-year National Student Clearinghouse data agreement; a minor SAT percentage typo was flagged for correction in the packet.

meetings.title: Durham Public Schools Board of Education Monthly Meeting November 17, 2016 6:30PM
meetings.executive_summary: At its November 17, 2016 regular monthly meeting (presided over by Dr. Mike Lee, with Minnie Forte-Brown excused to attend the NC School Boards Association conference in Greensboro), the Durham Public Schools Board of Education celebrated Northern High School's Be Our Guest culinary team, Student of the Month Elizabeth Wood, and Principal Gloria Woods-Weeks, and thanked voters for approving the $90 million school bond by the widest margin since 2003. During public comment, speakers urged multilingual and non-digital magnet lottery access, highlighted Playworks' Junior Coach Corps pilot, and criticized custodial contractor Service Solutions over recycling failures. In formal action, the board unanimously created the Office of Equity Affairs and appointed Dr. Daniel Kelvin Bullock as its first Executive Director on a two-year senior-staff contract, approved a House Bill 1030 merit-based bonus plan for non-educators earning $35,000 or less, and suspended Policy 6405.3 to permit an activity bus to transport 26 new refugee students and their families from Duke Manor to Forest View Elementary. All eight votes—including early and late closed sessions and the November 17 personnel report—passed unanimously 6-0 with no split votes.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Moment of Silence, and Celebrations
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Dr. Mike Lee called the meeting to order and led a moment of silence honoring Wake County school board member Zora Felton, Rep. Larry Hall's late wife, and public education following the November election. Celebrations recognized Northern High School culinary students for Be Our Guest, City of Medicine Academy Student of the Month Elizabeth Wood, and J.D. Clement Early College Principal Gloria Woods-Weeks as a regional Principal of the Year candidate.

agenda_items.title: Early Closed Session
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board unanimously entered a brief closed session prior to the superintendent's update and returned to open session at 00:25:49.

agenda_items.title: Superintendent's Update and Amended Agenda Approval
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Dr. Mike Lee noted Minnie Forte-Brown's excused absence for the NCSBA conference. Superintendent Dr. Bert L'Homme thanked voters for passing the $90 million bond, paid tribute to Rep. Paul Luebke and late DPS principal/coach Jim Armstrong, and added three items to the agenda—Dr. Daniel Kelvin Bullock's appointment, the Office of Equity Affairs announcement, and an activity bus waiver—which the board approved unanimously.

agenda_items.title: General Public Comment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Seven speakers addressed the board, including Silvio Baricaza and Pastor Ricardo urging paper, phone, and multilingual magnet lottery options for families lacking home internet, Playworks Executive Director Kristin Hathorn pitching the lower-cost Junior Coach Corps recess pilot for low-income elementary schools, and Crystal Dreisbach of Don't Waste Durham urging DPS to end its Service Solutions custodial contract over recycling breakdowns and bring custodians in-house.

agenda_items.title: Approval of October 27, 2016 Monthly Meeting Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board unanimously approved the minutes of the October 27, 2016 regular monthly meeting.

agenda_items.title: Launch of Office of Equity Affairs and Appointment of Dr. Daniel Kelvin Bullock
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Superintendent L'Homme announced the creation of the Office of Equity Affairs and recommended K–12 Social Studies Curriculum Specialist Dr. Daniel Kelvin Bullock for a two-year senior-staff contract as Executive Director reporting directly to the superintendent. Following unanimous board approval at 00:59:05, Dr. Bullock outlined plans for anti-bias and culturally relevant professional development and equity data tracking, noting DPS serves over 81% students of color and roughly 65% free-and-reduced-lunch students with a teaching workforce that is over 60% white.

agenda_items.title: Merit-Based Bonus Plan for Non-Educators (HB 1030)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following referral from the November 10 work session for greater public visibility, the board unanimously approved the House Bill 1030 merit-based bonus plan directing one-time bonuses to non-educator employees earning $35,000 or below.

agenda_items.title: Suspension of Policy 6405.3 for Forest View Elementary Refugee Families Activity Bus
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff requested using a school activity bus to transport 26 newly arrived refugee students from the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Rwanda, Somalia, and Afghanistan along with their families from Duke Manor to Forest View Elementary. Upon Board Attorney Ken Sue's advice that Policy 6405.3 requires a two-thirds vote to suspend the rule limiting activity buses to athletic teams and student groups, the board unanimously suspended the policy.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session (Calloway v. Board of Education) and November 17 Personnel Report
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board unanimously entered closed session at 01:18:37 to consult with the board attorney on confidential matters and the Calloway v. Board of Education litigation. Returning to open session at 01:57:58, the board unanimously approved the November 17, 2016 personnel roster and adjourned.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Closed session passed unanimously; Personnel report passed unanimously

meetings.title: Durham Public Schools BOE Operational Services and Policy Work Session November 10, 2016 4:30 PM
meetings.executive_summary: At its November 10, 2016 Operational Services and Policy Work Session—held remotely at W.G. Pearson Elementary School with School for Creative Studies student videographers and presided over by Xavier Cason (with Matt Sears absent while translating at Lakewood Elementary)—the board reviewed implementation of the district's new school bell schedule, noting smooth bus operations alongside reduced breakfast participation, closures of before-school care at 21 sites, and plans for a stakeholder survey. The board unanimously voted to allow Bettina Umstead, an employee of Student U, to recuse herself and then voted unanimously 5-0 to approve Student U's final $1,000,000 bid to purchase the old W.G. Pearson Central Services building after the county declined right of first refusal and no upset bids were filed. Members also reviewed the House Bill 1030 merit-based bonus plan for non-educators and unanimously amended the motion to refer it to the November 17 full board action agenda for greater public visibility, heard an extended i-Ready grades 3–8 academic diagnostic briefing, and held over Matt Sears's SchoolMessenger update until the December work session. No split votes occurred.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Moment of Silence, Remote Meeting Remarks, and Agenda Approval
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Xavier Cason called the remote work session at W.G. Pearson Elementary School to order and led a moment of silence. Dr. Mike Lee thanked staff and School for Creative Studies student videographers Jorge Rivera, Sean Woods, and John Cortez for piloting school-based board meetings, after which the board unanimously approved the agenda.

agenda_items.title: Approval of October 13, 2016 Work Session Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board unanimously approved the minutes from the October 13, 2016 Operational Services and Policy Work Session.

agenda_items.title: Bell Schedule Implementation Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Scott Denton reported that transportation rollout under the revised bell schedules went smoothly overall, though school breakfast participation declined, before-school care programs closed at 21 sites, elementary afternoon bus schedules conflicted with some after-school programs, and high school athletes missed late-afternoon class time. Board members welcomed plans by Denton and Dr. Spencer to conduct a survey of families, students, and staff while reiterating commitment to keeping the sleep-focused bell schedule in place for two years to measure achievement.

agenda_items.title: Recusal Permission and Final Bid Approval for Sale of Old W.G. Pearson Central Services Building
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following Board Attorney Ken Sue's opinion confirming Bettina Umstead had no personal financial benefit from the transaction, the board unanimously voted to permit Umstead—a Student U employee—to recuse herself. Staff then reported that Durham County Commissioners had declined their right of first refusal and no upset bids were received during the 10-day statutory notice period on Student U's $1,000,000 bid ($50,000 deposit, April 1 target closing), and the remaining five voting members unanimously approved the final sale bid.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Recusal passed unanimously; Final sale bid passed 5-0 (1 recused)

agenda_items.title: Merit-Based Bonus Plan for Non-Educators (HB 1030)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Finance and HR staff presented a plan to distribute House Bill 1030 state-funded merit bonuses (combined with local lapsed salaries and fund balance so non-state-paid employees receive equivalent bonuses) based on 2015–16 evaluations and continuous employment through October 1, 2016. After an initial motion to approve in committee, members agreed to amend the motion so the plan would go to the November 17 full board action agenda for broader public awareness while still meeting the December 1 state reporting deadline.

agenda_items.title: Public Comment Check and Middle School District Improvement Monitoring Measures (i-Ready Data)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Xavier Cason opened the mid-meeting public comment window at 5:12 PM with no speakers present. Dr. Stacy Wilson-Norman then presented fall grades 3–8 i-Ready math and reading diagnostics, showing 23% of math students and 27% of reading students on or above grade level in standard view alongside large 'emerging' cohorts one level behind, persistent geometry and informational-text weaknesses, severe seventh-grade math teacher turnover, and steep ELL proficiency gaps compared to national norms.

agenda_items.title: Postponement of SchoolMessenger Item, Follow-Up Items, and Adjournment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Xavier Cason noted Matt Sears was absent translating for Spanish-speaking parents at Lakewood Elementary and held over Sears's SchoolMessenger agenda item until the next Operational Services work session by consensus. Members reviewed follow-up items and upcoming remote work sessions at Northern High School (February) and Hillside High School before adjourning.

votes.notes: Unanimous voice vote among the six attending board members (Matt Sears absent translating at Lakewood Elementary).
votes.discussion_detail: Motion to approve the November 10, 2016 Operational Services and Policy Work Session agenda.

votes.notes: Unanimous voice vote (Matt Sears absent).
votes.discussion_detail: Motion to approve the minutes of the October 13, 2016 Operational Services and Policy Work Session.

meetings.title: Durham Public Schools Board of Education Quarterly Retreat November 9, 2016 8:30 AM
meetings.executive_summary: At its inaugural November 9, 2016 Quarterly Retreat (presided over by Chair Dr. Mike Lee with full board participation), the Durham Public Schools Board of Education reviewed 2015–16 teacher turnover data (19.15% districtwide, with over half of resignations among teachers with zero to nine years of experience), school-by-school academic and equity gaps, and Dr. Stacy Wilson-Norman's five-goal draft plan for raising achievement among African American and Latino boys. Staff also presented an operational and financial plan for opening eight new Pre-K classrooms (144 seats, expanding capacity by roughly 20% to 770 students) at the redeveloped Whitted School in August 2017 at an estimated $1.5 million operating cost split evenly between DPS and Durham County. Following the previous day's national and local elections, board members discussed working constructively with the Board of County Commissioners, establishing measurable progress indicators and short-cycle reviews for board goals, and clarifying the boundary between board governance and school-level operations. No formal votes were taken during the retreat.

agenda_items.title: Opening Remarks, Moment of Silence, and Quarterly Retreat Format
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Dr. Mike Lee opened the board's first quarterly retreat following Election Day, asking members to reflect during a moment of silence on working together across differences to move Durham Public Schools forward.

agenda_items.title: Teacher Turnover, Recruitment, and Retention Data Review
agenda_items.discussion_summary: HR staff presented 2015–16 resignation data showing a 19.15% overall turnover rate, with teachers leaving primarily for other North Carolina school districts and over 50% of departures occurring among educators with zero to nine years of experience. Members discussed beginning-teacher mentoring, principal quality and team culture as retention drivers, and upcoming January exit-interview tracking.

agenda_items.title: Equity Gap Analysis and Draft Plan for Boys of Color
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff reviewed poverty and achievement disparities—65% free-and-reduced lunch districtwide, one-third homelessness under McKinney-Vento at Eastway Elementary, and 47- to 51-point proficiency gaps for Black and Latino male students—alongside Dr. Stacy Wilson-Norman's five-goal draft plan for boys of color covering early learning, classroom mastery, disproportionality, system capacity, and college/career readiness. Board members debated moving urgently from study to visible action while scaling best practices from rapid-gain classrooms and addressing wraparound community needs.

agenda_items.title: Pre-K Expansion and Whitted School Facility Planning
agenda_items.discussion_summary: John Long and Dr. Stacy Wilson-Norman outlined plans to add 144 Pre-K seats across eight classrooms at the redeveloped Whitted School by August 2017—expanding DPS Pre-K capacity from 626 students across 21 sites to 770—with an estimated $1.5 million operating cost anticipated to be split $750,000 each with Durham County. Discussion covered bus loop sizing, EC self-contained classroom needs, extended childcare hours, potential NC Central University intern partnerships, and phasing enrollment.

agenda_items.title: Intergovernmental Collaboration, Measurable Board Goals, and Governance Role
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Board members discussed maintaining a professional, collaborative partnership with the Board of County Commissioners on budgets, setting concrete numerical indicators and regular review sprints to track board goals without pulling arbitrary targets, and balancing board member visibility in classrooms with proper governance boundaries. Members scheduled the next quarterly retreat for three months later at W.G. Pearson Elementary School and adjourned.

meetings.title: Durham Public Schools BOE Academic & Student Services Work Session November 03, 2016 4:30 PM
meetings.executive_summary: At its November 3, 2016 Academic and Student Services Work Session (presided over by Steve Unruhe), the Durham Public Schools Board of Education unanimously approved 2017–2018 traditional and year-round school calendars, moved its December monthly board meeting from December 22 to December 15, reviewed the 2015 Durham County Youth Risk Behavior Survey, and unanimously approved an updated disbursement agreement for the $5.8 million Whitted School redevelopment project to protect developer tax credits. The board experienced one split vote on a draft Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) with the Durham Board of County Commissioners: by a 5-2 hand vote, members approved Dr. Mike Lee's motion to table the MOU until January so the board could revise it alongside newly elected county commissioners, with Dr. Mike Lee, Natalie Beyer, Matt Sears, and Xavier Cason raising concerns about unbalanced obligations, vague funding exceptions, and joint site-selection language in Point 11, while Minnie Forte-Brown and Steve Unruhe argued for adopting the MOU immediately as a living document to get it behind them. The board also unanimously voted to postpone the middle school 6–8 academic data presentation to a subsequent meeting and entered closed session.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Moment of Silence, and Agenda Approval
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Steve Unruhe opened the work session with a moment of silence for Rep. Paul Luebke and Club Boulevard staff member Alicia Harris. The board unanimously amended the agenda to add moving the December board meeting date and the Whitted School disbursement agreement.

agenda_items.title: Approval of Amended October 6, 2016 Work Session Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following Natalie Beyer's correction clarifying that the AIG plan had been forwarded to the October action meeting rather than approved outright in work session, the board unanimously approved the minutes as amended.

agenda_items.title: 2017–2018 Traditional and Year-Round School Calendar Proposals
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Kendra O'Neill presented 2017–2018 traditional calendar drafts A and B and year-round drafts 1 and 2 constrained by North Carolina's calendar law, noting shorter winter breaks and inclement weather days. The board unanimously approved the recommended traditional calendar draft and year-round Draft 1 (beginning July 17).
agenda_items.vote_summary: Traditional calendar passed unanimously; Year-round Draft 1 passed unanimously

agenda_items.title: Rescheduling December 2016 Monthly Board Meeting
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Board members unanimously approved moving the December 2016 regular monthly board meeting from December 22 to December 15 to avoid conflicting with the start of winter break.

agenda_items.title: 2015 Durham County Youth Risk Behavior Survey (YRBS) Presentation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Durham County Department of Public Health staff presented 2015 YRBS findings covering mental health, sexual health, and weapons—including 24% of middle schoolers and 16% of high schoolers reporting carrying a weapon in the past 30 days overall, and 4% of high schoolers carrying a weapon at school. Board members requested disaggregated state comparisons, sexual orientation data, sex-education resource links, and a follow-up report in February or March on district interventions informed by the survey.

agenda_items.title: Amended and Restated Disbursement Agreement for Whitted School Redevelopment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff and board attorney Rob Malone presented technical updates to the Whitted School redevelopment disbursement agreement—updating dates, entities such as Whitted School Redevelopment LLC, and completed preconditions ahead of the developers' December 31 tax-credit deadline without altering DPS's $5.8 million commitment. The board unanimously approved the amended agreement.

agenda_items.title: Draft Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) with Durham Board of County Commissioners
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Superintendent L'Homme presented the revised draft BOCC–BOE MOU ahead of the commissioners' upcoming meeting. Matt Sears, Natalie Beyer, Dr. Mike Lee, and Xavier Cason objected that the draft lacked balanced county commitments on teacher pay (Point 9), allowed undefined 'financial crisis' opt-outs (Point 7), omitted 'draft budget' wording (Point 1), and infringed on DPS statutory authority over school site selection and architectural specs (Point 11), whereas Minnie Forte-Brown and Steve Unruhe urged adopting the living document immediately; Dr. Mike Lee's motion to table until January passed 5-2 by hand vote.

agenda_items.title: Postponement of Middle School DIMMs Report, Follow-Up Items, and Closed Session
agenda_items.discussion_summary: At 6:30 PM, the board unanimously voted to postpone the Middle School District Improvement Monitoring Measures (6–8 data) presentation to a subsequent meeting, reviewed YRBS follow-up items, and voted unanimously to enter closed session under NCGS 115C-402 and FERPA.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Postponement passed unanimously; Closed session passed unanimously

votes.notes: Unanimous voice vote; Minnie Forte-Brown had not yet arrived at the start of the meeting (per 00:26:57) and Bettina Umstead/Matt Sears presence at 00:03:43 is not explicitly named.
votes.discussion_detail: Motion to add the December board meeting date change after item 1 and the Whitted disbursement agreement after the Youth Risk Behavior Survey.

disagreements.meeting_title: Durham Public Schools BOE Academic & Student Services Work Session November 03, 2016 4:30 PM
disagreements.issue: Adoption vs. Tabling of Draft BOCC–BOE Memorandum of Understanding (MOU)
disagreements.summary: Board members split 5-2 on whether to adopt a negotiated draft Memorandum of Understanding with the Durham Board of County Commissioners immediately or table it until January to revise its terms with the newly elected commission.
disagreements.side_a_position: Table the draft MOU until January to revise unbalanced provisions and negotiate with the incoming Board of County Commissioners.
side_a_arguments: The draft imposes reporting duties on DPS while lacking concrete county commitments on competitive staff pay (Point 9) and includes an undefined 'financial crisis' loophole on per-pupil funding (Point 7).
Point 11's mandate for joint planning prior to purchasing school sites and finalizing architectural specifications encroaches on statutory school board authority.
Point 1 should specify submitting a 'draft' or 'preliminary' budget in March rather than a final budget, and waiting until January allows board-to-board negotiation after county commission elections.
disagreements.side_b_position: Adopt the draft MOU immediately as an imperfect but workable living document to avoid further intergovernmental friction.
side_b_arguments: The draft is a major improvement over the county's initial draft and represents a non-contractual commitment to collaborate early in the annual budget cycle.
Delaying risks prolonging political squabbles over wording instead of focusing on the upcoming budget; the MOU can always be amended later if needed.
disagreements.resolution: Dr. Mike Lee's motion to table the MOU until January passed 5-2 by raised-hand vote (roll call not read in transcript; Bettina Umstead's vote on the hand count was not verbally stated).

meetings.title: Durham Public Schools Board of Education Monthly Meeting October 27, 2016 6:30PM
meetings.executive_summary: At its October 27, 2016 regular monthly meeting (presided over by Dr. Mike Lee, welcoming newly appointed District 2 member Bettina Umstead to her first full board meeting), the Durham Public Schools Board of Education heard public comments from George Watts and Morehead Montessori families raising urgent concerns over racial achievement gaps, lack of a published strategic plan, and transparency around a proposed Pre-K sliding scale fee. The board unanimously approved its consent agenda, the 2016–2019 Academically and Intellectually Gifted (AIG) plan serving 5,761 students, and the 2017–2018 budget priorities and guiding principles, and held an informational discussion on the Pre-K sliding scale. On formal action, the board split 5-2 to approve amending Policy 3505 to allow sixth graders to participate in middle school athletics excluding football starting in spring 2017 (Ayes: Dr. Mike Lee, Matt Sears, Steve Unruhe, Minnie Forte-Brown, Bettina Umstead; Nays: Natalie Beyer, Xavier Cason, who objected to the mid-year timing and rushed rollout). Following closed session (after Minnie Forte-Brown's departure), the remaining six members unanimously approved 61 teacher appointments and one administrator appointment, then split 4-2 to approve contract extensions for ten senior staff members (voice vote without a named roll call).

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Moment of Silence, Celebrations, and Welcome of Bettina Umstead
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Dr. Mike Lee opened the meeting with a moment of silence encouraging civic participation during early voting. Celebrations honored Be Our Guest families, Northern High culinary students, J.D. Clement Early College Student of the Month Ivan Rosales, and Hillside IB Paralympic All-American Desmond Andre Jackson, and Lee welcomed newly appointed District 2 board member Bettina Umstead to her first full monthly meeting.

agenda_items.title: Superintendent's Update and Agenda Approval
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Superintendent Dr. Bert L'Homme congratulated high schools achieving 100% (Early College, City of Medicine Academy, Middle College), 98% (Hillside New Tech), and 90% (DSA) graduation rates, and affirmed students' right to free expression during the national anthem at athletic events. The board unanimously approved the agenda.

agenda_items.title: General Public Comment on Achievement Gaps, Equity, and Pre-K Sliding Scale
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Parents and community members—including Jovonia Lewis, Robin Furman, Jody White, Juana Rosales (through an interpreter), Rhonda Bullock, and Walt Barron—addressed persistent racial achievement gaps at George Watts Montessori (designated a Focus School) and across DPS, called for SMART goals and a strategic plan with equity funding, criticized PTA translation equipment rental barriers, and urged pausing the Pre-K sliding scale fee proposal until transparent community input and administrative cost analyses are shared.

agenda_items.title: Approval of Board Minutes and Consent Agenda
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board unanimously approved minutes from five September and October 2016 meetings, followed by unanimous approval of the consent agenda comprising the Policy 9000 facilities series and North Carolina School Boards Association policy updates.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Minutes passed unanimously; Consent agenda passed unanimously

agenda_items.title: Academically and Intellectually Gifted (AIG) Plan for 2016–2019
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Beth Cross and Laura Parrott presented the 44-page 2016–2019 AIG plan serving 5,761 identified students (~17% of enrollment compared to the state's 4% funding cap) plus over 400 additional enrichment students, adding a district review team, portfolio identification pathway, 96th-percentile stanine alignment, and high school AP lead teachers. Board members praised the program's diversity and unanimously approved the plan.

agenda_items.title: Middle School 6th-Grade Athletic Eligibility (Policy 3505 / HRSD-001)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following supportive public comment from coach Roger Reed and a briefing from Athletic Director Larry McDonald on the State Board of Education's August 4 rule change, Dr. Mike Lee moved to revise Policy 3505 to allow sixth graders to participate in middle school sports excluding football beginning January 18, 2017. Dr. Mike Lee, Matt Sears, and Steve Unruhe supported giving parents the choice and fostering school engagement, while Natalie Beyer and Xavier Cason opposed rushing implementation mid-year without broader parent input; the motion passed 5-2.

agenda_items.title: Pre-K Sliding Scale Proposal for Watts and Morehead Montessori Schools
agenda_items.discussion_summary: After public comments from Duke professor Anna Gassman-Pines and Watts/Morehead fee committee co-chair Tom Winger raising concerns about income-verification costs, non-payment penalties, and diversity impacts, staff presented the 200%-poverty-level sliding scale (free under $30,000 household income). Board members acknowledged communication breakdowns while noting that priority-zone gentrification and sibling preference already absorbed nearly all 58 Watts Pre-K seats and arguing local subsidies should help expand universal Pre-K access; the item was informational with no vote taken.

agenda_items.title: 2017–2018 Budget Priorities and Guiding Principles & FY 2016–17 Budget Calendar
agenda_items.discussion_summary: CFO Aaron Beaulieu presented revised 2017–2018 budget priorities and guiding principles incorporating board edits on social justice and equity, salary study comparisons, and energy efficiency, which the board unanimously approved. Staff also presented an informational update to the budget calendar specifying delivery of a draft budget to County Commissioners in March ahead of May final adoption.

disagreements.meeting_title: Durham Public Schools Board of Education Monthly Meeting October 27, 2016 6:30PM
disagreements.issue: Sixth-Grade Eligibility for Middle School Athletics (Policy 3505)
disagreements.summary: The board voted 5-2 to revise Policy 3505 so sixth graders may try out for middle school sports excluding football beginning in January 2017, over objections from two members regarding timing and academic transition readiness.
disagreements.side_a_position: Approve 6th-grade athletic eligibility (excluding football) effective January 18, 2017.
side_a_arguments: Parents, rather than the school board, should decide whether their sixth grader is mature enough to balance tryouts and academics.

Middle school coaches, athletic directors, and Durham Council PTA parents expressed support, and participation—especially in non-cut sports like track and cross country—fosters school belonging and academic motivation.
disagreements.side_b_position: Delay or reject mid-year implementation pending broader community engagement and focus on sixth-grade academic transition.
side_b_arguments: The State Board of Education pushed discretion to local districts hastily, and current sixth graders entered middle school expecting to wait until seventh grade.
Implementing the change mid-year in January leaves insufficient time for community feedback and parent readiness guidance.
disagreements.resolution: Motion passed 5-2.

meetings.title: Durham Public Schools BOE Operational Services and Policy Work Session October 13, 2016 4:30 PM
meetings.executive_summary: At its October 13, 2016 Operational Services and Policy Work Session (presided over by Matt Sears, with Minnie Forte-Brown on excused medical absence and Dr. Mike Lee arriving shortly after opening), Judge William Marsh III administered the oath of office to newly appointed District 2 board member Bettina Umstead. The board heard stark public comments from Riverside High School and Hope Valley Elementary teachers detailing severe custodial hour cuts and unpaid off-the-clock custodian labor, reviewed and unanimously advanced the $407.66 million FY 2016–17 budget resolution, revised 2017–18 budget priorities and calendar, an amended Zero-Base Budget Committee MOU drafted by Steve Unruhe, a $161,000 middle school gym bleacher contract for Githens and School for Creative Studies, and multiple 2000- and 9000-series policy updates. On Policy 5027/7275 (Weapons on Campus), the board split 5-1 to advance the updated policy (removing mace/pepper spray restrictions while retaining state-mandated concealed-carry vehicle exceptions) to the October consent agenda: Dr. Mike Lee moved and Xavier Cason seconded advancing it, while one unnamed board member explicitly requested to be recorded as voting Nay due to opposition to concealed carry on school grounds. Following closed session, the board unanimously approved the October 13 personnel roster.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Moment of Silence, and Agenda Modifications
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Matt Sears called the work session to order, noted Minnie Forte-Brown's excused medical absence and Dr. Mike Lee's imminent arrival, and led a moment of silence. The board unanimously added Item 6D (Zero-Base Budget Committee MOU), a post-meeting closed session, and moved Bettina Umstead's swearing-in ceremony to Item 4.

agenda_items.title: Swearing-In Ceremony for Bettina Umstead and Approval of September 8 Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Judge William Marsh III administered the oath of office to District 2 appointee Bettina Umstead alongside her family. The board then unanimously approved the September 8, 2016 work session minutes on a motion by Natalie Beyer seconded by Dr. Mike Lee.

agenda_items.title: General Public Comment on DSA Sibling Preference and Custodial Cuts
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Joe Gonzalez read a statement from the Durham School of the Arts PTSA supporting sibling preference. Riverside High School science teacher Micah Hunter Twidmeyer reported on behalf of the SIT, PTA, and boosters that cutting Riverside's custodial hours from 72 to 58—and dismissing a full-time custodian—left nine trailers, athletic bathrooms, and two classroom hallways uncleaned despite enrollment exceeding 1,840 students.

agenda_items.title: FY 2016–17 Budget Resolution ($407.66 Million)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: CFO Aaron Beaulieu presented the balanced $407,655,153 FY 2016–17 budget resolution ($141,859,083 local) based on 20th-day membership showing DPS enrollment down ~225 students to 33,275 while charter enrollment grew by over 500 to 6,411, warning that full budgeted spending would leave only $3.4 million in unassigned fund balance. Following questions on utilities, Child Nutrition, and charter school growth, Natalie Beyer moved and Xavier Cason seconded placing the resolution on the October consent agenda.

agenda_items.title: 2017–2018 Budget Priorities & Guiding Principles and Budget Calendar
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Board members debated edits to the 2017–2018 budget priorities—refining social justice and equity wording, salary study benchmarking toward $15/hour, extracurricular supplements, parental leave, and energy efficiency—and requested revising the FY 2016–17 budget calendar to label March 1 deliverables to County Commissioners as a 'draft' budget ahead of a May public hearing and final ratification. Both items were unanimously referred to the October full board action agenda.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Budget priorities passed unanimously; Budget calendar passed unanimously

agenda_items.title: Zero-Base Budget (ZBB) Committee Memorandum of Understanding
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Steve Unruhe presented a draft MOU clarifying that the Zero-Base Budget Committee is tasked with designing a long-term budgeting process rather than building the 2017–18 line-item budget. On Dr. Mike Lee's motion incorporating Natalie Beyer's edit to refer to 'principles of zero-based budgeting' and attach the guiding principles and date, the board unanimously adopted the MOU.

agenda_items.title: Mid-Meeting Public Comment on Custodial Conditions at Hope Valley Elementary
agenda_items.discussion_summary: A Hope Valley Elementary third-grade teacher testified that losing two custodial positions forced remaining custodians to work 16 to 20 unpaid off-the-clock hours weekly to keep the school sanitary without floor machines or regular classroom soap. Board members requested staff follow up on custodial conditions and clarify policy on responding to employee public comments.

agenda_items.title: Middle School Gym Bleacher Contract and Construction Policies 9115 & 9120
agenda_items.discussion_summary: John Long recommended a $161,000 combined bond-funded contract with Learning Environments to replace gym bleachers at Githens and School for Creative Studies over winter break; after initially voting to place it on consent, the board reconsidered and approved the bid immediately at 01:27:44. The board also unanimously advanced Policy 9115 (Pre-qualification of Bidders) and Policy 9120 (Bidding/MWBE, removing premature references to un-adopted Policy 9125) to the October consent agenda.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Bleacher contract approved immediately (unanimous); Policies 9115 & 9120 passed unanimously

agenda_items.title: Policy Series 2000 Revisions and Weapons on Campus Policy 5027/7275
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff and Board Attorney Ken Sue presented updates across the 2000 series, including choosing Option A on Policy 2500 (Hearing Panels) so non-unanimous panel decisions continue going to the full board, Policy 2610 (Board Attorney), and Leandro-mandated revisions across Policies 2120, 2123, 2300, 2341, and 2400 while skipping redundant Policies 2600 and 2650. On Policy 5027/7275 (Weapons on Campus), staff recommended deleting mace/pepper spray prohibitions and staff-escort language while retaining state-mandated concealed-carry handgun exceptions in locked vehicles; Dr. Mike Lee moved and Xavier Cason seconded advancing it to consent, passing 5-1 with one member voting Nay over the concealed-carry provision.

agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff summarized follow-up items including DSA sibling preference, custodial concerns, charter school 20th-day counts, and employee comment guidance.
